news.summaryZh: 2026年9月2日至3日，美国卫生与公众服务部民权办公室和国家标准与技术研究院联合主办了“保障健康信息：通过HIPAA安全构建信任2026”会议。会议明确了跨机构的人工智能主题：可信度继续作为联邦在医疗保健领域进行人工智能监督的组织原则。国家标准与技术研究院、食品药品监督管理局、卫生与公众服务部国家卫生信息技术协调员办公室以及民权办公室均表示关注可信人工智能，将其定位为连接整个健康数据生态系统中安全、保障和隐私义务的纽带。国家卫生信息技术协调员办公室的发言以治理为核心，呼应了卫生与公众服务部新发布的人工智能战略。国家标准与技术研究院的小组成员则预览了正在更新的《人工智能风险管理框架》，该框架仍以2020年《国家人工智能倡议法案》首次编纂的“可信度”概念为基础。会议还通过一场圆桌讨论更新了医疗保健行业的违规趋势和网络安全活动情况。黑客攻击是最大的违规风险，2026年迄今向民权办公室报告的大型违规中，绝大多数由黑客事件引起。此外，针对医疗保健实体的网络攻击勒索模式正在演变，从数据加密和勒索软件转向数据窃取或双重模式方案。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! On September 2-3, 2026, the Department of Health and Human Services (“HHS”) Office for Civil Rights (“OCR”) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (“NIST”) hosted the Safeguarding Health Information: Building Assurance Through HIPAA Security 2026 conference. Epstein Becker Green (“EBG”) was fortunate to attend and, below, shares takeaways in three key areas highlighted at the conference. A clear cross-agency AI theme emerged during the conference: Trustworthiness continues to serve as an organizing principle for federal AI oversight in health care. NIST, the Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”), the HHS Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology ONC (“ONC”), and OCR each signaled attention to trustworthy AI, positioning it as the connective tissue linking security, safety, and privacy obligations across the health data ecosystem. Two key themes stood out. First, ONC’s remarks centered on governance, echoing HHS’s newly released AI Strategy. As we previously explored here, HHS’s five-pillar AI Strategy elevates “Governance and Risk Management for Public Trust” as its lead pillar, formalizing a department-wide AI Governance Board and an “outcomes-first,” use-case-driven approach to adoption. ONC’s remarks reinforced that governance — not just technical safeguards — will anchor how health AI is deployed and overseen going forward. Second, NIST panelists previewed the ongoing refresh of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (“AI RMF”), still anchored in the concept of “trustworthiness” first codified in the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (“NAIIA”). Since its inception, as we discussed here, we have been tracking how the NAIIA impacts AI governance in the public and private sectors. In particular, the NAIIA directed NIST to develop voluntary standards and a risk management framework built around trustworthy AI — privacy, security, bias testing, and robustness among its pillars. NIST’s continuing maturation of the AI RMF, including sector-specific profiles, keeps that statutory trustworthiness mandate at its core. Together, these themes suggest OCR’s HIPAA Security enforcement priorities will increasingly intersect with NIST, FDA, and ONC's parallel efforts to operationalize trustworthy AI across health care. An HHS roundtable discussion at the conference provided an update on breach trends and cybersecurity activities in the health care industry. The timely discussion comes as health care organizations face increasing and more sophisticated cyberattacks. Key points noted in this discussion include: Hacking represents the biggest risk of breach. The vast majority of HIPAA breaches are now caused by hacking incidents. Indeed, of the 338 large breaches (affecting more than 500 individuals) reported to OCR so far in 2026, 313 reports (92.6%) identified the type of breach as “Hacking/IT Incident,” and 236 of those identified the location of breached information as “Network Server.” Extortion is evolving. Cyberattacks against health care entities continue to be part of extortion schemes. However, there is a shift away from the scheme of data encryption and ransomware to data exfiltration or dual modality schemes. This shift is, in part, a response to health care entities making improvements in data backup and restoration.

news.titleEn: CSBS Releases Artificial Intelligence Supervisory Framework for State Examiners
news.titleZh: CSBS发布面向州级审查员的人工智能监管框架
news.summaryZh: 州级银行监理会议于2026年9月16日发布了一份人工智能监管框架。该框架旨在协助州级金融审查员识别并理解受其监管的银行与非银行机构如何使用人工智能，评估相关风险，并判断何时需要进行更深入的审查。框架的发布正值银行与非银行机构快速扩展人工智能应用之际，它为州级审查员提供了统一的AI监管方法。该框架是一项裁量性监管工具，并未设立关于AI使用的新实质性要求。框架采用基于风险的监管原则，考虑机构的规模、复杂性、风险状况及具体AI应用。它借鉴了现有AI风险管理资源，包括美国国家标准与技术研究院的AI风险管理框架、网络风险研究所的金融服务AI风险管理框架以及美国财政部的AI术语表。框架包含多个组成部分：核心审查员指南提供了基本审查方法；审查员工作计划提供了应用该指南的额外指引；针对非银行机构的补充文件则涉及第三方与供应商风险、模型风险及消费者保护。CSBS还开发了可选的人工智能用例风险分级工作表。各州金融监管机构将自行决定在多大程度上将框架纳入其监管计划。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! The Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) on September 16, 2026 released an Artificial Intelligence Supervisory Framework designed to help state financial examiners identify and understand how the bank and non-bank institutions they regulate are using artificial intelligence, assess the associated risks, and determine when a more in-depth review may be appropriate. The framework is significant because it provides state examiners with a common approach to AI supervision at a time when banks and nonbanks are rapidly expanding their use of AI, including generative and agentic AI. At the same time, CSBS emphasizes that the framework is a discretionary supervisory tool and does not establish new substantive requirements governing the use of AI. CSBS is not the only group of regulators focused on artificial intelligence. The American Association of Residential Mortgage Regulators (AARMR), which is comprised of the state agencies who are responsible for supervising non-bank residential mortgage lenders, collaborated with the Mortgage Bankers Association on an industry survey conducted by the Boston Consulting Group as part of AARMR’s goal of understanding how mortgage companies are deploying AI across operations, risk management and compliance, while continuing to ensure consumers are protected. These same regulators will be determining whether they want to adopt the framework for the non-bank mortgage industry, and, if the past is any indication, we should expect wide-spread adoption and implementation of the framework. A Risk-Based Supervisory Framework CSBS says the framework is intended to take into account an institution’s size, complexity, risk profile, and particular uses of AI. It draws upon existing AI risk-management resources, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s AI Risk Management Framework, the Cyber Risk Institute’s Financial Services AI Risk Management Framework, and the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s AI Lexicon. The framework consists of several components. The Core Examiner Guide provides the basic examination approach, including initial scoping questions, a document request list, and procedures addressing AI governance and oversight, AI inventories and use cases, and generative AI and other emerging uses. The Examiner Work Program provides additional guidance for applying the Core Examiner Guide. For nonbanks, the Nonbank AI Supplements address third-party and vendor risk, model risk, and consumer protection. CSBS also has developed an optional AI Use Case Risk Tiering Worksheet that can be used to assess individual AI applications and determine whether additional review may be appropriate. The framework was approved by the CSBS State Supervisory Processes Committee and Nondepository Supervisory Committee in August. Each state financial regulatory agency will determine the extent to which it incorporates the framework into its supervisory program. Why the Framework Matters The most important point for financial institutions is that the framework does not itself impose new legal requirements. Rather, it gives state examiners a structured way to inquire into an institution’s use of AI and determine whether its existing governance, risk-management, and compliance processes adequately address the risks presented by those uses.

news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! The Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) and the NYDFS have each issued new guidance addressing how financial institutions should identify and manage risks associated with AI and other emerging technologies. On September 16, CSBS released a new AI supervisory framework designed to help state examiners assess AI use and related risks at state-chartered banks and state-licensed nonbank financial institutions. The framework follows September 10 guidance from NYDFS addressing cybersecurity risk assessments, including how regulated entities should account for AI and other emerging technologies. The CSBS framework is a discretionary tool designed to help state examiners identify and understand AI use, assess associated risks, and determine when additional review may be appropriate. Each state regulator will decide whether and how to incorporate the framework into its supervisory program. NYDFS, meanwhile, clarified how entities subject to its Cybersecurity Regulation should conduct and update required risk assessments. The NYDFS guidance does not create new obligations, but specifically identifies AI, including frontier AI models, as a technology that may materially change an entity’s cyber risk profile. Specifically, the CSBS framework and NYDFS guidance: Putting It Into Practice: The CSBS framework and NYDFS guidance follows other recent state-level efforts to address the use of AI and emerging technologies in financial services (previously discussed here). The latest developments reinforce the importance of maintaining clear AI governance, inventories of AI use cases, vendor oversight, and risk-assessment procedures that account for changes in technology and business operations. Financial institutions should also monitor how individual state agencies incorporate the CSBS framework into their examination and supervisory programs. news.titleEn: OpenAI Launches Astra For Law
news.titleZh: OpenAI推出面向法律行业的Astra
news.summaryZh: OpenAI正式推出Astra for Law，这是一款由GPT-6 Astra驱动的新产品，配备工具、设置和上下文，以支持律师和法律科技公司的专业判断。Latham & Watkins、Ropes & Gray、Cooley和Sullivan & Cromwell等律所已成为早期采用者。该产品将GPT-6 Astra与法律分析和写作指令、深度工作设置以及新的法律搜索索引相结合。该索引可搜索美国判例法、法规、规章、法院规则和行政决定，覆盖超过2.3亿个URL，并每日更新来源，帮助律师从案件事实转向相关权威和可自行审查的支持性段落。OpenAI还推出了26个合作伙伴构建的插件和47个社区插件，用于ChatGPT中的法律工作，合作伙伴包括Thomson Reuters、Harvey、Legora和iManage，可连接专业工具和知识。社区插件由律师和法律工程师构建，为律所提供可调整和扩展的技能。Astra for Law最初将通过ChatGPT和Codex中的Trusted Access向选定律所提供，API访问即将推出。OpenAI将维护法律配置，以便开发者专注于自身产品和工作流程。据悉，OpenAI最初考虑将法律垂直能力作为Codex的一部分推出，但今年年初以来发生了品牌转变。OpenAI表示将与实际应用该产品的律师和法律技术合作伙伴共同构建Astra for Law的下一篇章。
news.bodyText: After plenty of waiting, OpenAI has launched Astra for Law, a ‘new offering powered by GPT-6 Astra with tools, settings, and context to support the expertise and judgment of lawyers and legal technology firms’. Law firms such as Latham & Watkins, Ropes & Gray, Cooley and Sullivan & Cromwell are already early adopters (see more below). The company explained: ‘Astra for Law pairs GPT-6 Astra with instructions for legal analysis and writing, settings for thorough work, and a new Legal Search Index. The index searches U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, court rules, and administrative decisions across more than 230 million URLs – with sources added daily. That helps lawyers move from the facts of a matter to relevant authorities and supporting passages they can examine themselves. We’re also launching 26 partner-built plugins and 47 community plugins for legal work in ChatGPT. Partners including Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora, and iManage connect specialist tools and knowledge. Community plugins built by lawyers and legal engineers give firms skills they can adapt and extend. Astra for Law will initially be offered to selected firms through Trusted Access in ChatGPT and Codex, with API access coming soon. We’ll maintain the legal configuration so builders can focus on their own products and workflows. We’ll build the next chapter of Astra for Law alongside the lawyers and legal technology partners who put it into practice.’ And here’s a video about Astra for Law. – Initially it’s understood that OpenAI had been looking at rolling out its legal vertical capability as part of Codex, but it seems that between the start of this year and now it’s taken a branding shift, as so often happens. Regardless of what it’s called, it good to see it finally arrive. Here’s an overview from OpenAI of what it will do, then what some law firms are already doing with it.

news.titleEn: Astra for Law + The Battle for Centrality
news.titleZh: Astra for Law 与中心性之战
news.summaryZh: 法律科技领域当前最大的战略挑战是中心性之争，Astra for Law的加入加剧了竞争。其核心在于确定法律工作的主要承载平台。Astra for Law与谷歌的Gemini Enterprise for Legal以及Claude for Legal等大型LLM制造商一样，旨在提供用户愿意驻留的平台或生态系统。用户使用其基础AI和平台工具，当需要法律数据等其他资源时，则通过平台内的‘信息流’获取。这意味着用户可完全在该平台内工作，包括处理Word文档。与此同时，Harvey、Legora、Thomson Reuters和LexisNexis等许多大型法律科技公司也试图实现类似目标，希望用户因其服务而来并留在其生态内。它们会连接外部数据或解决方案以维持用户粘性。所有平台的战略目标一致：实现中心性，即让用户将特定平台视为‘家园’并习惯驻留，平台便能逐步构建更多功能巩固依赖。各大平台每年都在增加功能并不断扩展，倾向于整合其他解决方案或数据，希望成为聚会的中心。根本原因始终是吸引用户并留住他们。然而，这是一场危险的游戏。法律科技公司连接Astra、Claude等平台是为了留住客户，但像Legora这样的公司显然更希望用户始终留在自己身边。此外，在按使用量定价模式日益重要的背景下，这些公司尤其强烈地希望用户保持现状。
news.bodyText: The battle for centrality is now legal tech’s greatest strategic challenge – and Astra for Law just raised the stakes for everyone. That is to say: where does your legal work primarily live? And the answer to that will shape this sector. Astra for Law joins Google’s Gemini Enterprise for Legal and also Claude for Legal – among the largest LLM makers in trying to provide a platform, an ecosystem, or a context, if you prefer that term, that you will stay within. You use their foundational AI, the tools that come with that platform, and when you need something else, e.g. legal data, you use ‘the feed’ into that context. In short, if you want to, you can stay there. Word docs – which are essential for lawyers – are of course part of this, but just part of operating within this platform. Astra becomes the centre of your working life, Gemini does, Claude does….. At the same time, many large legal tech companies are trying to do the same thing. Harvey and Legora would prefer it if you stayed within their context. If you need to find legal data or point solutions that are not already ‘hard-wired’ inside those platforms, then they will seek to connect to them – or at least as much as possible – in a way that again, keeps you there. But then, Thomson Reuters and LexisNexis want you to come to them for their legal research data and then stay within their context for drafting and also transactional needs as well. They also connect to many other offerings. The want the same thing: for you to stay where you have landed. The strategic goal is always the same: centrality. I.e. keeping you there, because the more you see X, Y or Z platform as your ‘home’, the more you will get used to staying there. Then, that platform can build additional features over time that cement you into it. For example, ask yourself the question: have all the large legal tech platforms produced more features each year, or cut back to their core offering? Yep, exactly. They have all expanded, outwards, and outwards, and outwards again. If they can also bring in other legal tech solutions and/or legal data where applicable, into that platform, the better it is for them. No platform wants to be ‘a loner’, they want to be gregarious, extroverted, and friends with everyone. But, also the centre of the party – to be ‘where the action is’. They want to look like a legal tech conference exhibition hall – but their stand is the largest and in the middle of it all…! Why? It’s always the same reason: so you come to that platform, and you stay there. Dangerous Game This is all a dangerous game, of course. Legal tech companies connect to Astra, to Claude, to you name it…..because they want to keep their customers and allow them to use what’s in the market. Everyone is putting on a brave face. But, does Legora really, actively want its customers to fly over to Claude, or Astra and do their legal work from there, and then keep going back there? Would they prefer you stayed with them all of the time? Of course they’d prefer you stay with them. Also, in a world where usage-based (i.e. token) pricing is becoming more relevant to some companies, then such companies really, really want you to stay where you are.
news.relevanceReason: 文章核心围绕法律科技领域的战略竞争，深入探讨了Astra for Law、Gemini Enterprise for Legal、Claude for Legal等法律人工智能平台，以及Harvey、Legora、Thomson Reuters、LexisNexis等法律科技公司如何争夺成为律师工作流程的中心平台。全文聚焦于法律工作流程、平台生态系统、法律数据整合等法律科技核心议题。

news.titleZh: Astra for Law 的 26 个法律科技插件 + 另外一百万个 :)
news.summaryZh: OpenAI 在推出 Astra for Law 的同时，宣布已有 26 个由合作伙伴构建的插件，旨在帮助律师更深入地使用他们已有的工具和知识。这些插件覆盖法律执业和法律业务领域。例如，律师可以在 ChatGPT 中起草谈判简报，并通过 iManage 将其保存到案件文件中；Intapp 可以显示可能需要审查的时间录入活动；DeepJudge 可以将先前的交易引入比较；Thomson Reuters 将 HighQ 案件上下文引入 ChatGPT，并预览即将推出的 CoCounsel Legal 连接器。使用开发者模式，用户可以构建自定义私有插件，将专有数据与工具连接到 ChatGPT，或添加基于 MCP 的插件。私有插件可以使用 Apps SDK 构建。此外，OpenAI 指出，通过使用法律搜索索引，Astra for Law 可以搜索美国判例法、法规、条例、法院规则和行政决定，涵盖超过 2.3 亿个 URL，且来源每日更新。OpenAI 与 Free Law Project（CourtListener 背后的非营利组织）合作，将其判例法集合（覆盖超过 99.9% 的美国已公布先例判例法）纳入研究体验。文章提到，LegalQuants 从发布之初就参与其中。随着时间推移，Litera 和 Definely 也宣布加入该插件群体。文章预计，未来几天内将有更多法律科技公司推出插件，甚至可能所有法律科技公司都会为 Astra for Law 提供插件。
news.bodyText: Alongside the launch of Astra for Law, OpenAI has also announced that there are already 26 ‘partner-built plugins’ (see full list below), that help lawyers ‘go deeper with the tools and knowledge they already use’ – and as far as AL sees it, this increases the ‘centrality’ of the Astra context for lawyers. (Note: since then a million other legal tech companies have been in touch to say they also have a plugin….see below.) OpenAI commented: ‘These plugins cover the practice and business of law. With iManage, a lawyer can draft a negotiation brief in ChatGPT and save it to the matter file; Intapp can surface activities that may need a time entry for review; DeepJudge can bring prior deals into a comparison. Thomson Reuters is bringing HighQ matter context into ChatGPT and previewing a forthcoming CoCounsel Legal connector.’ They also added: ‘Using developer mode, you can build custom private plugins that connect proprietary data and tools to ChatGPT, or add MCP-based plugins from other sources. Private plugins can be built using the Apps SDK.’ As noted above all of this means that once you move your work into Astra, you will find it easier to stay there. Plus, special kudos to LegalQuants for being part of this from launch! One key additional point is legal research. OpenAI said that: ‘By using the legal search index, Astra for Law can search US case law, statutes, regulations, court rules, and administrative decisions across a corpus of more than 230 million URLs, with sources added daily. ‘Our work with Free Law Project, the nonprofit behind CourtListener, brings its case-law collection covering more than 99.9% of published US precedential case law⁠ into this research experience.’ And that’s a big deal just on its own. Now, will this be ‘as good as’ Lexis and TR? We shall see, but OpenAI is very bullish about what it’s able to achieve. So, when you add in all that Astra for Law can do, then add in the plug ins – plus the ability to develop your own, it’s really a massive platform. (Note: as the day has progressed and AL has come back from a wander around Regents Park, Litera has got in touch to say they’re also part of this group now, and Definely is also doing something with OpenAI. No doubt there are a bunch of other ones – and more will be added in the days ahead. In fact, by next Tuesday, at just about tea time, we can assume that every legal tech company on this planet will have a plugin for OpenAI’s Astra for Law. Kudos and safe travels to them all….!)
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要介绍 OpenAI 为法律领域推出的 Astra for Law 平台及其法律科技插件，涉及法律工作流程、法律研究工具和法律科技生态，属于核心法律 AI 报道。

policy.titleEn: Data Union Conference
policy.titleZh: 数据联盟会议
policy.summaryZh: 欧盟委员会将于2027年1月12日在比利时布鲁塞尔查理曼大楼举办高级别会议，汇聚政策制定者、企业、专家和研究人员，旨在将欧洲数据政策转化为更多服务于人工智能、增长和竞争力的数据，并推动关于欧盟数据政策未来的更广泛政治辩论。会议讨论聚焦：数字综合法案，简化欧盟数据规则、减轻行政负担并支持创新；工业人工智能数据，通过《数据法案》改善高质量数据的获取；国际数据流动，促进开放可信的数据流动并确保欧盟企业在海外获得公平待遇。议程将在此页面发布。参会需表达意向并经批准，活动将进行直播。背景方面，欧洲企业和研究人员需要更好地获取高质量数据以开发和部署人工智能。《数据联盟战略》提出了增加数据可用性和加强欧洲数据基础设施的实际措施。欧盟委员会还致力于简化欧盟数字规则，在《数据法案》及其他现有立法基础上减少不必要的负担，使企业更容易使用和共享数据。国际上，委员会寻求促进可信的跨境数据流动，并解决欧盟企业在其他市场面临的不公平限制。这些努力共同旨在支持人工智能发展并增强欧洲竞争力。
policy.bodyText:
12 January 2027

Charlemagne building, Brussels, Belgium

Bringing policymakers, businesses, experts and researchers together to turn Europe’s data policies into more data for AI, growth and competitiveness.

This high-level conference will be hosted by the European Commission. It will contribute to a wider political debate on the future of the EU data Policy.

Main topics on the agenda

During the conference, discussions will focus on:

Digital Omnibus: Simplifying the EU data rulebook, reducing administrative burden and supporting innovation

Data for industrial AI: Improving access to high-quality data through the Data Act

International data flows: Promoting open and trusted data flows and securing fair treatment for EU companies abroad

The agenda will be published here.

Register

You can express your interest in participating . Admission is subject to approval.

The event is going to be live streamed.

Background

European companies and researchers need better access to high-quality data to develop and deploy AI. The Data Union Strategy sets out practical measures to increase data availability and strengthen Europe’s data infrastructure.

The Commission is also working to simplify the EU’s digital rules. Building on the Data Act and other existing legislation, the aim is to reduce unnecessary burdens and make it easier for companies to use and share data.

Internationally, the Commission seeks to facilitate trusted cross-border data flows and address unfair restrictions faced by EU companies in other markets. Together, these efforts aim to support AI development and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness.

Organiser

European Commission

Express your interest in participating

Related topics

Big data

Data policy

Open data

Artificial intelligence

Last update

18 September 2026

Print as PDF

news.titleEn: Descrybe Brings Legal Intelligence Plugin to ChatGPT Enterprise
news.titleZh: Descrybe将法律智能插件引入ChatGPT Enterprise
news.summaryZh: Descrybe宣布其Descrybe Legal Engine插件将专业法律研究直接引入ChatGPT，为ChatGPT用户提供结构化、可验证的美国初级法律及专为AI构建的法律智能。随着AI助手成为法律研究、分析、起草和审查等专业工作的核心环境，将AI系统与权威领域信息连接变得至关重要。该插件帮助ChatGPT识别相关权威依据、评估案件与法律之间的关联，并基于可验证的初级来源开展工作。其技术将美国初级法律与引证关系、后续处理、法律问题、管辖背景、相关性信号和来源材料相连接，以确定哪些权威依据重要及其如何相互关联，然后返回专为AI助手高效使用而结构化的聚焦法律信息。Descrybe从一开始便使用OpenAI技术构建，OpenAI的模型帮助该公司大规模分类、结构化、总结和分析法律材料。此次发布反映Descrybe让复杂法律研究在人们和AI系统工作的任何地方可用的愿景。Descrybe可通过其自有平台、支持的AI环境以及通过Descrybe Open Connector和开发者工具在定制产品和工作流中使用。一份Descrybe Legal Engine订阅可跨支持的助手和应用访问，价格为每用户每月25美元；完整的Descrybe Platform价格为每用户每月50美元，包括Legal Engine访问权限以及完整的研究工作区和高级法律研究与审查能力。
news.bodyHtml:
The Descrybe Legal Engine plugin gives ChatGPT users access to structured, verifiable U.S. primary law and legal intelligence built specifically for AI.

 

BOSTON, Sept. 17, 2026 — Descrybe today announced that the Descrybe Legal Engine plugin is bringing specialized legal research directly into ChatGPT.

The launch comes as AI assistants are becoming a central environment for professional work, including legal research, analysis, drafting, and review. As that shift accelerates, connecting AI systems to authoritative domain information becomes critical. Descrybe was built for this moment. 

“AI is changing the way legal work gets done, and one of the most exciting parts of that shift is how much more accessible sophisticated legal research can become,” said Kara Peterson, co-founder and CEO of Descrybe. “Bringing deep legal intelligence directly into an environment like ChatGPT puts powerful research capabilities within reach of many more people and organizations through a tool they already know how to use. That can fundamentally change who can benefit from sophisticated legal research technology.”

The Descrybe Legal Engine plugin helps ChatGPT identify relevant authority, assess how cases and laws relate to one another, and work from verifiable primary sources. Its technology connects U.S. primary law with citation relationships, subsequent treatment, legal issues, jurisdictional context, relevance signals, and source material to help determine which authorities matter and how they fit together, then returns focused legal information structured specifically for AI assistants to use efficiently.

Descrybe itself was built from the beginning using OpenAI technology. OpenAI’s models have helped the company classify, structure, summarize, and analyze legal materials at scale.

“Frontier models made it possible for a small team like ours to build something extraordinarily ambitious,” said Richard DiBona, co-founder and CTO of Descrybe. “We’ve used OpenAI’s technology to transform a vast body of legal material into legal intelligence that AI can work with effectively. Bringing Descrybe into ChatGPT with this plugin closes that loop in a really powerful way.”

The launch reflects Descrybe’s broader vision of making sophisticated legal research available wherever people and AI systems work. Descrybe can be used through its own platform, across supported AI environments, and inside custom products and workflows through the Descrybe Open Connector and developer tools.

One Descrybe Legal Engine subscription provides access across supported assistants and apps for $25 per user per month. The full Descrybe Platform is available for $50 per user per monthand includes Legal Engine access along with Descrybe’s complete research workspace and advanced legal research and review capabilities.

###

About Descrybe

Descrybe is a legal research and intelligence platform for people and AI systems. Its technology combines extensive U.S. primary-law coverage with citation, subsequent treatment, legal issues, and source intelligence to help users move from finding law to understanding what matters. Descrybe can be used directly through the Descrybe Platform, through Descrybe Legal Engine in leading AI assistants, and through the Descrybe Open Connector in custom AI tools and workflows. Founded on the belief that sophisticated legal technology should be broadly accessible, Descrybe brings powerful, reliable legal research and intelligence wherever legal work happens.

For more information, visit Descrybe.com.

Media Contact
Kara Peterson
Co-Founder & CEO
kara@descrybe.com

news.titleEn: OpenAI Releases Astra for Law, A GPT-6 Model Tailored for Legal Work, Targeting Large Firms and Tech Vendors
news.titleZh: OpenAI发布面向法律行业的Astra，基于GPT-6模型定制，瞄准大型律所和技术供应商
news.summaryZh: OpenAI发布Astra for Law，这是其最新模型GPT-6 Astra针对法律工作配置的版本，包含专用法律搜索索引以及用于法律分析和写作的自定义指令。Astra for Law将很快向API客户开放，包括Harvey和Legora，并至少初期通过新的“Trusted Access”计划向部分律所提供，该计划针对Am Law 200律所，通过ChatGPT及其软件工程代理Codex授予专门访问权限。Trusted Access计划包括API新的零数据保留政策，以及ChatGPT Enterprise不被OpenAI任何人员人工审查。获得访问权限的律所和法律技术公司可在其基础上构建，无需自行组装和维护底层法律搜索与指令。OpenAI还推出了一系列新插件，使ChatGPT在法律工作中更实用和可扩展，包括来自Thomson Reuters、Harvey、Legora和iManage等供应商的26个插件、由律师和法律工程师构建的9个插件，以及47项自定义技能。此外，OpenAI宣布ChatGPT for Word正式可用，律师可在Word内使用ChatGPT进行校对、获取建议编辑并标记格式问题。此前，OpenAI于6月聘请合同生命周期管理公司Ironclad的联合创始人兼前CEO Jason Boehmig领导法律行业产品开发。在该招聘之前，竞争对手Anthropic已通过推出Claude for Legal大举进军法律领域。昨日，Boehmig和领导法律产品开发的OpenAI工程师Sherwin Wu就Astra for Law向媒体作了简报。Boehmig强调这不是新模型，而是为法律工作定制模型的配置，包括法律写作等任务的领域特定指令、响应长度等设置以及法律行业特定工具，这些都将随时间增长。
news.bodyHtml:
Calling it the beginning of its long-term investment in law, ChatGPT developer OpenAI today released Astra for Law, a version of its latest model, GPT-6 Astra, configured for legal work, including a dedicated legal search index and custom instructions for legal analysis and writing.

“Today, we’re introducing Astra for Law: a new foundation for law firms and legal technology companies to build AI products and workflows around their expertise,” the company said in a blog post announcing the product. “It combines GPT-6 Astra, our latest and most powerful model, with settings, tools, and context tailored for professional legal work — from researching complex cases to structuring consequential deals.”

The company said that Astra for Law will be available soon to API customers, including Harvey and Legora, and offered, at least initially, to selected law firms through a new “Trusted Access” program targeting Am Law 200 firms that grants specialized access through ChatGPT and Codex, its software engineering agent.

The Trusted Access program includes a new zero data retention policy for the API and exclusion of ChatGPT Enterprise from human review by anyone at OpenAI.

Firms and legal technology companies with access to Astra for Law will be able to build on its foundation without having to assemble and maintain the underlying legal search and instructions on their own, the company said.

In addition to launching Astra for Law, OpenAI said it is launching a series of new plugins designed to make ChatGPT more useful and extensible for legal work, including 26 from vendors such as Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora and iManage and nine built by lawyers and legal engineers, as well as 47 custom skills.

Also, OpenAI announced the general availability of ChatGPT for Word, enabling lawyers to use ChatGPT within Word to proofread, get suggested edits, and flag formatting issues.

All of this follows the company’s hiring in June of Jason Boehmig, the cofounder and former CEO of contract lifecycle management company Ironclad, to lead development of products for the legal industry.

Ahead of that hiring, OpenAI competitor Anthropic had announced its own major push into legal with the launch of Claude for Legal.

Related: On LawNext: Inside Claude for Legal — Anthropic’s Mark Pike on AI’s Next Frontier in Law.

Embedded Legal Research

Yesterday, Boehmig and Sherwin Wu, the OpenAI engineer who has led the development of the legal product, provided a briefing for the media on Astra for Law.

Boehmig emphasized that this is not a new model, but rather a model configuration to customize the model for legal work. It includes domain-specific instructions on tasks such as legal writing, settings such as the length of responses, and tooling specific to the legal industry, all of which will grow over time.

The first major implementation of that tooling is its Legal Search Index, a legal research capability that allows it to search U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, court rules and administrative decisions across a corpus of more than 230 million URLs.

To create its collection of legal research materials, OpenAI drew from CourtListener, the legal research library maintained by the nonprofit Free Law Project.

Beyond simply conducting legal research, OpenAI says that Astra for Law is designed to use that Legal Search Index to help lawyers apply the law to the facts of a matter, to develop arguments or deal terms, and to identify weaknesses or uncertainty.

During the briefing, Wu demonstrated three tasks, in which he used Astra for Law in ChatGPT to draft a motion to dismiss for a hospital defending a disability-discrimination and retaliation claim, a stockholder challenge to an asset sale rushed through over a holiday weekend, and for a sales-commitment dispute.

Product Benchmarking

OpenAI says it tested Astra for Law’s legal research capabilities against 200 U.S. legal research questions from the private validation set of Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, a benchmark that measures how well the model can find relevant sources and passages, and how well its research answers meet the evaluation criteria.

At the highest reasoning effort for both systems, the company says, Astra for Law passed the evaluation’s overall correctness check on 54% of questions, compared with 38.7% for GPT-6 Astra using web search alone – an increase of 15.3 percentage points, or a 40% relative improvement.

Astra for Law also produces more comprehensive answers, roughly twice as long on average as the Astra web-only baseline across the tested reasoning settings, the company says.

On case-law-focused questions, Astra for Law found 24% more reference cases than GPT-6 Astra using web search alone at the highest reasoning effort. On the audited set of target passages, it retrieved up to 54% more relevant passages from the correct court opinions, when comparing the systems at the same reasoning effort.

New Partner and Community Plugins

As part of today’s announcement, OpenAI is also launching a series of vendor- and community-developed plugins designed to help legal professionals do more with ChatGPT, including 26 developed by partners such as Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora and iManage.

As examples of what the vendor plugins will enable, OpenAI said iManage’s will allow a lawyer to draft a negotiation brief in ChatGPT and save it to the matter file, Intapp’s will surface activities that may need a time entry for review, DeepJudge’s will bring prior deals into a comparison, and Thomson Reuters’ will bring HighQ matter context into ChatGPT and later include a connector to CoCounsel Legal.

There are also nine community plugins developed by lawyers and legal engineers at LegalQuants, LegalEng Consulting Group (LECG), and Skills.law, and 47 custom skills that legal professionals can adapt, extend or draw inspiration from to do work in ChatGPT. OpenAI said these custom skills were developed by legal “power users,” not by OpenAI.

New ‘Trusted Access Program’

As part of the new offering, the company is creating a special Trusted Access Program under which eligible law firms will be able to give lawyers and people working under their supervision access to Astra for Law for professional legal work.

The program is targeted at Am Law 200 programs. For firms that qualify, the offering includes zero data retention on the API and usage of ChatGPT enterprise is excluded from human review.

In addition, OpenAI said it is working with the law firm Latham & Watkins to design for information permissions, ethical walls, client instructions, and firm oversight.

Asked by a reporter whether there were any exceptions to the zero data retention policy, Boehmig said that is a one-sentence summary of the full access-program agreement, which runs some 30 pages. But he said OpenAI has worked with the industry to validate that it works in this context. “It’s definitely more complicated than the one sentence,” he said, “but we also feel extremely confident that the 30 pages do meet the need.”

Building On Firms’ Own Knowledge

OpenAI’s announcement stresses the importance for law firms of building AI around their own precedents, methods and judgment, and offers several examples of how its forward-deployed engineers — OpenAI engineers who are embedded within a law firm — have been adapting ChatGPT Enterprise through custom integrations with firms’ proprietary data and workflows.

It says that Sullivan & Cromwell, for example, built an agreement analyzer that uses the firm’s negotiating playbooks and selected precedents in the review of a new deal. Another firm, Ropes & Gray, built an M&A diligence system around how its lawyers work through a data room and decide what matters to the deal.

Still another, Cooley, built GO Public to bring its capital markets expertise into how companies prepare to go public, from drafting the IPO filing to identifying the risks that deserve management’s attention.

“With frontier intelligence and the right controls, firms can turn their own precedents, methods, and judgment into AI tools and workflows built to their standards,” OpenAI says.

Just the Beginning

“OpenAI is investing in law for the long term,” the company said in making these announcements.

It said that it will continue to improve ChatGPT as a platform for firms to build around their expertise and connect the tools they already use, and to conduct rigorous evaluations and collect user feedback to monitor where improvements are needed and what to bulid next.

In response to a question at the media briefing, Boehmig said the company’s commitment to legal includes a commitment to access to justice, which he said is a “paramount concern” to him personally and to OpenAI as a company, but that today’s news is focused on Astra for Law and that there will be more to share in the future related to A2J.

“We’re committed to working with this ecosystem so firms can bring their own expertise, standards, and judgment to AI – and serve clients in ways only they can,” the company said.

news.titleZh: AI进入陪审团席：前景、局限与人类审议的作用
news.summaryZh:
北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校法学院据报在基于真实少年案件的模拟审判中，使用ChatGPT、Claude和Grok担任陪审员。与此同时，AI驱动的陪审团研究平台正进入诉讼咨询市场，为律师和理赔专业人员提供责任、比较过失和潜在损害赔偿的快速评估。这些工具有助于法律团队测试竞争性叙事、识别能引起共鸣的主题，并标记可能不受欢迎的论点，且比传统陪审团研究更快、成本更低。

但律师应区分可靠性与有效性。AI模拟可能稳定测量个人对案件摘要的反应，却仍无法捕捉实际陪审团达成裁决的方式。真实陪审员会讨论证据、质疑彼此假设，并通过审议修正观点。特定审判地的态度和社区规范也会影响结果，而广泛的模拟人群可能无法反映这些因素。因此，AI陪审团研究最好被视为筛选工具，而非焦点小组、模拟审判或其他互动方法的替代品。它可以为早期案件评估提供信息，帮助律师决定何处需要更深入研究，但其精美的百分比和损害赔偿范围不应被误认为实际裁决的预测。对法律团队而言，关键问题不是AI或传统研究哪个绝对更好，而是所选方法是否衡量了重要问题。当案件取决于有争议的证据、群体动态和集体判断时，人类审议仍然至关重要。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! Last fall, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Law reportedly used ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok as jurors in a mock trial based on a real juvenile case. At the same time, AI-powered jury research platforms are entering the litigation consulting market, offering attorneys and claims professionals rapid assessments of liability, comparative fault, and potential damages. These tools can provide valuable early insights. They may help legal teams test competing narratives, identify themes that resonate and flag arguments that could be poorly received, all faster and at a lower cost than traditional jury research. However, lawyers should distinguish reliability from validity. An AI simulation may consistently measure individual reactions to a case summary yet still fail to capture how an actual jury reaches a verdict. Real jurors discuss evidence, challenge each other’s assumptions, and revise their views through deliberation. Venue-specific attitudes and community norms also shape outcomes in ways that broad simulated populations may not reflect. AI jury research is therefore best viewed as a screening tool rather than a substitute for focus groups, mock trials, or other interactive methods. It can inform early case assessment and help counsel decide where deeper research is warranted, but its polished percentages and damages ranges should not be mistaken for predictions of an actual verdict. For legal teams, the key question is not whether AI or traditional research is categorically better, it is whether the chosen method measures the issue that matters. When a case turns on contested evidence, group dynamics, and collective judgment, human deliberation remains central. news.titleEn: AI Governance Lagging Behind Rapid Employee Adoption of AI Tools
news.titleZh: AI治理滞后于员工对AI工具的快速采用
news.summaryZh: OneTrust发布的《2026年AI就绪治理报告》调查结果显示，员工采用AI工具的速度超过了公司AI治理项目的跟进速度。尽管各组织表示正在采用治理项目来应对组织内AI的使用，但“一些组织知道代理正在业务的部分环节被使用，却缺乏一致的监督。另一些组织则对代理在何处以及如何使用缺乏可见性。”与其他研究一致，“近半数受访者报告称，在过去一年中至少发生过一次AI系统或代理采取未经批准行动的事件。”调查传达的信息是，在组织采用AI治理项目的过程中，你并不孤单。专注于风险分类、了解员工如何使用AI，并在应对AI快速采用的同时培养安全与安保文化，将有助于降低风险。最重要的是持续应对，不要因不堪重负而放弃。这是一个持续、迭代的过程，需要定期评估和微调，因此要深入投入并组建一个致力于长期努力的团队。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! Survey results released in OneTrust’s 2026 AI-Ready Governance Report shows that employees are adopting AI tools more rapidly than company AI governance programs can keep up. Although organizations indicated they were adopting governance programs to address the use of AI in their organizations, “Some organizations know agents are being used in parts of the business without consistent oversight. Others lack visibility into where and how agents are used.” Consistent with other research “nearly half of respondents reported at least one incident during the past year in which AI systems or agents took unapproved actions.” The message of the survey is that you are not alone in the journey to adopt an AI governance program for your organization. Concentrating on risk classification, understanding how employees are using AI, and developing a culture of safety and security while grappling with the rapid adoption of AI will help mitigate risk. The most important thing is to keep tackling it, and don’t get overwhelmed and give up. It is an ongoing, iterative process that will need regular assessment and fine tuning, so dig in and assemble a team committed to working on it for the long term. news.titleEn: Google Shows Off Cloud Legal AI Helpers + More
news.titleZh: 谷歌展示云端法律AI助手等更多功能
news.summaryZh: 昨日，“Google Legal”展示了Gemini Enterprise如何为律师部署，涵盖日常提示、NotebookLM使用及自定义应用开发。演示由Google Cloud法律顾问Xavier Polidoro主持，重点是他所称的“高级”用途，包括“云端法律AI助手”。这些定制解决方案似乎与更具体品牌的“Gemini Enterprise for Legal”相关联——该近期宣布的产品附带多个代理，但此处使用了不同措辞。展示内容概述如下，其中许多仅涉及律师如何使用Gemini LLM能力以及NotebookLM进行法律工作。最后，Polidoro介绍了可连接任意来源并执行特定任务（如红线标注文档或协助撰写简报）的定制代理开发。他们还提及Harvey使用Gemini，以及Freshfields和Inspira。演示包括：一般提示——使用Gemini Enterprise聊天加速合同摘要、风险标记和初步客户沟通；基于来源的研究——使用Gemini Notebook搜索、交叉引用和总结密集法律库及多修订协议，并完全基于来源；自定义助手——云端法律AI助手演练，展示法律团队如何构建和部署用于交易管理的自定义聊天机器人。在介绍如何充分利用Gemini标准提示后，Polidoro转向NotebookLM。它提供许多功能，包括将工作成果转为音频“播客”——这很疯狂，但主要好处是连接Notebook到多个来源然后开始工作。谷歌强调可添加300个来源，每个最多50万字。简言之，律所或法律团队可将Notebook连接到大量文档和数据，这非常有用。
news.bodyText: Yesterday, ‘Google Legal’ gave an inside look at how Gemini Enterprise can be deployed for lawyers, from everyday prompting, to NotebookLM use, to custom app development. Artificial Lawyer was there. The demonstration was led by Xavier Polidoro, Legal Counsel, Google Cloud, and the highlight was what he called the ‘advanced’ uses, which covered ‘Cloud Legal AI Helpers’. These customised solutions appear to connect to the more specifically branded ‘Gemini Enterprise for Legal’ – the recently announced offering that comes with a number of agents, although in this case they used a different wording. Here’s an overview of what was on show – with a lot of it simply about how lawyers can use the Gemini LLM capability and also NotebookLM for legal work. At the end, Polidoro covered the development of customised agents that can be connected to whatever sources you want, and then steered to perform certain tasks, e.g. redline a document, or help to write brief. They also interestingly mentioned Harvey’s use of Gemini, as well as Freshfields – which they have mentioned before, and also Inspira. So, first an overview of what they showed, then NotebookLM, then the Legal AI Helpers Live In-Tool Demonstrations: ‘General Prompting: Accelerating contract summaries, risk flagging, and preliminary client communications using Gemini Enterprise chat. Grounded Research: Using Gemini Notebook to search, cross-reference, and summarize dense legal repositories and multi-amendment agreements with full source grounding. Custom Helpers: A walkthrough of the Cloud Legal AI Helpers, showing how legal teams can build and deploy custom chatbots for deal management.’ – After an introduction on how to get the most out of standard prompting with Gemini, Polidoro moved onto NotebookLM. It’s got a lot on offer, including turning your work product into an audio ‘podcast’ – which is wild, but the main benefit is simply the way that you can connect Notebook to multiple sources and then get to work. Google highlighted that you can add in 300 sources, each up to 500,000 words. In short, a law firm or legal team could connect Notebook to a huge trove of documents and data. And that’s really useful.
news.relevanceReason: 文章主要介绍谷歌面向法律行业的AI工具，包括Gemini Enterprise for Legal、云端法律AI助手、NotebookLM在法律工作中的应用，以及定制代理开发等，核心内容围绕法律AI和律所技术。

research.titleEn: Structured Four-Stage Legal Translation: From Natural-Language Traffic Rules to PROLOG
research.titleZh: 结构化四阶段法律翻译：从自然语言交通规则到PROLOG
research.abstractEn: Traffic regulations are written for human interpretation and therefore rely on shared background knowledge and flexible phrasing, which inherently introduce ambiguity, context dependence, and semantic underspecification. These linguistic characteristics conflict with the precision required by computational reasoning engines such as Prolog, which demand explicit logical structure. This study evaluates two baseline translation approaches, Natural Language to Prolog ($NL\rightarrow Prolog$) and Logical English to Prolog ($LE\rightarrow Prolog$), and introduces a new reasoning-guided translation framework called Structured Four-Stage Legal Translation ($S4L\rightarrow Prolog$). The proposed S4L framework performs semantic role extraction, scene completion, logical mapping, and Prolog rule generation within a single guided prompt, enabling direct translation of raw traffic rules into executable logic without human intervention. A benchmark consisting of twenty real-world traffic rules was used to evaluate each approach in terms of syntactic validity, semantic correctness, and logical completeness. $S4L\rightarrow Prolog$ achieves the highest accuracy, correctly formalizing 75 percent of the rules, while $NL\rightarrow Prolog$ reaches 60 percent and $LE\rightarrow Prolog$ reaches 55 percent. Qualitative analysis further shows that S4L captures implicit causal relations, deontic modality, and exception structure more reliably than the baselines. These results demonstrate that structured reasoning prompts can substantially improve the reliability of natural-language-to-logic translation for legal and safety-critical applications.
research.abstractZh: 交通法规是为人类解释而编写的，因此依赖于共享的背景知识和灵活的措辞，这本质上引入了歧义、上下文依赖和语义不明确性。这些语言特征与Prolog等计算推理引擎所需的精确性相冲突，后者要求明确的逻辑结构。本研究评估了两种基线翻译方法：自然语言到Prolog（$NL\rightarrow Prolog$）和逻辑英语到Prolog（$LE\rightarrow Prolog$），并引入了一种新的推理引导翻译框架，称为结构化四阶段法律翻译（$S4L\rightarrow Prolog$）。所提出的S4L框架在单个引导提示中执行语义角色提取、场景补全、逻辑映射和Prolog规则生成，使得无需人工干预即可将原始交通规则直接翻译为可执行逻辑。使用包含二十条真实世界交通规则的基准，从语法有效性、语义正确性和逻辑完整性方面评估了每种方法。$S4L\rightarrow Prolog$达到了最高准确率，正确形式化了75%的规则，而$NL\rightarrow Prolog$达到60%，$LE\rightarrow Prolog$达到55%。定性分析进一步表明，S4L比基线更可靠地捕捉隐含因果 relations、道义模态和例外结构。这些结果表明，结构化推理提示可以显著提高法律和安全关键应用中自然语言到逻辑翻译的可靠性。

policy.titleEn: 守好网络法治防线 护航数字经济行稳致远 ——最高法发布典型案例聚焦网络法治
policy.titleZh: 守好网络法治防线 护航数字经济行稳致远 ——最高法发布典型案例聚焦网络法治
policy.summaryZh:
2026年9月14日至20日国家网络安全宣传周期间，最高人民法院于9月16日发布4件典型案例，聚焦网络法治，明确网络暴力人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害人格权责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务定罪量刑等问题。

案例一为李某申请人格权侵害禁令案。李某与张某、胡某均为短视频平台自媒体博主，张某、胡某账号合计超2000万粉丝。2023年7月起，张某以李某“插足”其与男友情感为由发布侮辱、诽谤言论并联合胡某炒作，煽动粉丝实施网络暴力，致李某部分商业合作方解约；诉讼中二人仍继续实施。法院认定符合民法典第九百九十七条人格权侵害禁令适用条件，明确应综合考量侵权方式与信息传播速度范围判断紧迫性、人格权类型与救济手段是否充分判断损害是否难以弥补、相关因素裁定禁令措施防止超出必要限度。《最高人民法院关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》亦对依法适用该禁令制度作出规范。案例二为李某瑾诉某文化公司网络侵权责任纠纷案。某文化公司委托带货主播制作发布短视频推广家庭育儿类图书，约定视频侵权由委托方担责；主播未经授权截取李某瑾演讲、授课视频片段，搭配音色、语调、发音风格高度近似的AI合成音频，制作发布带跳转购书链接的宣传视频，某文化公司未审核素材及授权材料。
policy.bodyText:
遭遇“网暴”如何快速拿起维权的法律武器？如何划分“技术创新”的权责边界？为网络犯罪提供“技术帮助”，究竟要承担怎样的法律责任？
2026年9月14日至20日是国家网络安全宣传周，主题为“网络安全为人民，网络安全靠人民——智能时代网安护航”。网络强国建设离不开司法审判工作的支撑与保障，宣传周期间，最高人民法院于9月16日发布4件典型案例，明确发生网络暴力时的人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害他人人格权的责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者的侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务的定罪量刑等问题，用鲜活案例明晰网络行为法律边界，用裁判规范引领网络空间法治风尚。
用好人格权禁令，筑牢人格权益“防火墙”
网络暴力传播快、范围广、伤害深，有时一条谣言、一场直播“围攻”，就足以让受害者陷入精神伤害、名誉贬损、经济损失的困境。而且这种损害结果往往不可逆，即使事后通过司法程序赢得了赔偿，也很难完全抚平受害人的创伤。
民法典第九百九十七条设立人格权侵害禁令制度，目的是及时制止人格权侵权、防止损害发生和扩大，按下侵权“停止键”。不久前出台的《最高人民法院关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》，亦对依法适用人格权侵害禁令制度作出相关规范。但在司法实践中，如何把握人格权侵害禁令条款“不及时制止将使其合法权益受到难以弥补的损害”这一适用条件，一直是实践中的难点问题。
在第一个典型案例“李某申请人格权侵害禁令案”中，李某与张某、胡某均为短视频平台自媒体博主，张某、胡某的网络账号共计有超2000万粉丝。2023年7月起，张某以李某“插足”其与男友情感为由，在网络平台公开发布针对李某的侮辱、诽谤言论，并联合胡某炒作相关话题，煽动粉丝对李某实施谩骂、攻击、举报等网络暴力行为。事件发生后，李某的部分商业合作方解除与李某的合作协议。
随后，李某提起名誉权侵权诉讼，但在案件审理过程中，张某、胡某仍煽动粉丝实施上述网络暴力行为，李某遂向法院申请人格权侵害禁令。
法院审理认为，张某、胡某对李某实施了群体性网络暴力违法行为，且在案件审理过程中仍继续实施上述网络暴力行为、扩大损害结果。张某、胡某通过直播等形式在网络上传播侵权信息，案涉信息传播速度快、波及范围广、负面影响大，已对李某造成精神损害和经济损失，不及时制止将导致李某合法权益受到难以弥补的损害，符合人格权侵害禁令适用条件。
对于网络暴力情形下适用人格权侵害禁令的审查，本案明确了三个应当综合考量的因素。一是综合考量侵权行为方式、信息传播速度和范围等因素，判断是否达到需要及时制止的紧迫性标准；二是综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵害行为性质、事后赔偿等救济手段是否能够充分弥补申请人的损害等因素，审查损害是否难以弥补；三是综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵权行为方式以及损害范围、程度等因素，裁定采取相应禁令措施，防止超出必要限度。
划清权责边界，回应数字时代新挑战
随着人工智能技术深度融入各类互联网场景，AI换脸拟声、大模型检索生成等新应用层出不穷。但技术在赋能产业的同时，新的侵权纠纷也随之衍生。
在电商平台，一些商家委托主播剪辑他人公开影像，配上高度仿真AI合成声音，假借名人影响力推销商品，殊不知已经违反了法律。
“李某瑾诉某文化公司网络侵权责任纠纷案”正是这样一起关于“AI仿名人带货”套路的典型案例。在本案中，某文化公司为推广销售家庭育儿类图书，委托某带货主播制作发布短视频进行网络宣传，并协议约定，视频侵犯第三方合法权益的，由委托方承担责任。某带货主播未经授权擅自截取李某瑾演讲、授课的视频片段，搭配音色、语调、发音风格与李某瑾高度近似的AI合成音频，制作并发布带有跳转购书链接的宣传视频。经查，案涉视频中的相关素材并未取得李某瑾的授权，某文化公司也未对案涉视频的相关素材及授权材料进行审核。
法院审理认为，案涉视频未经李某瑾同意，擅自使用李某瑾肖像并结合使用与其声纹特征高度吻合的AI合成声音，构成对李某瑾肖像权和声音权益的侵害。某文化公司未对视频素材的来源、视频素材是否获得李某瑾授权等事项进行审核，存在未尽合理审核义务的过失，构成共同侵权。遂判决某文化公司向李某瑾赔礼道歉、赔偿经济损失及维权合理支出。
本案判决提示广大电商经营者：带货主播受电子商务经营者委托，通过制作发布视频等方式进行商品推广时，故意使用侵害他人人格权等权益的素材的，构成侵权；委托人电子商务经营者对宣传推广内容未尽到法律规定或者合同约定的审核义务，对损害结果发生存在过失的，与带货主播成立共同侵权，应依法承担连带责任。

news.titleEn: On LawNext: Alex Su, Newly Named President of Latitude Legal, On Why AI Is Driving Demand for Flex Talent
news.titleZh: LawNext播客：新任Latitude Legal总裁Alex Su谈AI为何推动灵活人才需求
news.summaryZh: Alex Su被任命为灵活法律服务公司Latitude Legal的总裁，并再次做客LawNext播客。去年二月，他曾在该播客中谈及自己的职业经历：从Sullivan & Cromwell律师，到联邦法院书记员，再到法律科技初创公司，最终担任Latitude首席营收官。当时他预测，随着AI能力提升，对具备真正判断力的律师的需求只会增长，这些律师需要指导AI、核查AI并对工作成果负责。七个月后，这一预测得到验证。今年上半年新签约的律师事务所和企业客户数量增长了52%。Su此次回归节目，讨论为何他认为AI正在推动对经验丰富律师的更多需求，而非减少。他还谈到Latitude的客户服务模式如何依赖前律所合伙人和资深内部法律顾问，为何他反对将灵活人才称为“合同律师”或将Latitude称为ALSP，以及为何他预计随着律所和法律部门厘清AI能处理与不能处理的事务，灵活法律人才市场将持续扩大。本期节目由Paradigm（旗下拥有PracticePanther、Bill4Time、MerusCase和LollyLaw等执业管理平台，以及电子支付平台Headnote和法律会计软件TrustBooks）、Briefpoint（消除常规证据开示响应和请求起草任务）、CosmoLex（帮助律所在一个平台上管理从受理到支付的整个执业流程）和Ajax（律师想要使用的AI计时器）赞助。
news.bodyHtml:
Call it Alex Su, redux. We do not usually have the same guest on LawNext twice in the same year, but there is good reason to have Alex back, as he has just been named president of Latitude Legal, the flexible legal staffing company.

Last February, Alex and I recorded a live episode of this podcast over lunch in a Cambodian restaurant in Alex’s hometown of Alameda, Calif., as part of our LawNext on Location series. We talked about his winding career, from Sullivan & Cromwell associate to federal clerkship to legal tech startups and finally to chief revenue officer at Latitude.

In that interview, I asked Alex what was coming next. His answer was that as AI got better, the demand for lawyers with real judgment — to direct it, check it, and own the work — would only grow. Seven months later, that prediction is proving prescient. In just the first half of this year, Latitude says it has seen a 52 percent jump in new law firm and corporate clients.

So with Latitude’s promotion of Su to president, he returns to LawNext to discuss why he thinks AI is driving more demand for experienced lawyers, not less. He also talks about how Latitude’s client-service model relies on former law firm partners and senior in-house counsel, why he pushes back on labeling flex talent as “contract attorneys” or calling Latitude an ALSP, and why he expects the market for flexible legal talent to keep expanding as law firms and legal departments sort out what AI can and cannot handle.

news.titleEn: RelativityOne Gets A New Name To Reflect Its Increasing Capabilities Around AI and Data
news.titleZh: RelativityOne更名以反映其在AI和数据方面不断增强的能力
news.summaryZh: 电子取证公司Relativity宣布，将其云平台RelativityOne更名为Relativity aiR，该名称此前用于Relativity的AI与代理能力套件。更名旨在将平台及其AI能力统一在一个名称下。AI是如同当年云一样具有变革性的转变，Relativity拥有值得信赖的平台和经验来负责任地引领这一转变。Relativity自2001年成立以来长期仅提供本地部署产品，2017年推出SaaS替代方案RelativityOne。尽管本地产品曾是电子取证领域的巨头，云平台最终取代了它，去年Saunders宣布2028年所有新案件必须迁移至RelativityOne。同时，Relativity推出了一系列生成式AI产品，始于2023年宣布的Relativity aiR for Review，用于帮助用户更快定位响应发现请求的数据。此后陆续推出aiR for Privilege用于特权审查、aiR for Case Strategy用于创建叙述和时间线、aiR Assist用于对话式AI辅助，以及最近的Relativity claiR，专为律师设计的对话式AI。从RelativityOne到Relativity aiR的转变强化了Relativity的焦点：AI原生嵌入整个平台、AI代理支持现有工作并开启新工作、围绕AI代理构建更简单体验，以及可扩展性赋能合作伙伴和从业者社区解决新的独特法律挑战。更名反映客户越来越多地将平台用于诉讼之外的一系列数据智能目的。实际上，客户在平台上创建的新事项中超过一半并非用于诉讼。Brown写道，行业已完全进入AI平台时代，法律数据与专门构建的代理能力相结合，以推动更好的结果并扩展法律团队的事项智能。Relativity aiR的AI能力包含在平台当前定价中，因此采用2026定价计划的客户将能访问所有代理工具。
news.bodyHtml:
Perhaps it is only fitting that a product launched in the cloud should be renamed for the atmosphere it occupies.

The e-discovery company Relativity announced today that it has renamed RelativityOne, its cloud-based platform, as Relativity aiR, giving it the name that had previously been assigned to Relativity’s suite of AI and agentic capabilities.

The purpose of the name change, the company said, is to unify the platform and its AI capabilities under one name.

“This name confirms what our community already knows: AI is as transformative a shift as the cloud was years ago, and Relativity has the trusted platform and the experience to lead through it responsibly,” Phil Saunders, the company’s CEO, said in an announcement.

Starting from its founding in 2001, Relativity had long offered only as an on-premises product. In 2017, it introduced RelativityOne as a SaaS alternative. Even though the on-premises product had long been the 800-pound gorilla of e-discovery technology, the cloud platform eventually came to supersede it, to the point where, last year, Saunders announced a 2028 deadline for all new cases to move to RelativityOne.

Meanwhile, Relativity has been introducing a series of generative AI products, starting with its 2023 announcement of Relativity aiR for Review, designed to help users more quickly locate data responsive to a discovery request.

It has since rolled out aiR for Privilege for privilege review, aiR for Case Strategy for creating narratives and timelines, aiR Assist for conversational AI assistance, and, most recently, Relativity claiR, a conversational AI designed specifically for lawyers.

“The shift from RelativityOne to Relativity aiR reinforces where Relativity is focused: AI embedded natively throughout the platform, AI agents supporting the work already performed and opening up new kinds of work, simpler experiences built around AI agents, and extensibility that empowers Relativity’s community of partners and practitioners to solve new and unique legal challenges,” the company said in its announcement.

In a companion blog post, Chris Brown, who was recently named Relativity president after having been its chief product officer since 2018, said that the name change reflects the fact that customers are increasingly using the platform for a range of data intelligence purposes that extend beyond litigation.

In fact, he said, more than half of new matters customers are creating on the platform are not for litigation at all.

“Our industry is now fully entrenched in the era of the AI platform, where legal data is paired with purpose-built agentic capabilities to drive stronger outcomes and expand legal teams’ matter
intelligence,” Brown writes.

“That’s what we’ve been building: a system of record that securely houses your most sensitive and complex data at extraordinary scale, and a system of action that reads deeply into the documents, pairing agents with human judgment to surface insights and turn them into impactful work product.”

Relativity aiR’s AI capabilities are included in the platform’s current pricing, so customers on the 2026 pricing plan will have access to every agentic tool as part of the  platform.

news.titleEn: Charting Change in Legal: AI organisational readiness
news.titleZh: 法律领域的变革图景：AI组织就绪度
news.summaryZh: 在最新一期《法律领域的变革图景》节目中，Ari Kaplan与Caroline Hill回顾了ILTACON 2026的关键主题及更广泛的法律技术格局。生成式AI持续主导讨论，但双方认为行业已转向更成熟的讨论，聚焦实施、治理、技能发展和组织变革。人们进行的对话更加知情，能够流畅讨论可用技术、选择某工具的原因、试图捕捉的指标以及所应对的领导力挑战。一个反复出现的主题是技术转型依然困难。尽管律所对AI和法律技术的理解日益成熟，许多律所仍在变革管理、领导层支持、工作流整合和衡量成功方面挣扎。Kaplan观察到，法律技术专业人士如今在决策桌上拥有更具影响力的席位，但这种影响力取决于不仅参与技术讨论，还参与财务、数据、业务战略和组织变革的对话。双方还讨论了客户参与日益重要。律所不应假设客户需求，而有机会就服务交付、人员配置模式和技术角色与客户进行更直接、更具战略性的对话。客户对法律技术日益了解，期望律所智能运用技术，同时继续重视法律专业知识和判断力，而非任何特定工具组合。另一个关键要点是行业日益关注人才和能力发展。Hill强调与法律创新领导者的对话，内容涉及帮助律所构建长期技术能力，而非仅仅选择产品，包括随着技术重塑法律工作而重新思考培训、认证和职业发展。
news.bodyHtml:
In this latest episode of Charting Change in Legal, Ari Kaplan and Caroline Hill reflect on the key themes emerging from ILTACON 2026 and the broader legal technology landscape. While generative AI continues to dominate conversations, both agree that the industry has moved towards a more mature discussion centred on implementation, governance, skills development and organisational change.

“People are having much more informed conversations. They’re able to discuss with fluency the technology that’s available, the reasons they’ve chosen one tool over another, the metrics they’re trying to capture and the leadership challenges they’re answering to,” said Kaplan, a leading legal analyst.

Advertisement

A recurring theme was that technology transformation remains difficult. Although firms are becoming increasingly sophisticated in their understanding of AI and legal technology, many continue to wrestle with change management, leadership buy-in, workflow integration and measuring success. Kaplan observed that legal technology professionals now have a far more influential seat at the table, but that influence depends on engaging not just in technology discussions but also in conversations around finance, data, business strategy and organisational change.

The pair also discussed the growing importance of client engagement. Rather than making assumptions about what clients want, law firms have an opportunity to have more direct and strategic conversations with clients about service delivery, staffing models and the role of technology. Kaplan noted that clients are increasingly knowledgeable about legal technology and expect firms to use it intelligently, while continuing to value legal expertise and judgement above any particular suite of tools.

Advertisement

Another key takeaway was the industry’s growing focus on talent and capability development. Hill highlighted conversations with legal innovation leaders about helping firms build long-term technology capability rather than simply selecting products. This includes rethinking training, accreditation and professional development as technology reshapes legal work.

You can listen to this fun and informative chat on Spotify and YouTube below:

news.titleEn: Supreme Court judge McCormack joins Clio’s growing judiciary team
news.titleZh: 最高法院法官麦考马克加入Clio不断壮大的司法团队
news.summaryZh: 前密歇根州最高法院首席大法官布里奇特·玛丽·麦考马克以总经理（司法）身份加入Clio，从司法系统最高层进入法律科技领域，此举较为罕见。她将负责领导Clio在法院、司法官员及争议解决组织合作伙伴方面的增长，借助其对司法系统的深刻理解推动Clio的司法业务。她将与Casetext联合创始人巴勃罗·阿雷东多共事，后者上月从汤森路透加入Clio，担任高级副总裁（司法）。司法领域是改善法律体系运作的最大机遇之一，Clio正以长期雄心为此布局；麦考马克对该市场的理解鲜有人能及，她曾领导法院、在司法系统工作，深知如何赢得Clio希望服务的机构的信任。这是Clio更大愿景的一部分，旨在帮助塑造现代法律工作的基础设施，覆盖整个行业及支持它的机构。美国各地法院正以有限资源管理不断增长的案件量，每件事项仍需审慎考虑。麦考马克在密歇根州最高法院任职近十年，其中四年担任首席大法官，期间监督州法院系统并推动法院服务公众方式的现代化，亲眼目睹了这种压力。这段经历塑造了她对AI能在何处产生最大影响的看法。法院多年来在结构性压力下运作，技术如今让我们有机会重新思考支持可以是什么样子。
news.bodyHtml:
In a rare move from the highest levels of the judiciary into legal technology, former Michigan Supreme Court Chief Justice Bridget Mary McCormack has joined Clio as general manager, judiciary, strengthening the leadership team behind Clio’s expansion into the courts.

In her new role, McCormack will lead Clio’s growth across courts, judicial officers, and dispute resolution organisational partners, leveraging her deep understanding of the justice system to help Clio grow its judiciary business. She will be working alongside Casetext co-founder Pablo Arredondo, who joined Clio last month from Thomson Reuters as senior vice president, judiciary.

Advertisement

“The judiciary represents one of the largest opportunities to strengthen how the legal system works, and we are building for it with long term ambition,” said Jack Newton, CEO and founder of Clio. “Bridget understands this market at a level very few people do. She has led courts, worked across the justice system, and knows what it takes to earn the confidence of the institutions we want to serve. This is part of a much bigger vision for Clio to help shape the infrastructure of modern legal work, across the profession and the institutions that support it.”

Courts across the United States are managing growing caseloads with limited resources, and every matter still requires careful consideration. McCormack saw that pressure firsthand during nearly a decade on the Michigan Supreme Court, including four years as Chief Justice, where she oversaw the state court system and championed efforts to modernize how courts serve the public. That experience has shaped her view of where AI can have the greatest impact.

Advertisement

“Courts have been operating under structural pressure for years, and technology now gives us a chance to rethink what support can look like,” she said.
news.bodyText:
In a rare move from the highest levels of the judiciary into legal technology, former Michigan Supreme Court Chief Justice Bridget Mary McCormack has joined Clio as general manager, judiciary, strengthening the leadership team behind Clio’s expansion into the courts.

In her new role, McCormack will lead Clio’s growth across courts, judicial officers, and dispute resolution organisational partners, leveraging her deep understanding of the justice system to help Clio grow its judiciary business. She will be working alongside Casetext co-founder Pablo Arredondo, who joined Clio last month from Thomson Reuters as senior vice president, judiciary.

“The judiciary represents one of the largest opportunities to strengthen how the legal system works, and we are building for it with long term ambition,” said Jack Newton, CEO and founder of Clio. “Bridget understands this market at a level very few people do. She has led courts, worked across the justice system, and knows what it takes to earn the confidence of the institutions we want to serve. This is part of a much bigger vision for Clio to help shape the infrastructure of modern legal work, across the profession and the institutions that support it.”

Courts across the United States are managing growing caseloads with limited resources, and every matter still requires careful consideration. McCormack saw that pressure firsthand during nearly a decade on the Michigan Supreme Court, including four years as Chief Justice, where she oversaw the state court system and championed efforts to modernize how courts serve the public. That experience has shaped her view of where AI can have the greatest impact.

“Courts have been operating under structural pressure for years, and technology now gives us a chance to rethink what support can look like,” she said.

news.titleEn: Parker Poe Clients & Attorneys Build AI Assistants Together to Help Deliver Better Outcomes
news.titleZh: Parker Poe律师与客户携手共建AI助手，助力实现更优法律成果
news.summaryZh: 2026年9月10日，Parker Poe律师事务所在其夏洛特办公室举办了一场仅限受邀者参加的AI工作坊，总法律顾问、法务运营负责人、合规专业人士、企业高管及该所律师分组协作，共同构建并测试AI应用，以应对日常共同挑战。参与者以四至六人小组形式，利用Lega AI Builder Lab平台，探索AI模型、优化提示词并连接相关知识源。工作坊设公司研究、风险披露更新和高管法律简报三个方向，其中高管简报方向吸引了约90%的参与者，旨在将详细法律更新转化为企业领导者易于使用的信息，明确变化内容、对业务的重要性及所需决策或行动。工作坊注重实操，参与者从零开始设计可运行的AI助手，构建可重复、模板化的AI流程，这是将AI从使用推向运营化的桥梁。一位全球化学品公司高级IT主管开发了一款AI应用，通过询问行业、公司规模等数据为高管起草简报，并称该工作坊对构建提示词、比较不同AI模型响应及起草分级简报“超级有帮助”。该活动是Parker Poe“Moments That Matter™”客户体验项目的一部分，旨在强化信任、信心与长期客户关系。目标是将客户对业务的了解与该所法律判断及AI实际应用相结合，消除业务障碍。Lega创始人、现BARBRI创新主管Christian Lang主持活动并评选出三项优胜创新，Parker Poe将代表获胜团队向所选慈善机构捐赠奖金。Parker Poe是全美首批开展此类客户实验室的律所之一，此前与加拿大Fasken律所合作的类似项目案例在2026年SKILLS Law Showcase上荣获最具启发性展示观众奖。
news.bodyHtml:
Sept. 11, 2026 Charlotte, NC – General counsel, legal operations leaders, compliance professionals, business executives, and Parker Poe attorneys sat side by side on September 10 at the firm’s Charlotte office to build and test AI apps addressing challenges that company leaders and attorneys face together every day. Working in small teams, participants explored AI models, refined prompts, and connected relevant knowledge sources to develop practical tools designed to improve collaboration and legal outcomes.

Teams chose from three tracks: company research, risk disclosure updates, and executive legal briefings. The executive briefing track drew approximately 90% of the participants and focused on a common source of friction in the client relationship, translating detailed legal updates into information business leaders can readily use. Clients and attorneys worked together to build assistants that tailored updates on a commercial dispute to different executives, making clear what had changed, why it mattered to the business, and what decisions or actions were needed. The exercise reflected the workshop’s broader purpose, which was about creating a better client experience through the everyday interactions that may never appear on a legal bill but shape the attorney-client relationship, from clearer communication to anticipating what a client needs next.

“The workshop was hands-on and not just presentation slides,” said Zach Porfiris, who is head of legal at Symphonic Distribution, a global music distribution and technology company. “I teamed up with Parker Poe attorneys and other in-house counsel and business leaders to design working AI assistants from scratch. The practical skill goes beyond prompting. It’s building repeatable, templatized AI processes your team can run without you. That’s the bridge between using AI and operationalizing it.”

“I’m excited to bring ideas back to Symphonic as we expand AI-powered contract drafting and lifecycle management, operationalize legal workflows through AI, and develop frameworks considering AI-generated content across our global platform,” Zach added.

One senior IT leader of a global chemicals company who attended the event built an AI app that asks IT managers and directors what industry they belong to, the size of their company, and other relevant data in order to draft briefings for company executives. The workshop was a “super helpful” way to use AI to build the right prompts, compare how different AI models respond to those prompts, and then draft briefs for various levels of company executives so the information they would receive was relevant to them, the IT manager commented after the workshop.

The invitation-only workshop was part of the firm’s Moments That Matter™ client experience program. The program focuses on the interactions that most strongly shape trust, confidence, and long-term client relationships, and it helps create a more consistent and intentional client experience across the firm.

The event was intentionally created to make complex information easier to act on, surface risks sooner, and communicate more clearly, ultimately strengthening how clients and their lawyers work together, said Will Cannon, a Raleigh partner who leads Parker Poe’s Technology Industry Team and provided welcoming remarks for the event.

“Our clients know their businesses and the hurdles that slow their businesses down,” Will said. “Our goal is to combine that knowledge with our legal judgment and practical uses of AI to remove those obstacles. We’re working alongside our clients to build tools that make their work easier and help their businesses move faster.”

Using the Lega AI Builder Lab platform, participants collaborated in groups of four to six people. Christian Lang, the founder of Lega and now head of innovation at BARBRI (which recently acquired Lega), facilitated the event and selected three winning innovations.

“This is not a theoretical exercise,” Christian told the participants during the workshop. “Today we’re using these knowledge sources and data we created. Tomorrow we can be doing things that are directly plugging into your production and other systems. This is the kind of thing that I hope will start to inspire people about what’s possible and what we can do together.”

Parker Poe will donate the prize money for each winning team to a charity of their choice. The three winning teams presented their work informally during a cocktail reception that followed, with guests circulating between them.

Parker Poe is among the first firms in the country to run a client lab of this kind. A similar client AI lab with Fasken in Canada brought lawyers and clients together to build practical AI solutions, and the case study of Lega’s Client AI Lab with Fasken earned the Most Inspiring Showcase Audience Award at the 2026 SKILLS Law Showcase.

“This new technology and the ability to collaborate using AI is exciting because it allows us to provide a better work product for our clients,” said Russell Killen, a partner in the firm’s Raleigh office who leads the Technology Committee. “As lawyers, that’s our goal.”

“When used properly, AI provides lawyers and clients with a better basis for decision-making,” Russell added. “You can take the judgment and experience of a lawyer and the business needs of a client and now you’re able to use this tool to get to better decisions faster. That’s the real benefit of building AI tools together. You’re able to think through complicated problems in a more effective way. That’s good for the clients and the law firms.”

The most important thing to the client is not the technology, said Kristen Bateman Leis, Parker Poe’s chief marketing and business development officer. What they want is predictability, clearer communication, fewer surprises, and a team that knows their business well enough to see what is coming. The technology can help attorneys get to that better client experience and business outcome.

“The relationships that matter are not built at the closing table,” Kristen said. “They are built in the ordinary moments in between, and this was one of them. A client and their lawyer at the same table, building the same thing, deciding together what ‘better’ looks like. That is what the relationship is all about.”

About Parker Poe Adams & Bernstein LLP
Businesses and local governments turn to Parker Poe to structure transactions, navigate regulations, and resolve disputes. Founded in 1884, the Southeast business law firm today has approximately 300 attorneys across offices in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Washington, DC.

Parker Poe is a member of two leading international legal networks: TerraLex and the Employment Law Alliance. TerraLex and the ELA have chosen Parker Poe to help guide clients through the challenges of global business.
