news.titleZh: Paxton AI推出安全事项协作功能，为诉讼团队共享案件情报提供最先进方式
news.summaryZh:
Paxton AI于2026年7月17日宣布推出Secure Matter Collaboration，该功能使同一律所的多名律师能够安全地协作处理同一诉讼事项。团队可在共享的安全工作区内上传文件、构建案件时间线、审查证据，并起草简报、证据开示文件和庭审准备材料。该功能旨在解决诉讼中持续存在的运营挑战：随着案件推进，文件、时间线、研究和草稿往往分散在电子邮件、共享驱动器和个人工作区中，导致重复劳动、工作成果过时和不必要的风险。

该功能为加入事项的每位律师提供对相同案件文件和生成输出的即时访问，无需重新上传或转发附件。每位协作者使用个人账户登录，事项访问权限由律所集中管理并符合道德墙要求。功能包括：共享事项访问、单一工作区替代邮件链、个人账户与集中访问、审查而不覆盖、更快审批以及企业级安全，文档和数据不会用于训练Paxton的AI模型。目前支持医疗账单摘要、动议及其他生成物（包括时间线和案件草稿）的协作，更多协作功能在规划中。该功能现已向Paxton客户开放，完整文档可在Paxton网站获取。
news.bodyHtml:
This new collaboration feature lets multiple attorneys at a firm securely work the same case together — sharing files, chronologies, evidence, and drafts in one workspace instead of scattered email chains and duplicate uploads

San Francisco, California — July 17, 2026 — Paxton AI, the AI litigation platform for legal research, document drafting, and case analysis, today announced Secure Matter Collaboration, a new capability that enables multiple attorneys at the same firm to securely collaborate on a litigation matter. Teams can upload files, build case chronologies, review evidence, and draft briefs, discovery documents, and trial preparation materials – all within a shared, secure workspace.

The release addresses one of litigation’s most persistent operational challenges: keeping multiple attorneys aligned as a matter evolves. Files, chronologies, research, and drafts often become fragmented across email, shared drives, and individual workspaces, leading to duplicate effort, outdated work product, and unnecessary risk.

“Being able to collaborate using the same set of matter documents is a game changer,” said Ashley King Owner of Crown Discovery. “With other tools, attorneys may have to create separate workspaces and upload the same documents again. Paxton gives the entire team access to the same files and matter intelligence while still allowing each person to work independently. That is much closer to how litigation teams actually need to operate.”

 

Shared Access Respecting Ethical Walls

Secure Matter Collaboration gives every attorney added to a matter immediate access to the same case files and generated outputs — no re-uploading, no forwarding attachments, no waiting on whoever happens to hold the account. Each collaborator signs in under their own individual account, while access to the matter itself is managed centrally and in line with the firm’s ethical walls, eliminating the credential-sharing and duplicate-upload problems that slow teams down.

 

Key capabilities include:

  • Shared matter access. Every team member works from the same evidence, chronology, research, and case files — not separate copies that quietly drift apart.
  • One workspace instead of email chains. Uploading files, building chronologies, reviewing evidence, and drafting legal documents all happen directly in Paxton.• Individual accounts, centralized access. Attorneys use their own logins while matter-level access is managed by the firm, respecting ethical walls and removing the need to share credentials.
  • Review without overwriting. Teammates can review each other’s drafts and outputs without risk of overwriting one another’s work.
  • Faster approvals. Shared visibility into a matter’s current state means faster sign-off to file-ready output.
  • Enterprise-grade security. Collaboration is protected by enterprise-grade security, and documents and data are never used to train Paxton’s AI models.

 

The feature currently supports collaboration on medical billing summaries, motions, and other generated artifacts including chronologies and case drafts, with additional collaboration capabilities on the roadmap.

“Litigation is a team effort, but most legal AI software still treats a matter as though it belongs to one person,” said Tanguy Chau, Ph.D., CEO and Founder of Paxton AI. “We built Secure Matter Collaboration so every authorized member of a litigation team can work from the same files, chronologies, evidence, and work product without sharing credentials or recreating work. When the entire team has a common understanding of the matter, attorneys can move faster, collaborate more effectively, and reduce the risk of important information falling through the cracks.”

 

Availability

Secure Matter Collaboration is available now to Paxton customers. Full documentation is available on Paxton’s website.

 

About Paxton AI

Paxton AI is the AI platform built for Litigation teams, combining legal research, document drafting, and case analysis in one place. Paxton’s research tools surface on-point case law, statutes, and regulations at the state, federal, and appellate level, with a citation on every answer and an AI Citator that flags whether a case is still good law. Paxton is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA compliant, and customer data is never used to train its AI models. Learn more at www.paxton.ai.

 

Media Contact:

Dora Yun

650-392-2831

Dora@paxton.ai

news.summaryZh:
人身伤害索赔函是代表受伤客户协商和解的第一步正式程序，用于通知保险公司或过错方索赔事宜、陈述事故经过并说明客户所受损害的全部范围。一封有力的索赔函需包含以下关键要素：引言与目的、事故详情（日期、时间、地点、经过及警方报告引用、过错方身份）、伤情与医疗治疗（医疗记录摘要、费用明细及未来医疗费用预估）、损害分类（经济损失包括医疗账单、财产损失、误工费等；非经济损害包括精神痛苦、疼痛与折磨、生活乐趣丧失）、支持性证据（医疗记录与账单、警方报告、证人陈述、照片及事件时间线）以及具体的赔偿金额要求（分别列出经济与非经济损害总额并附证据依据）。

律师起草索赔函时应逻辑组织信息、简洁而全面、提供有力证据、保持专业语气、确保要求现实具体并以 certified mail 寄送。常见错误包括：未能确立明确责任、低估未来损害、遗漏证据、缺乏判例法支持。CloudLex 的人身伤害案件管理软件专为 PI 律所构建，其 Lexee AI 的 Demand Package Drafting 功能可从案件数据自动生成结构化索赔草稿，经 CloudLex Paralegal Services 人工审核后交付至案件档案，律师仅需审核与批准。CloudLex 与 Microsoft 365 的集成则允许律师在 Word 中直接调取案件数据完成索赔函。两种方式均旨在减少机械性数据收集与格式化时间，让律师专注于法律策略与案件判断。
news.bodyHtml:
Suffering an injury from an accident can be overwhelming — not just physically, but emotionally and financially. The stress of medical bills, lost income, and uncertainty about what comes next can make an already difficult situation even harder to navigate.

For personal injury attorneys, drafting a strong demand letter is one of the most consequential steps in securing fair compensation for a client. It sets the foundation for settlement negotiations, establishes the value of the claim, and signals to the insurance company that your firm is prepared to pursue the matter seriously. A well-structured demand letter doesn’t just outline damages — it makes a compelling case for why your client deserves to be made whole. This guide breaks down what goes into an effective demand letter, the mistakes to avoid, and how to draft one more effinciently — and includes a free, downloadable PI demand letter template you can use as a starting point.

What is the purpose of a personal injury demand letter?

A personal injury demand letter serves as the first formal step in negotiating a settlement on behalf of an injured client. It notifies the insurance company or at-fault party of the claim, presents the facts of the accident, and outlines the full scope of the damage your client has sustained.

A well-written letter frames the case persuasively, making clear that your client deserves compensation for both economic and non-economic damages. It also gives the insurance adjuster the information they need to evaluate the claim and formulate an initial settlement offer — which is why accuracy, completeness, and tone all matter from the first line.

Elements of a personal injury demand letter

A compelling demand letter must include the following key elements.

Introduction and purpose. Begin with a concise introduction that explains the document’s intent. Clearly state that the letter serves as a formal demand for compensation for damages and injuries resulting from the accident.

Details of the accident. Include a detailed account of the incident: the date, time, and location; a description of how it occurred, including references to any police report; and identification of the at-fault party and the actions that caused the injury.

Injuries and medical treatment. Provide a summary of the injuries sustained and the medical treatment received. This should include specific details drawn from medical records, a breakdown of expenses incurred (hospital bills, physical therapy, ongoing treatment), and projections for future medical costs related to injuries.

Damages breakdown. Separate damages into two categories. Economic damages cover medical bills, property damage, lost wages, and other tangible financial losses. Non-economic damages cover intangible harm — emotional distress, pain and suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

Supporting evidence. Attach all relevant documentation to substantiate the claim: copies of medical records and bills, the police report and witness statements, photos of injuries, property damage or the scene of the accident, and a chronological account of events from the incident to the client’s current status.

Specific demand for compensation. Conclude by clearly stating the monetary amount being requested, broken down into total economic and total non-economic damages, with justification tied directly to the attached evidence.

Tips for attorneys drafting a personal injury demand letter

Organize information logically. Frame the letter as a persuasive legal argument, not just a factual summary. Strategic organization of details builds a stronger case for maximum compensation.

Be concise but thorough. Include everything necessary without overloading the letter with repetition or tangential detail. A focused, well-structured letter is easier for adjusters to evaluate — and harder to dismiss.

Provide strong evidence. Every claim should be supported by documentation. Medical records, witness statements, police reports, and photos all strengthen your position and demonstrate the gravity of your client’s injuries.

Use a professional tone. Keep the letter formal and factual throughout. Emotional language or accusatory framing can undermine credibility. The focus should stay on the facts, the evidence, and the compensation being sought.

Be realistic and specific. Base the settlement demand on actual financial losses, documented expenses, and reasoned projections for non-economic damages. Calculations that are clearly grounded in evidence are far more persuasive — and harder to undercut — than inflated or vague figures.

Ensure proper delivery. Send the letter via certified mail with return receipt to confirm delivery. Proper documentation of delivery adds accountability and ensures the letter doesn’t go unacknowledged.

Common mistakes to avoid when drafting a demand letter

Failing to establish clear liability. Before detailing damages, the letter must make a strong liability argument. Weak or incomplete liability framing gives adjusters grounds to reduce or deny the claim outright.

Underestimating future damages. Don’t limit the demand to immediate medical expenses. Factor in future treatments, rehabilitation costs, and the potential for long-term impairment. Undervaluing future damages is one of the most common ways attorneys leave money on the table.

Omitting evidence. Missing documentation — a police report, a set of medical records, photos of the scene — can significantly weaken the case. Comprehensive, organized evidence is the backbone of a compelling demand.

Lack of case law or precedent. Referencing similar verdicts or settlements in your jurisdiction adds credibility to the demand amount. Relevant case law strengthens your negotiating position before the conversation with the adjuster even begins.

The role of personal injury attorneys in demand letters

Maximizing settlement potential. A well-crafted demand letter does more than communicate the facts of a claim — it sets the tone and trajectory for the entire negotiation. Attorneys who approach demand drafting strategically, not just administratively, tend to anchor negotiations at a stronger starting point.

Using legal expertise to justify damages. Attorneys bring a depth of knowledge in case valuation that no template can replicate. Ensuring that all economic and non-economic damages are properly accounted for, substantiated, and framed requires legal judgment — and its judgment that directly affects outcomes for clients.

For busy PI firms managing high case volumes, however, the gap between knowing what a strong demand letter requires and having the bandwidth to produce one from scratch on every case is real. That’s where the CloudLex’s personal injury case management software comes in. Unlike general-purpose legal software adapted for personal injury, CloudLex is built exclusively for PI firms. It connects case management, AI, and human paralegal support in one system, so the work of producing a demand doesn’t depend on stitching together separate tools or re-entering data the firm already has.

Leveraging CloudLex for demand letter efficiency

Demand drafting is one of the most time-intensive tasks in a personal injury practice. A single demand package can take hours — gathering facts from the case file, pulling medical records and bills, calculating damages, and assembling everything into a structured, professional document. Multiply that across a caseload of dozens or hundreds of active matters, and it becomes one of the most significant drains on attorney and paralegal time in the firm. CloudLex addresses this in two ways, depending on how your team works.

Lexee AI: From a conversation to a draft, inside your case

The newer — and more powerful — path is Lexee AI’s Demand Package Drafting capability, built directly into the CloudLex ecosystem.

The workflow starts with a simple request. An attorney or paralegal tells Lexee AI, inside the relevant matter in CloudLex, that a demand package is needed for the case. That’s it. Lexee AI identifies the matter, creates a tracked task with visible status stages — Requested, In Progress, Ready for Review — and pulls the case data already stored in CloudLex: incident details, treatment timeline, medical records, bills, lost-wage documentation, and other matter-specific information. From that data, Lexee AI assembles a structured demand draft. That draft is then reviewed by CloudLex Paralegal Services — the ecosystem’s human-led pillar, staffed by PI specialists with over a decade of experience. They check it for accuracy and structure before it’s delivered directly back into the case file in CloudLex. The result is a comprehensive demand draft built from AI speed and verified by human judgment.

When the draft is ready, the attorney is notified. What they receive isn’t a blank template with placeholders — it’s a structured foundation built from the actual facts of the case, with a liability narrative, medical summary, damages calculation, and exhibit checklist already in place. The attorney’s job at that point is to review, refine strategy and emphasis, and approve. The heavy lifting — gathering, organizing, and drafting from scratch — is already done.

A few things make this meaningfully different from using a standalone AI drafting tool. First, there’s no re-entry of case facts. The data Lexee AI uses is already in CloudLex because your team entered it as part of normal case management. Second, the draft lands in the matter — not in a separate tool that requires downloading and re-uploading to the case file. Third, the workflow is tracked, so at any point your team knows exactly where every demand request stands without having to ask for an update.

And critically, attorney oversight is built into the process by design. Lexee AI doesn’t send demands. It produces drafts for attorney review. The legal judgment, the final framing, the decision to send — that stays with the attorney, where it belongs.

CloudLex + Microsoft 365: For firms that live in Microsoft Word

For firms that prefer to draft and finalize demand letters in Microsoft Word, the CloudLex–Microsoft 365 integration provides a complementary path that preserves the workflow while eliminating the manual data-gathering step.

With the integration in place, attorneys and paralegals can work within a Word document and access CloudLex directly from it — pulling live matter details, client information, treatment records, and damages data into the document without switching between systems or re-entering information that already exists in the case file. The demand letter can then be finalized and sent from within that familiar Word environment.

This is particularly useful for firms that have established their own internal demand letter templates and want to retain that formatting and structure while still reducing the manual effort of populating each document from scratch. CloudLex pulls the data; the attorney controls the final document.

Two paths, one outcome

Whether your team works through Lexee AI’s guided drafting workflow or through the CloudLex–Microsoft 365 integration, the outcome is the same: less time spent on mechanical data-gathering and formatting, more time spent on the legal strategy and case-specific judgment that actually drives settlement outcomes.

Both capabilities are part of the broader CloudLex ecosystem — a platform built exclusively for personal injury law firms that bring together Platform, Lexee AI, and Paralegal Services to support every stage of the PI lifecycle. Demand drafting isn’t an isolated feature. It’s a piece of a connected system where the data your team enters from intake through active case management compounds in value across every workflow — including the demand that eventually goes out the door.

Every case is unique, and legal requirements vary by jurisdiction. We strongly recommend consulting with a qualified personal injury attorney before sending a demand letter. Use of this template does not establish an attorney-client relationship.

A compelling demand letter must include the following key elements.

Introduction and purpose. Begin with a concise introduction that explains the document’s intent. Clearly state that the letter serves as a formal demand for compensation for damages and injuries resulting from the accident.

Details of the accident. Include a detailed account of the incident: the date, time, and location; a description of how it occurred, including references to any police report; and identification of the at-fault party and the actions that caused the injury.

Injuries and medical treatment. Provide a summary of the injuries sustained and the medical treatment received. This should include specific details drawn from medical records, a breakdown of expenses incurred (hospital bills, physical therapy, ongoing treatment), and projections for future medical costs related to injuries.

Damages breakdown. Separate damages into two categories. Economic damages cover medical bills, property damage, lost wages, and other tangible financial losses. Non-economic damages cover intangible harm — emotional distress, pain and suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

Supporting evidence. Attach all relevant documentation to substantiate the claim: copies of medical records and bills, the police report and witness statements, photos of injuries, property damage or the scene of the accident, and a chronological account of events from the incident to the client’s current status.

Specific demand for compensation. Conclude by clearly stating the monetary amount being requested, broken down into total economic and total non-economic damages, with justification tied directly to the attached evidence.

Tips for attorneys drafting a personal injury demand letter

Organize information logically. Frame the letter as a persuasive legal argument, not just a factual summary. Strategic organization of details builds a stronger case for maximum compensation.

Be concise but thorough. Include everything necessary without overloading the letter with repetition or tangential detail. A focused, well-structured letter is easier for adjusters to evaluate — and harder to dismiss.

Provide strong evidence. Every claim should be supported by documentation. Medical records, witness statements, police reports, and photos all strengthen your position and demonstrate the gravity of your client’s injuries.

Use a professional tone. Keep the letter formal and factual throughout. Emotional language or accusatory framing can undermine credibility. The focus should stay on the facts, the evidence, and the compensation being sought.

Be realistic and specific. Base the settlement demand on actual financial losses, documented expenses, and reasoned projections for non-economic damages. Calculations that are clearly grounded in evidence are far more persuasive — and harder to undercut — than inflated or vague figures.

Ensure proper delivery. Send the letter via certified mail with return receipt to confirm delivery. Proper documentation of delivery adds accountability and ensures the letter doesn’t go unacknowledged.

Common mistakes to avoid when drafting a demand letter

Failing to establish clear liability. Before detailing damages, the letter must make a strong liability argument. Weak or incomplete liability framing gives adjusters grounds to reduce or deny the claim outright.

Underestimating future damages. Don’t limit the demand to immediate medical expenses. Factor in future treatments, rehabilitation costs, and the potential for long-term impairment. Undervaluing future damages is one of the most common ways attorneys leave money on the table.

Omitting evidence. Missing documentation — a police report, a set of medical records, photos of the scene — can significantly weaken the case. Comprehensive, organized evidence is the backbone of a compelling demand.

Lack of case law or precedent. Referencing similar verdicts or settlements in your jurisdiction adds credibility to the demand amount. Relevant case law strengthens your negotiating position before the conversation with the adjuster even begins.

The role of personal injury attorneys in demand letters

Maximizing settlement potential. A well-crafted demand letter does more than communicate the facts of a claim — it sets the tone and trajectory for the entire negotiation. Attorneys who approach demand drafting strategically, not just administratively, tend to anchor negotiations at a stronger starting point.

Using legal expertise to justify damages. Attorneys bring a depth of knowledge in case valuation that no template can replicate. Ensuring that all economic and non-economic damages are properly accounted for, substantiated, and framed requires legal judgment — and its judgment that directly affects outcomes for clients.

For busy PI firms managing high case volumes, however, the gap between knowing what a strong demand letter requires and having the bandwidth to produce one from scratch on every case is real. That’s where the CloudLex’s personal injury case management software comes in. Unlike general-purpose legal software adapted for personal injury, CloudLex is built exclusively for PI firms. It connects case management, AI, and human paralegal support in one system, so the work of producing a demand doesn’t depend on stitching together separate tools or re-entering data the firm already has.

Leveraging CloudLex for demand letter efficiency

Demand drafting is one of the most time-intensive tasks in a personal injury practice. A single demand package can take hours — gathering facts from the case file, pulling medical records and bills, calculating damages, and assembling everything into a structured, professional document. Multiply that across a caseload of dozens or hundreds of active matters, and it becomes one of the most significant drains on attorney and paralegal time in the firm. CloudLex addresses this in two ways, depending on how your team works.

Lexee AI: From a conversation to a draft, inside your case

The newer — and more powerful — path is Lexee AI’s Demand Package Drafting capability, built directly into the CloudLex ecosystem.

The workflow starts with a simple request. An attorney or paralegal tells Lexee AI , inside the relevant matter in CloudLex, that a demand package is needed for the case. That’s it. Lexee AI identifies the matter, creates a tracked task with visible status stages — Requested, In Progress, Ready for Review — and pulls the case data already stored in CloudLex: incident details, treatment timeline, medical records, bills, lost-wage documentation, and other matter-specific information. From that data, Lexee AI assembles a structured demand draft. That draft is then reviewed by CloudLex Paralegal Service s — the ecosystem’s human-led pillar, staffed by PI specialists with over a decade of experience. They check it for accuracy and structure before it’s delivered directly back into the case file in CloudLex. The result is a comprehensive demand draft built from AI speed and verified by human judgment.

When the draft is ready, the attorney is notified. What they receive isn’t a blank template with placeholders — it’s a structured foundation built from the actual facts of the case, with a liability narrative, medical summary, damages calculation, and exhibit checklist already in place. The attorney’s job at that point is to review, refine strategy and emphasis, and approve. The heavy lifting — gathering, organizing, and drafting from scratch — is already done.

A few things make this meaningfully different from using a standalone AI drafting tool. First, there’s no re-entry of case facts. The data Lexee AI uses is already in CloudLex because your team entered it as part of normal case management. Second, the draft lands in the matter — not in a separate tool that requires downloading and re-uploading to the case file. Third, the workflow is tracked, so at any point your team knows exactly where every demand request stands without having to ask for an update.

And critically, attorney oversight is built into the process by design. Lexee AI doesn’t send demands. It produces drafts for attorney review. The legal judgment, the final framing, the decision to send — that stays with the attorney, where it belongs.

CloudLex + Microsoft 365: For firms that live in Microsoft Word

For firms that prefer to draft and finalize demand letters in Microsoft Word, the CloudLex–Microsoft 365 integration provides a complementary path that preserves the workflow while eliminating the manual data-gathering step.

With the integration in place, attorneys and paralegals can work within a Word document and access CloudLex directly from it — pulling live matter details, client information, treatment records, and damages data into the document without switching between systems or re-entering information that already exists in the case file. The demand letter can then be finalized and sent from within that familiar Word environment.

This is particularly useful for firms that have established their own internal demand letter templates and want to retain that formatting and structure while still reducing the manual effort of populating each document from scratch. CloudLex pulls the data; the attorney controls the final document.

Whether your team works through Lexee AI’s guided drafting workflow or through the CloudLex–Microsoft 365 integration, the outcome is the same: less time spent on mechanical data-gathering and formatting, more time spent on the legal strategy and case-specific judgment that actually drives settlement outcomes.

Both capabilities are part of the broader CloudLex ecosystem — a platform built exclusively for personal injury law firms that bring together Platform, Lexee AI, and Paralegal Services to support every stage of the PI lifecycle. Demand drafting isn’t an isolated feature. It’s a piece of a connected system where the data your team enters from intake through active case management compounds in value across every workflow — including the demand that eventually goes out the door.

news.titleZh: 伊利诺伊州颁布《人工智能安全措施法案》
news.summaryZh: 2026年7月6日，伊利诺伊州州长JB·普利兹克签署《人工智能安全措施法案》，对先进人工智能模型开发者施加治理、透明度、审计和事件报告义务。该法案聚焦“前沿模型”，并将最多义务赋予年总收入超过5亿美元的“大型前沿开发者”。法案于2027年1月1日生效，许多实质性合规义务自2028年开始。法案适用于“前沿模型”开发者，即训练计算量超过特定阈值的基础模型开发者；“大型前沿开发者”指在前一日历年与关联公司合计年总收入超过5亿美元的前沿开发者。法案针对先进前沿AI模型开发者，而非典型AI用户或部署AI工具的公司。自2028年1月1日起，大型前沿开发者必须制定、实施、遵守并公开发布书面前沿AI框架，该框架须至少每年审查一次，重大变更须在30天内公开披露并说明修改理由。在部署新的或重大修改的前沿模型之前或之时，开发者必须发布透明度报告。大型前沿开发者承担额外披露义务。自2028年1月1日起（或成为大型前沿开发者后90天内），受涵盖公司必须聘请独立第三方进行年度合规审计，审计发现的高层摘要和经脱敏的审计报告须在收到后30天内公开发布，并提交给伊利诺伊州应急管理署和国土安全办公室及伊利诺伊州总检察长。法案设立了“关键安全事件”新类别。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! On July 6, 2026, Illinois Governor, JB Pritzker, signed the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act (the Act), imposing governance, transparency, audit, and incident-reporting obligations on developers of advanced AI models. The Act focuses on “frontier models” and places the most obligations on “large frontier developers” with annual gross revenues exceeding $500 million. The Act takes effect Jan. 1, 2027, with many substantive compliance obligations beginning in 2028. The Act applies to developers of “frontier models,” defined as foundation models trained above specified computational thresholds. A “large frontier developer” is a frontier developer that, together with its affiliates, generated more than $500 million in annual gross revenue during the preceding calendar year. The Act targets developers of advanced frontier AI models rather than typical AI users or companies that deploy AI tools. Beginning Jan. 1, 2028, large frontier developers must develop, implement, comply with, and publicly post a written Frontier AI Framework addressing: The framework must be reviewed at least annually, and material changes must be publicly disclosed within 30 days, along with a justification for the modification. Before, or at the time of, deployment of a new or substantially modified frontier model, developers must publish a transparency report containing: Large frontier developers face additional disclosure obligations and must summarize: Starting Jan. 1, 2028, (or within 90 days after becoming a large frontier developer), covered companies must retain an independent third party to conduct annual compliance audits. Among other requirements: A high-level summary of audit findings and a redacted audit report must be publicly posted and submitted to the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (the Agency) and the Illinois Attorney General within 30 days after receipt. 声明提出十五方面主张：培育以企业为主体、市场为牵引的创新生态并重视人才培养；推广“人工智能+”模式，培育词元经济新模式；以负责任方式鼓励共建开源生态；深化数据资源开发利用，保障数据安全和个人信息保护，构建数据产权等基础制度；推进人工智能与能源系统深度融合，推动绿色低碳发展；评估应对就业结构冲击，开展教育培训；构建法律法规、技术监测、风险预警、应急响应体系，探索分类分级管理；领先企业应为大模型加装必要护栏；明确智能体决策权限和行为边界，建立行为追溯和风险提示机制；共同防范打击恐怖主义等滥用恶用；践行真正的多边主义，发挥联合国核心作用，支持联合国全球人工智能治理对话、国际人工智能科学小组两项机制；探索构建人工智能国际经贸规则。
policy.bodyText:
新华社上海7月17日电
2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议主席声明
2026年7月17日至20日，2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议在中国上海举行。中华人民共和国主席习近平出席大会开幕式并发表主旨讲话。哈萨克斯坦总统托卡耶夫、柬埔寨首相洪玛奈、泰国总理阿努廷、联合国秘书长古特雷斯，以及来自100多个国家和国际组织的官方代表、产学研界嘉宾等出席大会。在新一轮智能浪潮席卷全球的重要历史节点，大会以“智能伙伴 共创未来”为主题，共同探讨如何促进全球人工智能向善普惠发展。
大会认为，人工智能全方位重构人类经济社会发展模式，将对人类文明进步产生深远影响。人工智能带来的机遇和挑战同步上升，一方面，人工智能深度融入产业、民生、科研等诸多领域，为经济转型、技术突破、效率提升注入强劲动能。另一方面，在人工智能持续迭代过程中，技术伦理、数据安全、监管体系等问题也随之凸显。
大会认为，人工智能是全球治理的最新课题，要秉持“同球共济”精神，通过人工智能国际协调为全球治理树立新范式。应当统筹发展和安全、平衡创新和治理、兼顾本国利益和全球福祉，坚持以人为本、智能向善、公平普惠、协同共治原则，加强人工智能国际合作，讨论和解决智能时代人类共同面对的重大问题、紧迫挑战，把人工智能能力建设国际合作置于人工智能全球治理的突出位置，着力解决资源分布不均、权力分配不公等突出问题，帮助全球南方国家在人工智能发展进程中平等受益，助力落实联合国2030年可持续发展议程，确保人工智能造福全人类。
一、创新是人工智能发展的核心驱动力。我们倡导培育以企业为主体、以市场为牵引、以应用为导向、以科研为基础、以人才为根本的创新生态。人在人工智能发展中发挥关键作用，要高度重视培养具备数字和人文素养、创新能力和全球视野的人工智能领域人才。
二、推动人工智能赋能千行百业、走进千家万户。人工智能具有鲜明赋能属性，应当积极推广“人工智能+”模式，激发全球创新活力，探索全新科研范式，打造智能经济新形态，培育以大模型为基础、智能体驱动为引领的词元经济新模式，协同推进传统产业的改造升级、新兴产业的培育壮大和未来产业的谋篇布局，推进人工智能在科学、教育、工业、农业、卫生、交通、气候、环境、政务等领域的应用。
三、开源开放是人工智能普惠发展的重要路径。应当以负责任的方式鼓励共建开源生态，积极打造开放包容的国际开源社区，尊重企业自主选择，在重视知识产权保护的前提下，促进人工智能研究成果和技术经验的分享，提升人工智能技术和服务的可及性。
四、数据在人工智能发展中发挥重要作用。应当把握数据高流动性、高赋能性特征，深化数据资源开发利用，切实保障数据安全，共同加强个人信息保护，加快构建数据产权等基础制度，确保数据可管、可控、可追溯，促进数据安全有序流动和高效开发利用。
五、发展可持续的人工智能，推进人工智能与能源系统的深度融合。通过在新能源富集地区布局规模化智算集群，引导算力负荷与电力资源的协调调度，关注人工智能对能源消耗和生态环境的影响，推动人工智能绿色低碳发展，促进人工智能与能源双向赋能。
六、关注人工智能技术对社会转型的影响，系统评估和应对人工智能对就业结构的冲击，发挥人工智能在创造就业岗位方面的潜能，积极开展人工智能教育和技能培训，激发全社会创新创业活力，切实维护劳动者的权利和尊严，构建更有温度的智能社会。
七、重视人工智能带来的安全风险，积极推动构建法律法规、技术监测、风险预警、应急响应体系，坚持风险导向、敏捷治理，探索分类分级管理，筑牢安全底线，防范滥用恶用，确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下。
八、人工智能前沿技术的升级迭代给网络安全带来复杂影响，对金融、电力、通信、交通等关键基础设施构成潜在威胁。全球领先的人工智能企业应以审慎态度推进人工智能研发，为人工智能大模型加装必要护栏，确保前沿模型的安全部署，防范人工智能带来系统性风险。
九、智能体是人工智能产品和服务的新形态，应当明确决策权限和行为边界，建立行为追溯和风险提示机制，着力提升智能体内生安全能力，化解应用衍生风险。
十、应当共同防范和打击恐怖主义、极端势力和跨国有组织犯罪集团对人工智能技术的滥用恶用，在国际上建立必要的危机管控和应急响应机制。
十一、应当践行真正的多边主义，发挥联合国在全球治理中的核心作用，重视人工智能全球治理碎片化问题，支持联合国全球人工智能治理对话、国际人工智能科学小组两项机制发挥作用，进一步凝聚全球共识、分享最佳实践，确保各国权利平等、机遇平等、规则平等。
十二、探索共同构建人工智能国际经贸规则，促进人工智能产业链供应链普惠合作，支持发展中国家更多参与全球分工，确保各国企业公平参与国际竞争，维护人工智能产业链供应链稳定。
十三、针对联合国可持续发展目标执行严重滞后的实际，应当持之以恒推进落实“加强人工智能能力建设国际合作”联大决议，结合发展中国家的实际需求开展务实合作，支持各国发掘自身潜力和独特优势，共享人工智能发展红利。
十四、加快安全、产业、伦理标准制修订，兼顾技术进步、风险防范、社会伦理，建立具有广泛共识、科学、透明、包容的标准规范框架，促进各国间标准互认，降低人工智能国际合作的成本和门槛。
十五、尊重各国历史文化、社会制度、文明形态差异，保护世界文化多样性。推动人工智能技术适配多元文化场景，促进各国文化的创造性转化和创新性发展，维护世界文明多样性和各国文化独特性。
大会期间，《关于成立世界人工智能合作组织的协定》签署仪式在上海举行。世界人工智能合作组织是全球首个人工智能政府间国际组织，总部将设在上海。世界人工智能合作组织坚持向善普惠原则，旨在支持全球南方国家加快人工智能发展，提升创新、应用、治理综合能力，追赶科技革命浪潮，弥合智能鸿沟。世界人工智能合作组织的基本原则是遵循《联合国宪章》宗旨和原则，尊重各国主权和文明多样性，坚持平等相待，践行多边主义，秉持共商共建共享理念，实现互利共赢。世界人工智能合作组织向所有国家开放，并将同其他国际组织保持沟通，探讨适当的合作形式。

policy.bodyText:
7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。新华社记者 黄敬文 摄
新华社上海7月17日电（记者王永前、杨依军）7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。
黄浦江畔，潮启新澜。世界会客厅内嘉宾云集。
7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。这是习近平同与会的国家元首、政府首脑、国际组织负责人及各国代表团团长集体合影。新华社记者 殷博古 摄
习近平同与会的国家元首、政府首脑、国际组织负责人及各国代表团团长集体合影。
在热烈的掌声中，习近平发表题为《携手构建公正合理的全球人工智能治理体系》的主旨讲话。
7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。新华社记者 申宏 摄
习近平指出，当前，世界百年变局加速演进，新一轮科技革命和产业变革加速突破，全球人工智能技术创新进入前所未有的活跃期，既蕴含巨大机遇，也面临治理挑战。人类不得不直面时代之问：当机器开始思考，人类如何与之相处？当算法参与决策，安全如何保障？当技术挑战伦理，治理如何跟上？当鸿沟不断拉大，普惠如何实现？中方认为，各国应当秉持以人为本、向上向善理念，让人工智能成为促进共同繁荣、维护共同安全的一个重要动力源，携手构建公正合理的全球人工智能治理体系。
习近平就此提出4点意见：
第一，坚持开放共赢，驱动创新发展。抓住难得的历史性机遇，鼓励开源开放、合作共享，全面促进人工智能科技创新、产业发展、场景应用，协同推进传统产业改造升级、新兴产业培育壮大、未来产业前瞻布局，让人工智能赋能千行百业。
第二，强化风险意识，确保安全可控。高度重视人工智能引发的各类内生和衍生风险，推动构建法律法规、技术监测、风险预警、应急响应体系，筑牢安全底线，防范滥用恶用，确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下。共同反对在人工智能领域泛化国家安全概念、把本国安全凌驾于他国安全之上的做法。
第三，鼓励包容并蓄，促进文明互鉴。用全人类共同价值塑造人工智能的价值观，善用人工智能技术增进不同文明的理解和包容，促进不同文明交流互鉴，精心培育各美其美、美美与共的文明百花园。
第四，倡导和衷共济，完善全球治理。践行真正的多边主义，切实发挥联合国的重要作用，加强人工智能发展战略、治理规则、技术标准的对接协调，早日形成具有广泛共识的全球治理框架，让这一前沿技术更好造福人类社会。帮助全球南方国家加强能力建设，弥合数智鸿沟，促进可持续发展，避免在人工智能领域造成新的历史不公。
7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。新华社记者 谢环驰 摄
习近平强调，今年是中国“十五五”开局之年。“十五五”规划为未来5年中国经济社会发展擘画蓝图，也为国际社会提供机遇清单。近年来，中国坚持有效市场和有为政府相结合，加强人工智能科技创新，积极推进“人工智能+”行动，培育各类主体共生共荣的健康生态，智能经济核心产业规模已经超过万亿元人民币，“中国智造”已成为中国式现代化的又一亮丽名片。同时，中国坚持发展和安全并重，不断完善相关法律法规、政策制度、应用规范、伦理准则，确保人工智能安全、可靠、可控。作为负责任大国，中国在人工智能领域始终致力于做国际公共产品的提供者，源源不断贡献中国方案。
习近平指出，在各方共同努力下，世界人工智能合作组织在上海应运而生。这是中方响应全球南方呼声、团结国际社会积极推动人工智能发展和治理的重大举措，将成为人工智能发展史上的一个重要里程碑。为进一步支持全球人工智能发展、推进全球人工智能能力建设，未来5年，中国将面向发展中国家提供5000个人工智能专题研修培训名额；面向东盟、阿盟、非盟、拉共体、上合组织、金砖国家建设国际人工智能应用合作中心；推动气象智能预警方案“妈祖”在30个国家落地应用。中国愿以更加开放的姿态、更加务实的行动、更加长远的目光，同各方一道把握和应对人工智能发展的机遇和挑战，携手共创人类社会更加美好的未来。
哈萨克斯坦总统托卡耶夫、柬埔寨首相洪玛奈、泰国总理阿努廷、联合国秘书长古特雷斯分别致辞。他们热烈祝贺世界人工智能合作组织协定签署仪式在上海举行，高度评价中国为推动人工智能全球治理作出的重要贡献，积极呼应习近平主席提出的倡议和举措。各方表示，人工智能有望成为人类最大的发展机遇，也潜藏着风险。中国倡导智能向善、普惠包容、安全可控，积极帮助发展中国家加强相关能力建设，推动人工智能国际合作，彰显了负责任的大国担当。人工智能技术应由各国共享共治，使其公平惠及所有国家，服务全人类可持续发展，消弭全球数智鸿沟和南北发展差距。人工智能带来的机遇与挑战跨越国界，需要各方携手合作把握和应对。希望并相信世界人工智能合作组织将为此发挥重要作用，通过开放包容、平等互惠的合作，共同打造安全、繁荣、不让任何国家掉队的美好未来。
大会发表《2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议主席声明》。
7月17日上午，国家主席习近平在上海世界会客厅出席2026世界人工智能大会暨人工智能全球治理高级别会议开幕式并发表主旨讲话。这是7月16日晚，习近平和夫人彭丽媛在世界会客厅为与会国际贵宾举行欢迎宴会。新华社记者 王晔 摄
7月16日晚，习近平和夫人彭丽媛在世界会客厅为与会国际贵宾举行欢迎宴会。
蔡奇、丁薛祥、王毅等出席上述活动。
陈吉宁主持开幕式。

news.titleEn: Intapp Makes Celeste Generally Available, Calling It An ‘AI Coworker’ To Run the Business Side of Law Firms
news.titleZh: Intapp 正式发布 Celeste，称其为管理律所业务运营的“AI 同事”
news.summaryZh: Intapp 宣布其代理式 AI 产品 Celeste 正式可用，该产品被描述为“专家级 AI 同事”，旨在运行律所的业务运营，涵盖交易筛选、利益冲突清理、业务拓展和横向招聘。此次发布距 Intapp 在纽约年度产品活动上首次预览 Celeste 约五个月，期间 Celeste 已在包括律所 BakerHostetler 和私募股权公司 Hg 在内的早期采用者中限量发布。Intapp 将 Celeste 定位为“律所 AI”，区别于通用助手和执业 AI，专注于律所运营侧，如案源开发、受理、冲突、定价和招聘。Celeste 自主运行，执行设计为剧本的多步骤工作流，附带覆盖案源开发、业务拓展、受理、冲突、定价、募资和横向招聘的剧本库，以及无代码构建器。产品与律所记录系统原生集成，可摄取律所文档并通过开放连接器连接外部数据合作伙伴。在治理方面，Intapp 表示适用于律所人员的道德墙、需知限制和审计要求同样适用于 Celeste。Intapp 此前宣布与 Harvey 合作，使 Celeste 能调用 Harvey 的执业工作流，同时执行合规和道德墙标准；并与 Anthropic 合作，将其 Claude 模型引入 Intapp 的治理环境。对于律所，Celeste 可在几分钟内而非几小时内呈现相关事项、合伙人经验和过往推介材料，并能运行端到端的横向招聘生命周期。BakerHostetler 的关注点一直是受理和冲突，其首席信息官 Katherine Lowry 表示相信 Celeste 能对受理和冲突流程产生积极影响，并帮助律所更高效运营。在 Hg，吸引力在于 AI 基于律所自身积累的知识工作，数据与平台战略负责人 Shirin Veeran 表示，Celeste 根据实际投资授权进行筛选，利用律所二十年积累的知识。Intapp 并非唯一寻求在法律 AI 业务侧占据一席之地的公司，但凭借二十年来嵌入记录系统。
news.bodyHtml:
Intapp, the publicly traded company whose software manages intake, conflicts, and deal workflows for law firms and other professional services firms, yesterday announced the general availability of Celeste, an agentic AI product it describes as an “expert AI coworker” designed to run the business operations of a firm — from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring.

The launch, announced during a global broadcast event, comes roughly five months after Intapp first previewed Celeste at its annual product event in New York in February, where the company described it as a purpose-built agentic AI platform for professional firms in regulated industries.

Since then, Celeste has been in limited release with early-adopter firms, including the law firm BakerHostetler and the private equity firm Hg.

For the Business, Not the Practice, of Law

With Celeste, Intapp is targeting what it sees as a gap in legal AI. While most firms now have AI assistants on every desk, drafting and reviewing faster than ever, that AI is built for the individual practitioner. It speeds up the practice of law without speeding up the business behind it.

Intapp’s answer to that gap is what it is branding “Firm AI,” a category it distinguishes from horizontal assistants (general-purpose tools for everyday tasks) and practice AI (tools that help produce the legal work product itself). Firm AI is aimed at the operational side of the firm, functions such as origination, intake, conflicts, pricing and hiring.

“Firms will run several kinds of AI: horizontal assistants for everyday work, practice AI for the work product, and Firm AI for the business of the firm itself,” said Thad Jampol, Intapp’s co-founder and chief product officer, in a statement. “That last category is the hard one, and it’s the one almost nobody is building.”

“When a conflicts team can clear 10 times the matters and a fund can screen 10 times the deals, that’s not saved time — that’s a new business model,” he said.

(Jampol lays out more of his thinking on this in A Blueprint for Firm AI, co-authored with Intapp’s chairman and CEO John Hall.)

Executing Multi-Step Workflows

According to Intapp, Celeste operates autonomously rather than waiting to be prompted, executing multi-step workflows designed as playbooks. It ships with a library of playbooks covering origination, business development, intake, conflicts, pricing, fundraising and lateral hiring, along with a no-code builder that lets firms create their own.

“Celeste encodes the firm’s own methods as playbooks — multi-step workflows that automate the firm’s best practices,” the company says.

The product is natively integrated with a firm’s systems of record — which makes sense given that Intapp’s applications already sit atop the intake, conflicts and relationship data of many large firms — andit  can ingest the firm’s documents and connect to outside data partners through open connectors.

On the governance front, Intapp says the same ethical walls, need-to-know restrictions, and audit requirements that apply to a firm’s people apply equally to Celeste. Restricted information stays restricted regardless of who asks, and firms can produce a full record of every action the AI takes for clients and regulators.

Intapp had previously announced a partnership with Harvey, allowing Celeste to invoke Harvey’s practice-of-law workflows while enforcing compliance and ethical wall standards. It similarly announced a partnership with Anthropic to bring its Claude models into Intapp’s governed environment.

Feedback from Early Adopters

For law firms specifically, Intapp says Celeste can surface relevant matters, partner experience, and prior pitch materials in response to an urgent client request in minutes rather than hours, and can run an end-to-end lateral hiring lifecycle, from candidate research and conflicts pre-screening through clearance preparation and onboarding.

At BakerHostetler, the focus so far has been on intake and conflicts. according to Katherine Lowry, the firm’s chief information officer and head of its IncuBaker innovation team.

“We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process,” she said in a statement provided by Intapp, adding that the firm’s substantial lateral growth in recent years has brought a significant volume of new clients and complex engagements. “We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.”

At Hg, the appeal is that the AI works from the firm’s own accumulated knowledge. “The intelligence is ours, not something generic applied to our firm,” said Shirin Veeran, who leads data and platform strategy at Hg, in a statement. “Celeste screens against our actual mandate, drawing on knowledge we have built across the firm over two decades.”

My Take

Intapp is not alone in seeking to stake a claim on the business side of legal AI — territory that Harvey, CoCounsel, and the rest of the practice-focused AI products are not directly contesting.

And it is, unquestionably, an area where the potential impact of AI could be significant. Large-firm workflows such as conflicts clearance, intake, lateral hiring, and others often remain highly inefficient, with process improvement hindered by the proprietary nature of firm data.

This is an area in which Intapp has the advantage of incumbency. It has spent two decades embedding itself in the systems of record where that data lives, and that makes it a natural home for AI that acts on that data.

news.summaryZh: 家庭法AI是帮助律师及法律人员自动化并提升离婚、监护、抚养等事务效率的工具，可减少行政负担、提高工作流效率并强化案件结果。常见应用包括文件起草、客户沟通、计费和案件受理，如生成诉状或协议草稿、总结案件文件、整理财务披露、起草客户更新、简化受理问卷及自动化客户入职，从而让律师专注于策略、谈判和客户咨询。AI用于处理文件起草、分析、客户受理、日程安排、沟通和计费等高频任务。文件起草方面，律师约40%至60%的时间用于起草，Clio Draft可自动化创建；法律研究方面，Clio Work结合研究、分析和起草；客户沟通方面，AI协助起草常规更新和常见问题回复；计费方面，Manage AI提供可靠的工作流；客户受理方面，AI表单和筛查缩短从首次联系到委托的时间。选择工具需考虑实践领域覆盖和司法准确性、数据安全与保密标准（如SOC 2 Type II）、与现有实践管理软件的集成、团队易采用性以及平台集成与独立工具。通用AI工具如ChatGPT和Gemini并非为法律工作设计，缺乏判例法训练、司法特定性和隐私保护。Clio报告显示，57%的独资律所和55%的小型律所没有正式AI政策。伦理方面，律师须遵守ABA模型规则1.1的胜任义务并监督AI工具，输出需由律师审查验证，符合规则5.1和5.3，并防范幻觉风险，检查AI辅助研究。保密是核心义务，避免将客户信息输入通用AI工具。律师协会和州监管机构正在发布AI使用指南。AI不会取代家庭法律师，实践仍依赖法律判断、谈判和客户咨询。
news.bodyHtml:
How is AI used in family law?

AI in family law streamlines high-volume tasks like document drafting, document analysis, client intake, scheduling calendar events, client communication, and billing. This helps attorneys reduce administrative workload and improve consistency, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, where judgment and empathy are essential.
news.bodyText: What is family law AI? Family law AI refers to artificial intelligence tools designed to help attorneys and legal staff automate, accelerate, and enhance work across divorce, custody, support, and related matters. These tools support solo practitioners and small to mid-sized firms alike by reducing administrative overhead, boosting workflow productivity, and strengthening case outcomes. Common applications of AI tools for family lawyers include document drafting, client communication, billing, and intake. In practice, this may involve generating drafts of pleadings or agreements, summarizing case files, organizing financial disclosures, drafting client updates, streamlining intake questionnaires, and automating client onboarding. By alleviating the burden of repetitive and administrative tasks, AI enables family lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, areas where legal judgment and human understanding are essential. How is AI used in family law? AI in family law streamlines high-volume tasks like document drafting, document analysis, client intake, scheduling calendar events, client communication, and billing. This helps attorneys reduce administrative workload and improve consistency, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, where judgment and empathy are essential. Key use cases for AI in family law practice AI tools for family law attorneys can be especially impactful in the day-to-day tasks that consume significant lawyer time and shape the client experience. Document drafting According to recent survey data , lawyers spend roughly 40% to 60% of their time drafting documents. Family lawyers in particular draft divorce petitions, custody agreements, parenting plans, and settlement letters, often under tight deadlines. Much of this work is repetitive and involves high document volume, making efficiency gains especially valuable in family law practice. Built into broader practice management workflows, Clio Draft helps firms automate document creation and generate routine family law documents more efficiently, without constant switching between disconnected tools. Legal research AI can help family lawyers analyze case law, interpret legislation, identify relevant precedents, and quickly get up to speed on unfamiliar issues. Tools grounded in authoritative legal sources generally provide greater accuracy and jurisdictional relevance than general-purpose AI systems. Built specifically for legal work, Clio Work combines legal research , analysis, and drafting in a single workspace. It helps lawyers uncover relevant authority, assess how it applies to the facts of a matter, and produce work product they can stand behind. Client communication Family law clients benefit from frequent communication. Because family law matters are highly personal and emotionally sensitive, tone and messaging are crucial, and lawyers must remain thoughtful, empathetic, and appropriate. AI can support the client-lawyer relationship by assisting with drafting routine updates, intake confirmations, and responses to common questions, improving both speed and consistency. To learn how AI-assisted client communication can help you gain a competitive advantage, see Clio’s guide to AI for client communication . Billing and time tracking Family law matters generate significant administrative work, making accurate billing and time capture a persistent challenge. AI-assisted billing can help reduce write-offs, record more billable time, and streamline administrative tasks. Integrated tools like Manage AI create reliable timekeeping and billing workflows. Client intake AI-powered intake forms and screenings can shorten the time between your first contact with a prospective client and the engagement process. This is especially valuable in family law, where firms handle high volumes of inquiries from individuals navigating urgent, emotionally charged situations. Across these use cases, AI helps reduce administrative friction and support more consistent, responsive client service. This allows firms to deliver higher quality legal services and achieve stronger outcomes for their clients. Be the first to see where legal is headed Sign up now to get the Legal Trends Report in your inbox the moment it drops, and you’ll be automatically entered to win a one-hour strategy session. Join the waitlist How to choose the right AI tool for your family law firm The job of evaluating AI tools for family law firms might fall to lawyers, paralegals , or support staff. It requires balancing speed and efficiency with confidentiality, accuracy, and workflow fit. Key criteria to consider include: Practice area coverage and jurisdictional accuracy Look for tools trained on legal data, ideally with family law use cases and jurisdiction-specific awareness. Note that general-purpose AI tools often lack reliable case law grounding and can produce inaccurate outputs. Data security and client confidentiality standards Client data in family law is highly sensitive. Prioritize tools with strong security certifications ( such as SOC 2 Type II ), clear data retention policies, and explicit commitments not to use client data for model training. Integration with existing practice management software AI for family lawyers delivers the most value when it fits into existing workflows rather than operating in isolation. Integration with your practice management system reduces the risk of duplicated work and constant context switching, and keeps client data centralized and organized. Ease of adoption across the team AI tools should be intuitive enough for lawyers and support staff to adopt quickly. Complex interfaces or fragmented workflows can slow adoption and reduce ROI . This matters especially in legal environments, where professionals are often time-constrained and resistant to tools that disrupt established billing and matter management routines. Platform integration vs. standalone tools Standalone AI tools can offer flexibility but often require more manual work. By contrast, AI that’s built into a broader platform provides stronger continuity across intake, matter management, billing, and communication. It’s worth emphasizing that general-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini are not designed for legal work. They typically lack case law training, jurisdictional specificity, and the privacy protections required for handling sensitive client information. These limitations are especially important in family law practice. According to Clio’s latest Legal Trends Report for Solo and Small Firms , 57% of solo firms and 55% of small firms have no formal AI policy in place. Without clear guidelines, staff can easily default to public tools and paste sensitive client information directly into them, creating real risks around confidentiality and malpractice. When evaluating purpose-built legal AI platforms, look for SOC 2 Type II compliance, a commitment to never training on client data, and direct integration into your existing practice management workflow. Clio’s AI tools meet all of these criteria and are directly integrated into the broader practice management platform already in use. The result is stronger security, consistency, and overall workflow efficiency. Explore Clio’s family law software to learn how it enables secure and efficient management of family law matters. AI ethics and professional responsibility in family law Ethics and professional responsibility are central to family law practice. First and foremost, attorneys must meet their duty of competence under ABA Model Rule 1.1 , which includes understanding and supervising any AI tools they use. AI systems can support drafting and research, but their outputs should always be reviewed and verified by a lawyer . This is required by ABA Model Rules 5.1 and 5.3 . Another concern is the risk of hallucinations , including inaccurate or entirely fabricated citations and legal propositions. This reinforces the need to check all AI-assisted research against primary sources before relying on it in legal advice or court filings. Legal-specific tools such as Clio Work ￼ help reduce this concern by grounding outputs in verified legal data sources. Confidentiality is also a core ethical obligation in family law, where matters often involve highly sensitive personal information. Attorneys should avoid entering confidential client details into general-purpose AI tools that may not offer sufficient data privacy protections or clear limits on how data is stored or used for model training. Amid the rapid expansion of AI tools, bar associations, including the ABA, along with various state regulators, are actively issuing guidance on AI use . Lawyers have an ongoing obligation to stay current as professional responsibility standards continue to evolve alongside the technology. Will AI replace family lawyers? No. While AI automates parts of legal work, family law practice still relies heavily on legal judgment, negotiation, and client counseling, all of which require human expertise and complex decision-making. What are the best AI tools for family law? Adoption of AI is already widespread, especially across small firms. Clio’s 2026 Legal Trends for Solo and Small Law Firms shows that 71% of solo practitioners and 75% of small firms now use AI, with lawyers reporting higher quality work, less time spent on tedious tasks, faster client response times, and lower stress levels. Those gains are most pronounced when AI is embedded within platform-based systems that connect intake, document drafting, research, and billing in a single workflow. Clio’s integrated AI suite includes multiple functions across practice management: Manage AI for communication, billing and task management; Clio Work for legal research and drafting strategy; and Clio Draft for automating document creation and standardizing frequently used forms and agreements. Some firms supplement their practice management platform with standalone tools for specific tasks like legal research, drafting support, or brainstorming. These tools can add value, but their impact tends to be limited to individual tasks. To truly transform how your practice operates, AI needs to be woven into the workflows you already use, rather than scattered across separate tools. For a broader overview of how AI tools fit into legal workflows, see Clio’s AI tools for lawyers resource page. What is the best AI for family law? There is no single “best” AI for family law firms, but the most effective approach is to combine a legal practice management platform with integrated AI tools designed specifically for legal workflows, rather than relying on standalone general-purpose systems. AI is already changing family law. Here’s your next step. The field of family law is far from static. From “grey divorce” to the rise of self-represented litigants (now reportedly accounting for 72% of family law cases ), family law continues to evolve with the times. AI is further reshaping practice by streamlining intake, improving drafting and research workflows, and reducing the administrative burden that often consumes attorneys’ time. Despite the pace of change, the attorney remains in the driver’s seat, with AI serving as an assistive tool rather than a replacement. Family law depends on judgment, empathy, and trust. These elements cannot be automated and remain integral to the attorney-client relationship. Firms that adopt AI tools early are already delivering a faster, more consistent experience while improving operational performance. Family law will always be a fundamentally human area of practice. Now, with the aid of AI technology, lawyers can redirect their attention toward what matters most: the people they serve. Discover how family law firms use Clio to streamline intake, drafting, billing, and day-to-day practice management. Ready to take the next step? news.titleEn: Xperate appoints first marketing head
news.titleZh: Xperate任命首位市场主管
news.summaryZh: 全球法律软件开发专业公司Xperate任命Hannah Perryman为其首位专职市场主管，以支持公司在现有及新兴市场的扩张，并专注于建立合作伙伴关系。Xperate由首席执行官Simon Hill和首席运营官Mark Garnish于2021年10月创立，两人此前均曾领导Tikit。这家英国公司依靠自有资金发展，营业额每年增长50%，在印度拥有大量人才，正进入下一增长阶段，计划拓展南美、中东和东南亚市场。该公司约有160名员工，目标是在五年内实现5000万英镑年收入。随着公司接近五周年，Xperate设立了这一新的高级市场职位以支持下一阶段战略增长。Perryman将领导Xperate在所有地区的市场战略制定与执行。她此前在营销机构Consortium工作，管理包括Xperate在内的专业服务客户。Xperate已发展到需要全职人员的阶段，将制定新战略以启动第五年，并指出合作伙伴关系是关键，将致力于提升全球品牌认知度。Xperate的市场与人力资源经理Becky Patterson此前承担了非常广泛的职责，随着公司发展，她将更专注于人力资源和董事支持。Xperate品牌今天的实力是四年专注、努力和真正致力于为法律行业交付价值的结果；随着业务持续发展，公司认识到需要专职市场领导来推动下一阶段增长。Hannah的任命是一项重要的战略举措，她带来了市场专业知识、商业洞察力和活力，相信她将在公司继续扩大影响力、进入新市场并进一步巩固在法律行业地位的过程中产生重大影响。
news.bodyHtml:
Global legal software development specialist Xperate has appointed Hannah Perryman as its first dedicated head of marketing, as it expands its presence across existing and emerging markets and focuses on building its partnerships.

Xperate was founded in October 2021 by CEO Simon Hill and chief operating officer Mark Garnish, who both previously headed Tikit. The UK-founded company, which is bootstrapped and has grown in turnover by 50% a year, has a substantial talent pool in India and is entering its next phase of growth, with plans to expand into South America, the Middle East and South-East Asia. We wrote in October that it has around 160 people and is targeting £50m annual revenue within five years.

Advertisement

With the business now approaching its fifth anniversary, Xperate has created this new senior marketing role to support the next phase of strategic growth.

Perryman will lead the development and execution of Xperate’s marketing strategy across all regions. She previously worked for marketing agency Consortium, managing professional services customers including Xperate. Speaking to Legal IT Insider, Perryman said: “Xperate has got to the stage that they now need a full time person. We’ll be creating a new strategy to kick start our fifth year.” She added: “Partnerships are key and we’ll be looking at increasing global brand recognition.”

Advertisement

Xperate’s marketing and HR manager Becky Patterson has held a very wide role, and as Xperate has grown, will focus more on HR and director support going forward.

Hill said: “The strength of the Xperate brand today is the result of four years of focus, hard work and a real commitment to delivering value to the legal sector. As our business continues to evolve, we recognised the need for dedicated marketing leadership to help drive the next stage of growth. Hannah’s appointment is an important strategic move for the business. She brings a strong blend of marketing expertise, commercial insight and energy; as a result we believe she will make a significant impact as we continue to expand our presence, enter new markets and further strengthen our position within the legal sector.”

news.titleEn: LawSites – Intapp Makes Celeste Generally Available, Calling It An ‘AI Coworker’ To Run the Business Side of Law Firms
news.titleZh: LawSites：Intapp 将 Celeste 全面上市，称其为运营律所业务端的‘AI 同事’
news.summaryZh: 记者兼律师 Bob Ambrogi 发表文章，报道 Intapp 公司旗下产品 Celeste 正式全面上市。Celeste 是一款代理式 AI 同事，旨在协助律所处理业务端事务，涵盖交易筛查、利益冲突排查、业务拓展以及横向招聘等环节。Celeste 能够以剧本形式执行多步骤工作流程，在律所自身的道德边界和审计要求范围内运作，并依托律所的系统记录。文章还提及早期采用者的反馈，包括 BakerHostetler 和 Hg 两家机构。该报道由 LawSites 于 2026 年 7 月 16 日发布，标题为《Intapp Makes Celeste Generally Available, Calling It An ‘AI Coworker’ To Run the Business Side of Law Firms》。
news.bodyHtml:
Journalist and lawyer Bob Ambrogi published an article on the general availability of Intapp Celeste, an agentic AI coworker built to run the business side of a firm — from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring. His article covers how Celeste executes multi-step workflows as playbooks, operates within a firm’s own ethical walls and audit requirements, and draws on the firm’s systems of record, along with early feedback from adopters including BakerHostetler and Hg.

news.titleEn: Relativity President Chris Brown on the Gavel Acquisition, Opening Up to Claude, and the ‘Gangbusters’ Growth of aiR
news.titleZh: Relativity总裁Chris Brown谈收购Gavel、向Claude开放平台及aiR的‘迅猛’增长
news.summaryZh: Relativity上周宣布，自2018年起担任首席产品官的Chris Brown被任命为公司总裁，任命于7月13日生效。在新职位上，Brown继续领导产品组织，同时将市场营销和技术合作纳入其职责范围。这一变动恰逢首席营销官Cristina Rossman在任职六年多后离职。此次任命之际，这家法律数据智能公司正进行一系列重要举措，包括6月收购由Dorna Moini创立的文档自动化公司Gavel，以及推出受治理的MCP集成，使Claude等AI助手能够在RelativityOne中编排事务和工作流程。周二，在Brown正式上任一天后，作者与他进行了对话，讨论将产品和营销合并于一位领导者之下的考量、收购Gavel的理由、Relativity向通用AI助手开放的原因、其aiR产品的采用轨迹，以及他在Orbitz构建消费旅游产品十年间积累的经验。对话记录经编辑，省略号表示省略内容，括号表示为清晰起见添加或替换的词语。
news.bodyHtml:
Last week, Relativity announced that Chris Brown, its chief product officer since 2018, had been named the company’s president, effective July 13. In the new role, Brown continues to lead Relativity’s product organization while adding marketing and technology partnerships to his scope — a change that coincides with the departure of Chief Marketing Officer Cristina Rossman after more than six years with the company.

The appointment comes amid a series of notable moves for the legal data intelligence company, including its June acquisition of Gavel, the document automation company founded by Dorna Moini, and its rollout of governed MCP integrations that allow AI assistants such as Claude to orchestrate matters and workflows within RelativityOne.

On Tuesday, a day after Brown officially stepped into the role, I sat down with him to talk about all of this — the thinking behind combining product and marketing under one leader, the rationale for the Gavel acquisition, why Relativity is opening itself up to general-purpose AI assistants, the adoption trajectory of its aiR products, and the lessons he carried over from a decade spent building consumer travel products at Orbitz.

Below is a transcript of that conversation, which I have edited for length, style and consistency. Ellipses indicate omitted text, and brackets indicate words added or substituted for clarity.

news.titleEn: Firm AI: AI that runs the business of the firm, not just the practice.
news.titleZh: 律所AI：不仅服务于业务实践，更驱动律所运营的AI
news.summaryZh: 若机构要大规模引入AI，需先解决如何将机构背景、机构知识和经验融入模型的问题。这些内容大量存在于文档中，且分散于共享驱动器、桌面、不同的SharePoint实例和Dropbox等各处，管理混乱。因此，机构必须在将信息分享给模型前取得控制权，确保能够保护重大非公开信息（MNPI）、独立性及机密信息。为此，需将信息纳入有序结构。Intapp Collaboration的配置引擎可根据业务类型创建合适结构，将内容放入其中，进而由Intapp Walls正确应用安全策略并保护信息。此外，即使有权访问信息，其中仍可能包含敏感或机密内容，不宜输入模型，因为一旦输入便失去控制，可能被任何人获取或与其他信息混合。因此需剥离、编辑或匿名化这些内容，向模型提供经过净化的版本，保留有价值实质信息但排除机密信息。这构成两到三步的价值主张：组织信息、通过保密政策保护信息，然后以安全负责的方式为AI模型构建基础。无论选择Copilot、Claude还是Celeste等AI解决方案，均可提供这一完整基础。
news.bodyHtml:
So what does that foundation actually look like?

Thad Jampol

Work backwards from a firm that says, “We need to make a major jump into AI.” Okay — the next challenge is: How do you infuse these models with the firm’s context? A lot of that context, institutional knowledge, and experience resides in documents. And in a lot of firms — particularly accounting — content is everywhere: shared drives, desktops, different SharePoint instances, Dropbox. It’s madness.

So they say, “We’re going to have to get control of this information before we’re comfortable sharing it with a model.” That means you need to be able to secure it, lock it down, protect MNPI, protect independence, protect confidential information. To do that, you need to put it into some kind of organized structure. That’s a lot of what Intapp Collaboration’s provisioning engine does: Based on the engagement type, it creates the right structure so you can put content into it. And by putting it into that structure, Intapp Walls can then apply the security policies correctly and protect the information.

And then the coup de grâce: Even if you have access to that information, there may still be sensitive, secretive content in there you really wouldn’t want to feed into a model. Because once it goes in, you lose control. Anyone can surface it, and sometimes it gets commingled with other information. So you strip that out. You redact it. You anonymize it. You feed the model sanitized versions that have all the good substance in it but not the secret information.

That’s a two- or three-step value proposition: Organize your information, protect it with confidentiality policies, and then build the foundation for your AI models in a safe, responsible way. And we provide that whole foundation for whatever AI solution you choose — whether that’s Copilot, Claude, or Celeste.

news.titleZh: Vanilla、肉丸与Cooley的固定费用——对话David Wang
news.summaryZh: Cooley的基金设立平台Vanilla现将其业务中的关键环节——转让——以495美元的固定费用提供。Artificial Lawyer与Cooley创新主管David Wang探讨了定价应基于产出而非投入、法律市场动态的变化，以及宜家肉丸的类比。Vanilla是Cooley专为基金设立提供法律帮助和产品化服务而打造的平台，基金设立是这家加州律所的重要业务领域。但并非该工作的每个环节都需要全律师团队或按小时计费模式。事实上，部分法律工作可以低至495美元的固定费用出售给客户，对于这样一家律所而言这并不算多，因为初级律师一小时工作就可能收费如此。定价变化会在任何市场释放强大力量。更低的产出价格不一定意味着更差的律师。价格变动可以改变需求和购买量，从而推高利润。如果生产成本（即投入）也更低，更低的产出价格可以维持高利润率。新价格改变客户行为和忠诚度，并可激励购买更高价值的产品。总之，固定费用和产品化服务并不意味着大律所律师的PEP降低，只是比每年在小时费率上加5%并为手工工作填写时间表更复杂的模式。而且两者可以协同运作。法律经济学——Artificial Lawyer对法律科技和AI兴趣的基础——正日益成为对话的核心。讽刺的是，法律科技既不全是关于法律本身，也不只是技术。
news.bodyText: Cooley’s fund formation platform, Vanilla, is now offering a key element of its work – transfers – for a $495 flat fee. AL talked to Head of Innovation, David Wang, about how pricing should be all about outputs rather than inputs, the changing legal market dynamic, and the analogy of Ikea’s meatballs. In the short interview we unpack a lot, but the key points are as follows. Vanilla is a dedicated platform built by Cooley to provide legal help and productized services for fund formation – an important area for the California-based firm. But, it’s also where not every element of that work needs a full team of their lawyers, nor a billable hour model. In fact, as noted above, some components of this legal work can be sold to clients on a fixed fee for as little as $495. And that’s not a lot for a firm like this, given a junior associate might bill that for one hour of work. AL and Wang explore some of the key aspects here, which include: Overall, changes to pricing unleash incredibly powerful forces within any market. Moreover, lower output prices don’t necessarily mean poorer lawyers. Price shifts can change demand and the volume of purchases – and that can drive up profits. Lower output prices can sustain high profit margins if production costs – i.e. inputs – are also lower. New prices change customer behaviour and loyalty, and as noted above can incentivise purchases of higher value goods. In short, fixed fees and productised services do not mean Big Law lawyers with less PEP. It’s just a more complex model than adding 5% to the billable hour every year and filling in time sheets for the manual work performed. Moreover, also as explored, the two can operate in unison. Any road, legal economics – the foundation of Artificial Lawyer’s interest in legal tech and AI – is an area that is becoming more and more central to the conversation. Ironically, legal tech is neither all about the law itself, or just technology. We’re gonna dig into this. ⁓ David, good to have you with us. Tell us, what is Vanilla? David (00:00:33)

news.bodyHtml:
After 30 years serving 99% of the Am Law 100, Litera relaunches around one platform, one agent, and one dataset spanning every corner of the firm

CHICAGO – July 15, 2026 – Litera, the Legal AI platform provider that best unifies the practice and business of law, unveiled a company relaunch and unified platform vision, positioning itself as the Legal AI provider best built to run across the practice and business of law on one agent and one dataset. Building on Lito’s first year in market, the relaunch sets the stage for ILTACON in August, where the company will showcase the next version of its award-winning Legal AI agent across Foundation, GrowthTech, and the broader Litera product portfolio. The relaunch also coincides with the expanded deployment of Litera Foundation 365 across five of the 10 largest law firms in the world.

For 30 years, Litera has been the connective tissue of the profession’s most demanding work: 10 million document comparisons a month, over a million daily users across more than 15,000 global customers, 99% logo retention, and 99% penetration of the Am Law 100. What changed over the last 18 months is that firms now expect AI to run through every workflow – not just drafting. The relaunch reflects that shift, and the fact that Litera has already built for it.

“Every AI startup in legal is selling a feature,” said Avaneesh Marwaha, Chief Executive Officer, Litera. “We’re selling the platform those features run on. The practice of law and the business of law have run on separate systems for as long as firms have existed. That ends here: one agent, one dataset, every partner, associate, and business development lead working from the same intelligence.”

Adam Ryan, Chief Product Officer, Litera, added: “AI is table stakes. Trust is the moat. You can’t retrofit years of deterministic accuracy, and you can’t pilot your way into the Am Law 100.” 

The relaunch highlights three areas of platform differentiation:

  • One Agent across the Firm: Lito, embedded natively in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, spans drafting, comparison, contract review, institutional knowledge, and client development – no separate tool to learn, no separate login, no separate dataset. Already, 70% of active Litera One accounts use Lito.

  • Deterministic Accuracy on High-Stakes Work: Litera’s redline algorithm, refined over three decades and 10 million comparisons a month, is rules-based and deterministic. It doesn’t guess, and it doesn’t hallucinate the way probabilistic models can. For high-stakes work, firms confirm in every major benchmarking exercise that large language models do not match it.

  • Foundation for the Business of Law: Litera Foundation and Foundation 365, the institutional knowledge and client relationship management (CRM) platform for the business of law, are now used by five of the 10 largest law firms in the world. Native to Microsoft Dynamics 365 and recognized among the top Microsoft AI partners in the Microsoft AI Inner Circle, Foundation is the counterweight to orchestration-only platforms and generic CRM tools that were never built for how firms run. 

See It Live at ILTACON

The relaunch features a new brand campaign that went live today, in addition to a refreshed website on litera.com and lito.app. It will be reinforced at ILTACON 2026 in Nashville, Aug. 23–27, where Litera will showcase the unified Lito platform vision. See where Litera is headed: litera.com/iltacon. 

About Litera
Litera is the Legal AI platform provider that best unifies the practice and business of law, built on 30 years of legal expertise that no AI startup can shortcut, and engineered for the decades ahead. The company combines purpose-built legal technology with Lito, its award-winning Legal AI agent, to Raise The Bar™ for the legal profession worldwide. With AI solutions spanning legal drafting, document comparison, contract review, knowledge management, business development, and more, Litera serves over 15,000 global customers and more than 1 million daily users, including 99% of the Am Law 100. Integrated directly into Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace across devices, Litera delivers the right data, in the right place, at the right time – reducing context-switching so lawyers can practice law, not manage tools, while winning more business, driving efficiency and the deeper client relationships that fuel sustainable growth. For more information, visit litera.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

Press Contacts

Jared Albert

PR and Communications, Litera

jared.albert@litera.com

Tracy Wemett

BroadPR, Inc. for Litera

twemett@broadpr.com

news.summaryZh: Intapp（纳斯达克代码：INTA）于2026年7月15日在全球发布直播中宣布，此前于2月预览的Celeste现已正式全面可用。Celeste是一款专家级AI协作伙伴，负责运营事务所的业务，涵盖交易筛选、利益冲突审查、业务拓展及横向招聘等环节。它基于各事务所的专有知识，并受事务所自身方法与合规规则约束。当前多数事务所已为每位员工配备AI代理，用于起草、建模和审阅，但事务所增长并未同步加快；为个人从业者构建的AI加速了执业，却未加速其背后的业务，Celeste正是为弥合这一差距而推出。Celeste以事务所自身方法作为可编排的多步骤工作流，内置覆盖业务发起、业务拓展、案件受理、利益冲突、定价、募资、横向招聘等场景的剧本库，并提供无代码构建器。它原生集成于事务所的记录系统，摄取事务所文档，并通过开放连接器对接首选数据合作伙伴。道德墙、知悉必要规则和审计对Celeste的适用方式与对人完全相同，受限信息无论被如何询问都保持受限，事务所可向客户和监管机构展示每项操作的完整记录。Celeste已在早期采用机构中投入使用，包括Hg和BakerHostetler。在私募资本领域，Celeste将保密信息备忘录转化为结构化投资筛选；在投资银行领域，它梳理董事会和管理层关系以寻找最佳业务路径；在法律领域，它能在数分钟内而非数小时内为紧急客户请求呈现相关事项、合伙人经验和过往推介材料，并运行从候选人研究、利益冲突预筛到审查准备和入职的端到端横向招聘生命周期。
news.bodyHtml:
Celeste runs the business of the firm — from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring — on each firm’s own data, under its own rules

PALO ALTO, Calif. — July 15, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announced at its global launch broadcast that Celeste, previewed in February, is now generally available. Celeste is an expert AI coworker that runs the business of the firm, from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring. It’s grounded in each firm’s proprietary knowledge and governed by the firm’s own methods and compliance rules.

Most firms today have AI agents on every desk — drafting, modeling, and reviewing faster than ever. But few firms are growing faster. Firms are finding that AI built for the individual practitioner speeds up the practice, but not the business behind it. That’s the gap Celeste closes.

The work that runs a firm depends on what only the firm knows: its deals, clients, matters, and relationships. It runs on the firm’s own methods — the way it originates a deal, runs a conflict check, or prepares for a pipeline meeting. And it’s bound by obligations that generic AI was never built for, from ethical walls and conflicts rules to client confidentiality. Intapp has spent 20 years building that knowledge, those methods, and that governance into the systems these firms already run on. Celeste starts there.

That’s what makes Celeste different.

  • Celeste gets the firm’s work done. Celeste is an expert AI coworker built for the business workflows of the firm — the work that drives its growth and determines how efficiently it runs. It runs on its own rather than waiting to be asked.
  • Celeste works your way. Celeste encodes the firm’s own methods as playbooks — multi-step workflows that automate the firm’s best practices. It ships with a library of playbooks spanning origination, business development, intake, conflicts, pricing, fundraising, lateral hiring, and beyond, and a no-code builder so teams can easily create their own.
  • Celeste knows your firm. Every firm has access to the same models. What sets a firm apart is what those models don’t know: its deals, clients, relationships, and prior judgment. Celeste is natively integrated into the firm’s systems of record, ingests the firm’s documents, and connects to its preferred data partners through open connectors.
  • Celeste enforces your guardrails. Ethical walls, need-to-know rules, and audits apply to Celeste exactly as they apply to people. Restricted information stays restricted no matter what anyone asks, and the firm can show clients and regulators a full record of every action.

Celeste is already at work in early-adopter firms, including Hg and BakerHostetler. In private capital, Celeste turns a confidential information memorandum into a structured investment screen, drawing on the firm’s own investment criteria, mandate, and deal history. In investment banking, it maps board and management relationships to give bankers the strongest path into a mandate. In legal, it surfaces relevant matters, partner experience, and prior pitch materials for an urgent client request in minutes rather than hours. It also runs an end-to-end lateral hire lifecycle, from candidate research and conflicts pre-screening to clearance preparation and onboarding. For accounting and consulting firms, the same governed coworker works within independence and conflicts obligations from day one.

Intapp calls this Firm AI, the category of AI aimed not at the individual or the work product, but at the business of the firm itself. Horizontal assistants speed up everyday tasks. Practice AI helps produce the work product. Firm AI runs the business behind both.

Availability

Intapp Celeste is generally available now. Firms can explore the use case library, request a demonstration, or contact their Intapp account team at intapp.com.

Supporting quotes

Thad Jampol, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer, Intapp

“Firms will run several kinds of AI: horizontal assistants for everyday work, practice AI for the work product, and Firm AI for the business of the firm itself. That last category is the hard one, and it’s the one almost nobody is building. That’s Celeste — an expert AI coworker built on a firm’s own playbooks, knowledge, and guardrails. When a conflicts team can clear 10 times the matters and a fund can screen 10 times the deals, that’s not saved time — that’s a new business model.”

Katherine Lowry, Chief Information Officer and Head of IncuBaker, BakerHostetler

“Our immediate focus is on conflicts and intake, because that’s where Celeste will have the biggest impact on our operations. Clearing conflicts faster to win engagements — and going through clearance at a much faster rate when bringing in laterals with thousands of matters — will make a real difference for our teams. What drew us to Intapp was the shared alignment on process and on governance.”

Shirin Veeran, Data, Tech & AI Strategy, Hg

“The intelligence is ours, not something generic applied to our firm. Celeste screens against our actual mandate, drawing on knowledge we have built across the firm over two decades. Having a clear, always-current view of deal progress and pipeline speed — without the usual reporting lift — is genuinely valuable to any deal team.”

Additional resources

  • Explore Intapp Celeste
  • Watch the full launch broadcast on demand at intapp.com/celeste-launch/

Connect with Intapp

  • Learn more at Intapp
  • Get more news in the Intapp newsroom
  • Follow Intapp on LinkedIn

About Intapp

Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA) is the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries. Intapp’s vertically tailored agentic solutions are built for the specialized workflows, complex relationship networks, and professional compliance requirements of accounting, consulting, investment banking, law, private capital, and real assets firms. By applying Firm AI to core processes and data, Intapp helps partners, dealmakers, and advisors drive firm growth, manage compliance, and improve profitability. Learn why the world’s top firms trust Intapp’s industry-specific enterprise solutions at intapp.com.

Contact
Emily Martinez
Global Media and Communications Director
press@intapp.com
