news.titleEn: NewMod General Legal Hits $11.5m Funding in 3 Months
news.titleZh: NewMod律所General Legal三个月内融资1150万美元
news.summaryZh: AI原生律所General Legal宣布，自正式成立仅三个月以来，已累计获得1150万美元的种子轮和种子前轮融资。本轮融资由Audacious Ventures领投。联合创始人Ryan Walker曾担任Casetext首席技术官及汤森路透副总裁，他表示，该律所专注于商业合同领域，其精英商业律师通过Slack平台与客户协作，能够以远低于传统外部律师费的成本快速处理合同。General Legal的定价模式为每份合同固定收费500美元，通过私人Slack渠道在数小时内完成工作。该律所仅聘用美国执业资格律师，所有协议均经过资深人工律师审核，服务范围涵盖MSA、DPA、NDA、供应商协议、服务条款及最终用户许可协议等标准商业合同。律所支持通过Slack、电子邮件、视频会议或电话协作，不按小时计费，无隐藏费用，无最低消费，并可参与谈判及起草新协议。General Legal是Y Combinator孵化器本冬季批次中的多家NewMod律所之一，主要面向早期成长阶段企业。此类律所将AI置于业务核心，同时配备熟练律师，摒弃按小时计费模式，实现快速价值交付和相对低成本。
news.bodyHtml:
NewMod, AI-native law firm General Legal has announced it has hit $11.5m in Seed and pre-Seed funding since launching officially just three months ago.

Co-founder, Ryan Walker, who previously was CTO at Casetext and then a VP at Thomson Reuters, said: ‘I’m so proud to announce that General Legal – the AI native law firm for commercial contracts – has raised a combined $11.5m Seed and Pre-Seed round led by Audacious Ventures!

‘Our elite commercial attorneys live in your Slack and turn contracts lightning fast, for a fraction of the cost of traditional outside counsel.’

So, what is this all about? Well, see their rate card below – which is an eye-opener. Then read some of the answers to their FAQs.

And as you can see, they will handle your work via a private Slack channel, take just hours, and charge a flat rate of $500 per contract. How many Big Law firms would be able to do that with their current business model?

..

Some illustrative FAQs and answers:

‘We’re a law firm that hires only highly-qualified, US barred attorneys. Our attorneys are trained to use our AI platforms to accelerate their work but all agreements handled by our firm are reviewed by an experienced human attorney.

‘We can help with any standard commercial agreements, including MSAs, DPAs, NDAs, vendor agreements, TOSs EULAs, and more.

‘Our lawyers work where you work. Many of our clients use Slack and our lawyers can work with you or your legal team directly in your Slack. We can also support you over email, video-conference, or phone.

‘For our flat review price, our firm will support your contract through every turn all the way to signature. Our lawyers can even join a negotiation with the other side. We don’t bill by the hour, there are no surprise fees, and no minimums.

‘We’re happy to draft new commercial agreements.’

–

Is this a big deal?

One conversation that keeps coming up with AL, at least among folks focused on the frontier of the legal tech market, is NewMods / AI-native law firms. And understandably so. Their combination of putting AI at the core of the business, but also adding skilled lawyers around the ‘means of legal production’ creates what AL has been hoping to see since this site started. I.e. lawyers really using AI as it’s meant to be used, not as a little helper on the side of your work, but right in the centre of it, in a way that allows its full capabilities to be leveraged.

Naturally, to do so means dropping the time-based approach to billing. Time to value for clients is thus rapid and the costs are – relatively – far less than what Big Law currently charges.

General Legal, as with many others now, such as Soxton which has already pioneered the area of helping startups, is focused on early-stage companies. And that makes sense. Those companies are new to having legal needs, maybe don’t have a legal team internally, and are cost-sensitive as they’re running on VC money.

But.…..! AL is sure that once they get going, the legal market segments they will approach will expand. In fact, while General Legal says on its website that it’s for those ‘in the growth stage’, its offer of handling MSAs and NDAs could be useful for companies of any size.

And finally, there is the fact that this Y Combinator cohort startup – one of several NewMods in this Winter’s group to get backing from the legendary investor and incubator – is only a few months old and already has some solid capital to help it grow.

More about General Legal here.

Note: ‘NewMod’ is an AL term, which stands for New Business Model Law Firm. This site tends to prefer this over AI-native, or AI-first in this context, because the term AI-native is getting used very broadly and AI-first doesn’t really tell us what is going on at a commercial level. So, NewMod refers specifically to a new business model approach, (i.e. no hourly bills and not shaped in the traditional way), plus it’s the AI that makes that possible – rather than the other way round.

—

Legal Innovators California Conference – June 10 and 11

If you’re in the US and looking for the next major event to join after Legal Week, then see you in California this June!

Legal Innovators California, the landmark West Coast legal tech event, will take place on June 10 and 11, in the heart of the Bay Area, the home to many of the world’s leading AI businesses – and plenty of legal tech pioneers as well! More information and tickets here.

news.titleEn: Legora Partners With Jus Mundi For Arbitration Needs
news.titleZh: Legora与Jus Mundi合作满足仲裁需求
news.summaryZh: Jus Mundi与Legora建立合作伙伴关系，将Jus AI工具整合到更广泛的生成式AI平台中，以协助国际仲裁需求。该合作将于今年晚些时候全面推出。这是Legora及其主要竞争对手Harvey自推出以来达成的一系列以数据为重点的合作之一。双方称其为“代理对代理集成”，但更简单地说，这是通过Legora获取非常有用的仲裁数据。关键功能包括：在Legora内部调用Jus Mundi的AI，无需切换平台或丢失上下文即可查询Jus Mundi的专业仲裁智能；将权威仲裁智能集成到Legora工作流程中，基于Jus Mundi的专业内容构建工作流程；一键访问可信来源，引文直接链接到Jus Mundi上的完整文档以进行深入分析。因此，现在在Legora内，可以查询Jus AI以获得全面的、有引文支持的答案，这些答案基于Jus Mundi的仲裁文件集合，包括国际裁决、条约、机构规则、出版物以及与全球100多家领先仲裁机构合作的独家数据。该合作旨在将专业AI带到从业者工作的地方，Jus AI是为仲裁从头构建的，其推理方式不同，理解国际争议的背景，并已得到仲裁从业者的验证。仲裁律师处理的是职业中最复杂的法律信息，通过将Jus AI与Legora集成，使从业者能够直接在AI工作流程中访问领先的仲裁智能。
news.bodyHtml:
Jus Mundi and Legora have formed a partnership that will integrate the Jus AI tool within the wider genAI platform to help with international arbitration needs. It will roll out in full later this year, they added.

Sounds useful, and it is one of a growing number of data-focused partnerships that Legora – and its main rival Harvey – have done across the market since launching. They’re calling it ‘an agent to agent integration’, but it’s probably simpler just to think of this as access to very useful arbitration data that you can get to via Legora.

They added that the key features are:

  • ‘Call Jus Mundi’s AI inside Legora: Query Jus Mundi’s specialized arbitration intelligence without switching platforms or losing context.
  • Integrate authoritative arbitration intelligence into Legora workflows: Build workflows grounded in Jus Mundi’s expert content.
  • One-click access to trusted sources: Citations link directly to full documents on Jus Mundi for deeper analysis.’

So, now within Legora, you can ‘query Jus AI to receive comprehensive, citation-backed answers grounded in Jus Mundi’s collection of arbitration documents, including international awards, treaties, institutional rules, publications, and exclusive data from partnerships with more than 100 leading arbitration institutions worldwide’.

Jean-Rémi de Maistre, CEO and Co-Founder of Jus Mundi, commented: ‘This partnership is about bringing specialized AI where practitioners work. We built Jus AI from the ground up for arbitration. It reasons differently, it understands the context of international disputes, and arbitration practitioners have validated its high quality. Legora’s platform brings research, review, and drafting into one collaborative workspace, and together we are making Jus AI’s unique capabilities accessible within workflows lawyers already use.’

Gabrielle Persson, VP Content & Partnerships at Legora, added: ‘Arbitration lawyers work with some of the most complex legal information in the profession. By integrating Jus AI with Legora, we are enabling practitioners to access leading arbitration intelligence directly within their AI workflows.’

As ever access to quality legal data is key….!

—

And, if the above was interesting, wait until you see these events: 

A Legal Tech Conference For All of Europe

Legal Innovators Europe – Paris – June 24 and 25.

There will be more news about the conference and key speakers as we get closer to June.

Look forward to seeing you there!

Richard Tromans, Founder, Artificial Lawyer and Legal Innovators conference Chair.

news.titleEn: AI-First ‘Keith’ Bags £2m For Property Work
news.titleZh: AI优先的‘Keith’获200万英镑融资，专注房产交易
news.summaryZh: 英国出现一家名为Keith的AI优先律师事务所，专注于住宅物业销售（即产权转让），已筹集200万英镑。Keith计划由英国产权转让师官方机构CLC监管，而非SRA。联合创始人包括曾创办素食香肠公司的Andy Shovel、曾创建植物基食品品牌THIS的Pete Sharman，以及曾创办混合调度平台Common Surface的Sam Tucker，后者现负责产品。英国产权转让协会前主席、90年代一家市场领先产权转让公司的创始人Eddie Goldsmith担任战略顾问和非执行董事。Keith将提供与其他律所相同的产权转让服务，但幕后流程不同：AI自动审查信件和文件，每项操作通过预定义工作流管理。客户可通过电子邮件、短信或电话即时联系Keith，实时跟踪交易进度，在线完成任务，全天候可用。AI负责审查产权文件、分析房产搜索结果、处理来信和起草回复，标记问题、提取信息并提出建议，但合格产权转让师始终在内容发送给客户或对方前进行审查和批准。客户还可与AI代理Keith对话，安全获取交易详情并回答产权转让问题。最初主要使用OpenAI模型，近几个月发现Anthropic的Opus和Sonnet模型表现更好。AI由律师团队管理，设有严格护栏确保只完成范围内工作，并在有疑问时低阈值转人工。定价待定，计划定位市场低端。Keith旨在通过AI即时处理任务、快速审查文件，解决产权转让师积压和延误问题，明确各方行动，集中化平台，通过API与搜索提供商、土地登记处和HMRC等外部服务交互，并提供24/7电话服务。融资轮已于今年早些时候完成，投资方包括Backed、Breega和Notion等欧洲风投。
news.bodyHtml:
There is another NewMod, AI-first ‘law firm’ in town. In this case it’s called Keith and will focus on residential property sales in the UK, (AKA conveyancing). It has just raised £2m.

AL asked its co-founder Andy Shovel – who previously launched a vegan sausage company – all about it, (see below). It’s understood that Keith won’t be regulated by the SRA, but instead the plan is to be regulated by the official body for conveyancers in the UK, the CLC.

Also a co-founder is Pete Sharman, who previously created the plant-based food brand THIS, with Shovel. Then there is Sam Tucker who is Keith’s third founder; previously he started hybrid scheduling platform Common Surface and now oversees product at Keith. Eddie Goldsmith, former Chairman of the UK Conveyancing Association and founder of a market-leading conveyancing firm in the 90s, is a strategic advisor and non-exec Director, they added.

AL Interview with Andy Shovel

Can you please set out what it will offer in terms of conveyancing?

Keith will be a law firm offering all the same conveyancing services you’d expect from any other – handling both purchases and sales of residential property. However, behind the scenes we’ll be running the process very differently: AI automatically reviews correspondence and documents and every action is managed through pre-defined workflows. For clients, rather than lengthy email chains and time spent on hold waiting to speak to a conveyancer, they’ll be able to instantly speak to Keith via email, text or phone, track real-time progress on their transaction, see exactly what they need to do next, and complete tasks like signing documents or uploading information directly through our online platform – all available 24/7, not just during office hours.

What will the AI do, what will lawyers do?

AI handles the heavy lifting across the transaction: reviewing title documents, analysing property search results, processing incoming correspondence, and drafting responses. It flags issues, extracts key information, and makes recommendations – but a qualified conveyancer always reviews and approves before anything goes to the client or the other side. The result isn’t fewer lawyers, it’s dramatically more efficient ones – focused on judgment calls and client care rather than admin. Clients will also be able to speak to Keith, our AI agent, who can securely provide details about their transaction and answer conveyancing questions.

Which LLMs are you using?

Initially we were mostly using models provided by OpenAI; however, in recent months we have found Anthropic’s Opus + Sonnet models to perform better.

How will it be managed?

The AI will be managed our team of lawyers, and with strict guardrails in place to make sure that it only completes in-scope work, and has a low threshold for human referral, when there is any doubt.

What will you charge?

This is still TBC but we plan to come in around the lower end of the market.

Given that one of the biggest challenges with house sales is the human factor and the Land Registry data, how will Keith speed things up?

Currently conveyancers are often overwhelmed and it can take days for simple tasks to reach the top of their to do list. Keith will be able to immediately action tasks, requests or enquiries – and because AI can review documents and process information in seconds rather than hours, the work itself gets done faster and more accurately too. Secondly, it’s often unclear who needs to act and what is holding up the process. At Keith, we’ll make it clear who needs to act when and be able to handhold through every step of the process. Clients get a much better experience – guided step by step through what they need to do, with forms pre-filled from information we already hold so they’re never duplicating work. Today, conveyancers juggle multiple different portals and systems for each external service. At Keith, everything is centralised in one platform. We’ll interact with most external services such as Search Providers, Land Registry and HMRC via API. Also, you’ll be able to call and speak to Keith 24 hours a day. Keith is a much more sophisticated client service agent than 99% of people will have ever experienced.

And, has the £2m already been invested into your new company?

Yes we closed the funding round earlier this year. We’re pleased to be working with several leading European VCs: Backed, Breega and Notion.

—

So, there you go. There is no stopping NewMods / AI-first firms now. As predicted by AL at the end of 2025, there will be more and more of them this year, in the UK, in the US, and elsewhere. AI has simply made their arrival totally logical and the best way for many work streams to be handled.

More here about Keith.

There will be more news about the conference and key speakers as we get closer to June.

Look forward to seeing you there!

news.titleEn: Head of Weil Dealvision360: Innovation Should be ‘Key Emphasis in Law Firm Culture'
news.titleZh: Weil Dealvision360负责人：创新应成为律所文化的‘核心重点’
news.summaryZh: 在LegalTech Monitor奖项系列问答中，Weil, Gotshal & Manges私募股权合伙人兼Weil Dealvision360负责人Arnie Fridhandler分享了对律所创新的看法。大型律所因繁文缛节导致创新项目审批困难耗时，小型律所则受限于人力、财力和市场数据获取。Weil凭借规模、经验与案件量，能准确反映市场状况并灵活批准新想法。创新应成为律所文化核心，得到各层级尤其是领导层支持；成功实施需要清晰沟通、有力商业论证及领导层和员工认同。此外还存在“技能缺口”，律师需接受新技术培训，以有效利用技术并向客户传达益处。生成式与代理式AI正推动律所自动化达到新水平。DealVision360通过提升效率并提供实时数据驱动的交易洞察，改善私募股权客户成果。随着AI广泛采用，文档审查、法律研究和合同起草等常规任务自动化提高，律所需实施新技术并培训员工专注更具战略性的高价值任务，并更多利用AI支持的高级数据分析工具提升效率与客户服务。AI加速尽职调查等流程，部分律所将考虑替代业务模式。未来更多律所将转向AI工具，基本法律任务自动化需要更先进数据安全工具，并要求与相关客户清晰沟通和完全透明。客户将要求更高生产力和可操作数据以区分律所。因此律所应投资内部基础设施以支持内部创新。Weil DealVision360的实现离不开强大内部结构、领导层支持及鼓励大胆想法的环境，重新定义了Weil作为战略合作伙伴凭借市场情报为客户交付价值。
news.bodyHtml:
As part of our awards series, we asked our winners about what they see as the biggest barriers and drivers of innovation, the impact of emerging technologies, and how they believe the market will change in the near future.

Here’s our Q&A with Arnie Fridhandler, private equity partner and head of Weil Dealvision360 at Weil, Gotshal & Manges, which won the award for Innovations in Dealmaking.

What do you currently see as the biggest barriers to, and biggest drivers of innovation in law firms?

It can be more difficult and time-consuming to get an innovative project approved at the largest law firms due to the excess of red tape, and smaller firms suffer from a lack of manpower, financial resources and access to broader market data. Weil occupies an ideal position here with respect to its size, as we have the reach, experience and volume of matters to provide an accurate snapshot of market conditions and can be nimble in our approach to approving new ideas. 

Innovation should be a key emphasis in law firm culture and should be supported at all levels, especially by leadership. Successful implementation requires clear communication, a strong business case, and buy-in from leadership and staff. There is also the issue of a “skill gap” or shortage of employees with the necessary skills to implement and manage new technologies effectively. Lawyers need training on new technologies to ensure they can be used effectively to benefit the firm and its clients and to ensure that they can communicate these benefits to clients in an effective way.

Emerging technologies such as generative and agentic AI are enabling new levels of automation in law firms. How do you expect these changes to impact law firms' operations, staffing and/or business models?

DealVision360 demonstrates how AI can improve outcomes for our private equity clients by enhancing efficiency and providing crucial deal insights driven by real-time data. As widespread adoption of AI by law firms leads to the increased automation of routine tasks such as document review, legal research and contract drafting, firms will need to adapt by implementing new technologies and training their staff to dedicate their focus to more strategic, high-value tasks. Firms will make increasing use of advanced data analytics tools, with the support of AI, to pursue business efficiencies and improve client service. As AI significantly speeds up due diligence and other important processes, some firms will begin to consider alternative business models.

How would you like to see technology specifically designed for law firms change over the next few years, and why?

In the coming years we will see an increasing number of firms turn to AI tools to enhance their legal services and workflows. The increasing automation of basic legal tasks will necessitate the development of more advanced data security tools and will require clear communication and full transparency with any clients whose matters may interact with those technologies. 

As clients begin to recognize these efficiencies, they will begin to demand more productivity for their fees as well as actionable data that separates a law firm from its competitors. As such, more firms should focus on investing in their internal infrastructure to support the generation of innovative ideas from within. Weil DealVision360 represents a game-changing innovation that could not have occurred without a robust internal structure, buy-in from leadership and an environment that is supportive of bold and ambitious ideas. It has redefined how Weil delivers value to its clients—as strategic partners armed with unmatched market intelligence.

research.titleEn: Can Small Models Reason About Legal Documents? A Comparative Study
research.titleZh: 小型模型能否推理法律文件？一项比较研究
research.abstractEn: Large language models show promise for legal applications, but deploying frontier models raises concerns about cost, latency, and data privacy. We evaluate whether sub-10B parameter models can serve as practical alternatives by testing nine models across three legal benchmarks (ContractNLI, CaseHOLD, and ECtHR) using five prompting strategies (direct, chain-of-thought, few-shot, BM25 RAG, and dense RAG). Across 405 experiments with three random seeds per configuration, we find that a Mixture-of-Experts model activating only 3B parameters matches GPT-4o-mini in mean accuracy while surpassing it on legal holding identification, and that architecture and training quality matter more than raw parameter count. Our largest model (9B parameters) performs worst overall. Chain-of-thought prompting proves sharply task-dependent, improving contract entailment but degrading multiple-choice legal reasoning, while few-shot prompting emerges as the most consistently effective strategy. Comparing BM25 and dense retrieval for RAG, we find near-identical results, suggesting the bottleneck lies in the language model's utilization of retrieved context rather than retrieval quality. All experiments were conducted via cloud inference APIs at a total cost of $62, demonstrating that rigorous LLM evaluation is accessible without dedicated GPU infrastructure.
research.abstractZh: 大型语言模型在法律应用中展现出潜力，但部署前沿模型引发了关于成本、延迟和数据隐私的担忧。我们通过测试九个模型在三个法律基准（ContractNLI、CaseHOLD和ECtHR）上使用五种提示策略（直接提示、思维链提示、少样本提示、BM25检索增强生成和稠密检索增强生成），评估了参数少于100亿的模型是否能作为实用替代方案。在每种配置使用三个随机种子进行的405次实验中，我们发现仅激活30亿参数的专家混合模型在平均准确率上与GPT-4o-mini相当，同时在法律判决识别方面超越它，并且架构和训练质量比原始参数数量更重要。我们最大的模型（90亿参数）整体表现最差。思维链提示策略被证明高度依赖任务，能改进合同蕴含推理但会降低多项选择法律推理的表现，而少样本提示策略成为最持续有效的策略。比较BM25和稠密检索在检索增强生成中的表现，我们发现结果几乎相同，表明瓶颈在于语言模型对检索上下文的利用而非检索质量。所有实验均通过云推理API进行，总成本为62美元，证明无需专用GPU基础设施即可进行严谨的大型语言模型评估。

news.titleEn: Foley & Lardner's Director of Innovative Tech: 'Truly Agentic, AI-driven Workflows Will be Transformative'
news.titleZh: Foley & Lardner创新技术总监：真正智能体化的AI驱动工作流将带来变革
news.summaryZh: Foley & Lardner荣获最佳人工智能应用奖，其创新技术与研究总监Charlotte Logullo接受问答，分享了对律所创新障碍与驱动因素、新兴技术影响及市场变化的看法。律所创新由客户对更快速、透明和价值导向法律服务的期望驱动，促使采用AI、分析和云技术来简化工作流并提升响应能力。领导力和实验文化至关重要，专门的创新团队和持续培训帮助律师利用新工具。战略规划、稳健治理以及与技术供应商和客户的合作进一步加速解决方案开发和商业模式创新。但重大障碍依然存在：法律专业人士对变革的抵制、组织复杂性、保密担忧和风险规避，以及仅关注技术而非整体问题解决的狭隘创新观。生成式和智能体AI正在改变律所工作方式，自动化法律研究、合同审查和文件起草等常规任务，使律师能专注于战略工作和客户关系。业务专业人员和律师角色可能转变，初级律师和业务人员更多关注审查AI结果和提供专家建议，技术技能变得更有价值。有效使用AI的律所将吸引更多客户和人才，否则可能落后。律所需要强有力的AI政策、持续培训和负责任安全使用AI的承诺。Logullo希望律所技术从基础自动化转向真正智能体化的AI驱动工作流，以最少人工输入管理文件审查、合同分析和法律研究等常规任务。安全实时协作平台、直观文档管理和集成分析正变得不可或缺。技术提供商必须优先考虑用户友好界面、无缝互操作性和灵活配置，摒弃一刀切方案。
news.bodyHtml:
As part of our awards series, we asked our winners about what they see as the biggest barriers and drivers of innovation, the impact of emerging technologies, and how they believe the market will change in the near future.

Here’s our Q&A with Charlotte Logullo, director, innovative technology and research at Foley & Lardner, which won the award for Best Use of Artificial Intelligence.

What do you currently see as the biggest barriers to, and biggest drivers of innovation in law firms?

Innovation in law firms is driven by client expectations for faster, more transparent, and value-focused legal services, prompting adoption of AI, analytics, and cloud technologies that streamline workflows and enhance responsiveness. Leadership and a culture of experimentation are essential, with dedicated innovation teams and ongoing training helping lawyers leverage new tools and adapt to evolving market dynamics. Strategic planning, robust governance, and partnerships with tech vendors and clients further accelerate solution development and business model innovation.

However, significant barriers persist: resistance to change remains strong among legal professionals accustomed to established workflows, and organizational complexity can slow coordinated adoption. Confidentiality concerns and risk aversion often hinder collaboration and the inclusion of non-lawyer professionals, while a narrow view of innovation—focused solely on technology rather than holistic problem-solving—can limit progress. Successful law firms overcome these obstacles by aligning innovation with strategic goals, fostering open-minded leadership, and continuously improving processes. Ultimately, innovation flourishes where technology, leadership, culture, and client-centricity intersect, enabling law firms to deliver higher-quality work with greater speed, efficiency, and confidence.

Emerging technologies such as generative and agentic AI are enabling new levels of automation in law firms. How do you expect these changes to impact law firms' operations, staffing and/or business models?

Generative and agentic AI are changing how law firms work by automating routine tasks including components of legal research, contract review, and document drafting. This allows lawyers to spend more time on important strategic work and building client relationships. With AI handling repetitive jobs, law firms can work faster and provide services more efficiently.

Business professional and attorney roles will likely shift, as junior lawyers and business professionals focus more on reviewing AI results and giving expert advice, while technology skills become more valuable. Firms that use AI effectively will attract more clients and talented professionals, while those that do not may fall behind. For these changes to succeed, law firms need strong AI policies, ongoing training, and a commitment to using AI responsibly and securely. In the end, AI should aid law firms to become quicker, more accurate, and more flexible in their work.

How would you like to see technology specifically designed for law firms change over the next few years, and why?

As law firm technology evolves, the shift from basic automation to truly agentic, AI-driven workflows will be transformative, enabling routine tasks such as document review, contract analysis, and legal research to be managed with minimal human input and delivering new efficiencies across daily practice. Rather than simply speeding up repetitive work, these advancements empower legal professionals to focus on strategic, client-centered activities while AI proactively anticipates client needs and provides actionable insights directly within familiar workflows.

Secure, real-time collaboration platforms, intuitive document management, and integrated analytics are becoming indispensable, as they support teamwork across practice groups and with clients, all while upholding strict confidentiality standards.

To promote widespread adoption, technology providers must prioritize user-friendly interfaces, seamless interoperability, and flexible configuration options so firms can tailor solutions to their strategic goals and practice specialties — moving away from one-size-fits-all offerings. As agentic AI becomes more mainstream and readily available, legal technology vendors should view AI capabilities as a fundamental value-add to their platforms, not as a separate expensive add-on, ensuring that pricing reflects AI’s role in enhancing the efficiency and overall value of legal services rather than capitalizing on novelty. Ultimately, these advances will drive better client engagement by improving transparency and providing quicker turnaround for routine matters, helping law firms become faster, more accurate, and more adaptable in a competitive market.

news.titleEn: Harvey reaches $11bn valuation with $200m new funding round
news.titleZh: Harvey完成2亿美元新融资，估值达110亿美元
news.summaryZh:
Harvey于3月25日宣布完成2亿美元新融资，由现有投资方GIC和Sequoia联合领投，现有投资方Andreessen Horowitz、Coatue、Conviction Partners、Elad Gil、Evantic和Kleiner Perkins参投。本轮融资对Harvey的估值为110亿美元。投资将用于扩展客户在Harvey上运行的代理，并壮大全球范围内支持客户的嵌入式法律工程团队。

AI不仅是在协助律师，而是正在成为法律工作得以完成的系统；走在前面的律所和内部团队正在构建代理来执行复杂工作流，使律师能够专注于判断、战略和成果。超过25,000个自定义代理在Harvey上运行，执行并购、尽职调查、合同起草和文件审查等工作。客户越来越多地部署长周期代理，在基金设立等复杂用例中处理长期多步骤工作流，并在Shared Spaces内部署代理，以安全协调法律团队及其外部合作伙伴的工作。Harvey的法律工程师与客户并肩工作，构建并持续改进运行其工作的代理。同一家公司联合领投三轮对Sequoia而言实属罕见，这反映出自A轮首次合作以来信念只增不减；全球超过100,000名律师在Harvey上运行最关键的工作，Sequoia相信Harvey有望成为未来十年最重要的公司之一。
news.bodyHtml:
Harvey today (25 March) announced $200 million in new funding co-led by returning investors GIC and Sequoia. The round values Harvey at $11 billion and includes participation from existing investors Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Conviction Partners, Elad Gil, Evantic, and Kleiner Perkins. Harvey says that the investment will be used to expand the agents customers run on Harvey and grow the embedded legal engineering teams supporting them globally.

“AI isn’t just assisting lawyers. It’s becoming the system through which legal work gets done,” said Winston Weinberg, CEO and co-founder of Harvey. “The law firms and in-house teams leading the way are building agents that execute complex workflows so lawyers can focus on judgment, strategy, and outcomes.”

Advertisement

In a blog post noting the raise today, Harvey said that more than 25,000 custom agents operate on Harvey, executing work across M&A, due diligence, contract drafting, and document review. Customers are increasingly deploying long-horizon agents that handle multi-step workflows over extended periods for complex use cases such as fund formation. They are also deploying agents within Shared Spaces to securely coordinate work across legal teams and their external partners. Harvey’s legal engineers work alongside customers to build and continuously improve the agents that run their work.

Pat Grady, a partner at Sequoia, said: “Co-leading three rounds in the same company is rare for Sequoia and reflects conviction that has only grown stronger since we first partnered at the Series A. More than 100,000 lawyers around the world run their most critical work on Harvey, and we believe it’s positioned to become one of the most important companies of the next decade.”

news.titleEn: Legora Launches Legal AI Scholars Program Among US Law Schools
news.titleZh: Legora在美国法学院推出法律AI学者计划
news.summaryZh:
在法律院校寻求为学生提供更多AI相关培训之际，Legora推出了法律AI学者计划。法律教育工作者对此类计划需求旺盛。他透露，长期以来收到许多教授和法学院的合作请求，但公司花时间真正将 offerings 落地，并与这些机构的负责人、院长等共同设计。目标不仅是让师生在平台上获得赋能，还要塑造课程及更广泛的支持体系，这只能通过与法学院合作实现。

该计划涵盖西北普利兹克法学院、斯坦福法学院、芝加哥大学法学院、康奈尔法学院、加州大学洛杉矶分校法学院、德克萨斯大学法学院、范德堡法学院、波士顿大学法学院和旧金山大学法学院。Legora计划在未来几个月扩展与其他大学的合作。培训将涵盖如何有效且合乎伦理地使用AI进行起草和审查，以及大规模开展法律分析、综合和文件审查，以提升AI熟练度和职业准备。AI正迅速变得强大，掌握其使用方法的从业者将显著超越不掌握者，律所领导者也在寻找能实际展示最新技术能力的候选人。Legora并非首个与法学院合作教授AI的法律科技初创公司，Harvey于8月宣布了类似免费合作计划。但Junestrand不认为Harvey等项目与Legora存在竞争，学生和教师接触法律AI技术的机会越多越好。
news.bodyHtml:
The program's introduction comes at a time when law schools are trying to offer their students more AI-related training. According to Legora CEO and co-founder Max Junestrand, there has been ample demand among legal educators for such an initiative.

“We've gotten a lot of requests from professors and law schools to work with them over a long period of time, but we took the time to really operationalize an offering that we then co-designed together with the leaders of these organizations, the deans, et cetera,” Junestrand told Legaltech News. “We wanted to [not only get] people and law students empowered on the platform, but also shape the curriculum and the broader enablement around that, and that can really only be done in collaboration between us and the law school.”

The program includes participation from Northwestern Pritzker School of Law, Stanford Law School, University of Chicago Law School, Cornell Law School, University of California Los Angeles School of Law, the University of Texas School of Law, Vanderbilt Law School, Boston University School of Law and University of San Francisco School of Law. Legora plans to expand its partnerships with other universities in the coming months.

Legora’s training will cover using AI effectively and ethically for drafting and review as well as conducting legal analysis, synthesis and document review at scale to encourage AI proficiency and professional preparedness.

“The reality is that AI is now quickly becoming so good that the practitioner who knows how to leverage it will be able to significantly outperform the people who don't,” Junestrand added. “We're certainly seeing that in engineering, where being able to write software with the help of AI is an incredibly valuable and marketable skill, and when we speak with law firm leaders, they are looking for candidates who don't only talk a big game, but can actually show proficiency with the latest tech.”

Legora is not the first legal tech startup to collaborate with law schools to teach students about AI. Harvey announced a similar free-of-charge partnership program with a number of U.S. law schools in August.

However, Junestrand said he does not view programs like Harvey's as being in competition with Legora's, noting that the more access students and instructors have to legal-focused AI technology, the better.

“I think that no law school student would not benefit from being part of the work that we're doing and if they're doing that in parallel with something else, I think that's super,” he said. “You want to give these students and professionals the best chance at a wonderful career, and you want to give them the chance to use AI in a way that serves them and not the other way around, and that can happen in many different ways probably.”

news.titleEn: Dentons deploys Lexis Everyfile within its UK Legal Delivery Centre
news.titleZh: 大成律师事务所英国法律交付中心部署Lexis Everyfile
news.summaryZh: 全球律所大成（Dentons）经过分阶段推广，已将LexisNexis基于网页的案件管理应用Lexis Everyfile嵌入其英国法律交付中心（LDC）的核心。LDC为广泛的法律和行政工作提供流程驱动支持，使大成英国业务团队能够专注于更高价值的事务。Everyfile已成为LDC协调和交付工作不可或缺的一部分，其灵活性允许塑造真正反映团队运作方式的工作流程，同时保持重复性任务所需的结构和一致性，帮助提高可见性、减少摩擦，让人员有更多精力专注于真正需要其专业知识的工​​作。Lexis Everyfile旨在简化案件交付，在可配置环境中连接律师专业知识、关键文档、流程步骤和数据洞察。该平台的结构化数据采集和一致的工作流设计也支持大成在AI就绪方面的更广泛目标。随着Lexis Everyfile在关键工作流中提供更完整、更准确的数据集，大成将能更好地负责任且有效地利用新兴AI工具。Everyfile旨在使律所的运营骨干更智能、更互联，大成的实施表明单一数字文件可以释放知识和流程的价值，赋能团队并加强整个业务的决策。2024年，其礼律师事务所（Clyde & Co）也部署了Lexis Everyfile。
news.bodyHtml:
Following a phased rollout, global law firm Dentons has embedded LexisNexis‘ web-based matter management application Lexis Everyfile at the core of its UK Legal Delivery Centre (LDC). The LDC provides process‑driven support across a broad range of legal and administrative work, enabling Dentons’ UK practice groups to focus on higher‑value matters.

“Everyfile has quickly become an integral part of how we coordinate and deliver work across the Legal Delivery Centre. Its flexibility allows us to shape workflows that genuinely reflect how our teams operate, while maintaining the structure and consistency we need across recurring tasks,” said Greg Rigby, head of LDC at Dentons. “It’s helped us improve visibility, reduce friction and give our people more headroom to focus on the work that really requires their expertise.”

Advertisement

Designed to simplify matter delivery, Lexis Everyfile connects lawyer expertise, key documents, process steps, and data insights in a configurable environment. The platform’s structured data capture and consistent workflow design also support Dentons’ broader goals around AI‑readiness. With Lexis Everyfile providing a more complete, more accurate dataset across key workstreams, the firm will be better positioned to leverage emerging AI tools responsibly and effectively.

“Everyfile is designed to make the operational backbone of a law firm more intelligent and more connected. Dentons’ implementation shows how a single digital file can unlock the value of knowledge and process in ways that empower teams and strengthen decision‑making across the business,” said Nigel Williams, product director of LexisNexis Enterprise Solutions.

In 2024 Clyde & Co deployed Lexis Everyfile and you can watch our webinar, From Rollout to Results, here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NWEBAmYXFMQ

news.titleEn: Agentic AI in Action: How Simplifai is Disrupting the Insurance Industry with Artem Gonchakov
news.titleZh: 智能体AI实战：Simplifai如何颠覆保险业——对话Artem Gonchakov
news.summaryZh: 了智能体AI（Agentic AI）在保险行业的实际应用。主持人Joseph Raczyński长期关注智能体AI话题，此前多停留在理论层面，近期通过播客讨论了智能体平台。如今，他带来了一个真实案例：保险业正在验证自主智能体的价值。保险业是地球上最复杂、文档密集且监管严格的行业之一。英国最大的非标准保险提供商之一Acorn Group，在其400人的理赔运营中部署了Simplifai。这不仅仅是聊天机器人，而是作为“指挥家”的AI智能体，编排整个理赔生命周期，将人工分拣减少90%，每月节省数千个运营工时。随着智能体自主性增强，如何建立信任、确保其遵守规则成为关键。文章深入探讨了保险业的“信任层”，以及“了解你的智能体”（KYA）理念的兴起，并展示了AI在现实世界中的实际应用。文中还提供了相关网站、博客、播客和社交媒体链接，以及订阅新闻通讯的提示。
news.bodyHtml:
I’ve been discussing Agentic AI for some time now. It started off more in theory then it got very practical with a recent podcast about Agent platforms. Today we have a real example of Agentic AI in practice in the insurance industry. Artem leads a company that is proving the value of autonomous agents in one of the most complex, document-heavy, and highly regulated industries on earth: Insurance. Acorn Group, one of the UKs largest non-standard insurance providers, has implemented Simplifai, for its 400-person claims operation.

We aren’t just talking about chatbots here. We’re talking about AI agents that act as “conductors,” orchestrating entire claims lifecycles, reducing manual triage by 90%, and saving thousands of operational hours every month. But as these agents gain more autonomy, how do we trust them? How do we ensure they follow the rules? Today, we’re going deep on the “Trust Layer” of insurance, the move toward KYA (Know Your Agent), and what it really looks like to put AI to work in the real world.

For more information, please visit the following:

Website: https://www.josephraczynski.com/

Blog: https://JTConsultingMedia.com/

Podcast: https://techsnippetstoday.buzzsprout.com

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/joerazz/

X: https://x.com/joerazz

news.titleEn: Exclusive: Smokeball and Thomson Reuters Partner to Integrate CoCounsel Legal AI with Practice Management Platform
news.titleZh: 独家：Smokeball与汤森路透合作，将CoCounsel法律AI整合至实践管理平台
news.summaryZh: Smokeball与汤森路透宣布战略合作，将汤森路透的CoCounsel Legal AI嵌入Smokeball的实践管理软件。这一组合将深厚的法律内容与先进AI能力及广泛实践管理功能结合，在小律所市场前所未有。合作采取伙伴关系而非收购，类似去年Clio收购vLex的行业趋势。整合将连接Smokeball实践管理工具与CoCounsel Legal，后者是汤森路透的代理AI解决方案，提供Deep Research法律研究、文件分析和起草功能。合作将法律业务与实践统一，Smokeball提供运营骨干，CoCounsel带来基于Westlaw和Practical Law的AI辅助法律研究、分析和起草。初始整合包括实时数据连接器，允许用户批量推送文件至CoCounsel Legal，并涵盖Westlaw Advantage和Practical Law Dynamic Tool Set。第一阶段目标在晚春或初夏，年内计划更深整合。用户需同时订阅两款产品。Smokeball的Archie AI与CoCounsel互补而非竞争，关键区别是CoCounsel提供权威法律研究。Smokeball CEO Hunter Steele强调运营角度，汤森路透小律所总经理Aaron Rademacher称合作填补市场空白。已有数百Smokeball客户单独订阅CoCounsel，整合将消除系统切换摩擦。合作解决中小律所获取企业级法律研究和AI能力的持续挑战。
news.bodyHtml:
Smokeball, the cloud-based practice management platform serving small to mid-sized law firms, and Thomson Reuters announced a strategic partnership today that will embed Thomson Reuters’ CoCounsel Legal AI into Smokeball’s practice management software — a combination the companies say brings together deep legal content and advanced AI capabilities with broad practice management functionality in a way that has not existed before in the small firm market.

The partnership represents a significant move in the convergence of practice management and legal research — something that the industry first saw last year with Clio’s acquisition of vLex. But rather than acquiring a legal research provider outright, Smokeball has opted for a partnership approach that allows both companies to focus on their core strengths.

Perhaps more importantly, it also represents another example of legal technology providers striving to unite the business and practice of law within a single platform. The integration will connect Smokeball’s practice management tools with CoCounsel Legal, Thomson Reuters’ agentic AI solution that provides legal research through its Deep Research capability, document analysis and drafting functionality.

“No other combination of technology in the small to mid-size law firm market brings together this depth of legal content and AI capability with this breadth of practice management functionality,” Smokeball said in its announcement.

Goal: One Seamless Interface

In an interview with LawSites ahead of the announcement, Smokeball U.S. President Ruchie Chadha said that the partnership is significant for bringing together the business and practice of law into a single, connected experience for small and mid-sized firms.

“Smokeball provides the operational backbone of the firm, from intake through billing, with Archie AI embedded directly into matters to surface insights, draft work, and answer questions based on the firm’s own data (in a secure environment),” she said. “Thomson Reuters, through CoCounsel Legal, brings best-in-class AI-assisted legal research, analysis, and drafting grounded in Westlaw and Practical Law.”

For law firms, the benefit is the ability to leverage AI across both their own matter data and trusted legal research in one place, Chadha said.

“In practice, that means moving seamlessly from managing a matter to researching, analyzing, and producing legal work, without switching between disconnected systems.”

How It Will Work

The initial integration, Chadha told me, will feature a real-time data connector allowing Smokeball users to push documents into CoCounsel Legal in bulk rather than uploading them individually.

“All of our customers will have the opportunity to have AI access all of their key matter details both in Smokeball and utilizing the legal research, analysis and drafting from CoCounsel,” Chadha said. “It really takes the ability to move the workflow through and reason and plan and execute on multi-layer steps of legal tasks.”

The integration with CoCounsel Legal will include Westlaw Advantage and Practical Law Dynamic Tool Set.

Initially, Thomson Reuters will launch a real-time data connector that syncs legal documents across platforms, allowing Smokeball users to push documents into CoCounsel Legal in bulk rather than uploading them one by one. Documents will flow directly from Smokeball into CoCounsel Legal, saving time and reducing the risk of errors or version mismatches.

The first phase of this integration is targeted for late spring or early summer, with deeper integration across additional Thomson Reuters products planned throughout the year.

The ultimate goal is to provide an experience where joint customers can access Thomson Reuters legal content, AI and know-how tools, combined with up-to-date matter facts and information in one seamless interface.

“Over time, our teams are working toward a more deeply integrated experience that combines Smokeball’s practice management capabilities with Thomson Reuters’ commanding legal research, document analysis, and drafting,” Chadha said.

To take advantage of the integration, users will have to be customers of both products.

Complementing, Not Replacing, Archie

Smokeball has been developing its own generative AI capabilities through Archie, its matter assistant that provides document summaries, matter-specific queries, file comparisons and document drafting — all within a ring-fenced security environment where client data is never shared or used to train external models.

Chadha emphasized that the Thomson Reuters partnership complements rather than competes with Archie. The key differentiator is the addition of CoCounsel’s authoritative legal research capabilities.

“The main difference is being able to access that back-end legal research, which is not something that Archie does,” Chadha explained. “This is authoritative legal research which Archie does not have. There is some overlapping capability, but they’re not at odds with each other. I would say it more enhances each other.”

A Partnership Built on Trust

Smokeball says that the partnership reflects its careful approach to selecting technology partners, particularly given the high-stakes nature of the legal work its customers handle.

“We’re always very thoughtful about who we partner with,” Chadha said. “Thomson Reuters has 150, 160 years of trusted data. Our goal is always to make sure that our firms are able to deliver outcomes for their clients. When those stakes are high and the type of law that most of our law firms do, you want to make sure your answers are trusted, the research is good, the data is good. Thomson would probably have been one of very few, if not the only company we would have partnered with on this aspect.”

In a statement announcing the partnership, Hunter Steele, Smokeball’s CEO, emphasized the operational angle: “By partnering with Thomson Reuters, we’re connecting the operational layer of running a practice with trusted legal content, analysis and drafting tools. Our clients will be able to get, do, research and bill their work in one place  —powered by AI that understands both the mechanics of running a firm and the substance of legal work.”

Aaron Rademacher, general manager of small law firms at Thomson Reuters, framed the partnership as filling a market gap: “CoCounsel Legal is an agentic AI solution purpose-built for legal professionals, and we partnered with Smokeball because they provide a premium practice management software that’s already an essential part of the operating stack. Together, we’re creating a solution in the market that combines a premium business-of-law platform with industry-leading practice-of-law content and solutions — a combination that simply hasn’t existed until now.”

Addressing A Persistent Challenge

According to Chadha, there is already substantial overlap between the Smokeball and CoCounsel user bases, with several hundred — possibly more — Smokeball customers already subscribing to CoCounsel separately. The integration, she said, will eliminate the friction of working across disconnected systems for these users.

The announcement comes at an interesting moment in legal technology, as the small law market sees increased competition among platforms seeking to offer comprehensive products.

The Clio-vLex deal last year signaled that practice management vendors were looking to expand their platforms into deeper capabilities for AI and legal research. The Smokeball-Thomson Reuters partnership gets there a differnt way, through a partnership rather than through an acquisition.

For small and mid-sized firms, the partnership addresses a persistent challenge they face, that of accessing enterprise-grade legal research and AI capabilities comparable to those at larger firms, while also maintaining the operational efficiency of a modern practice management platform.

“We’re incredibly excited about what this represents,” Chadha said. “Thomson Reuters’ content has long been the gold standard in the industry and combining that with Smokeball’s platform and Archie creates a much more complete and practical AI experience for our law firms.

“It also aligns closely with what we stand behind at Smokeball: making it easier for attorneys to deliver the best outcomes for their clients, while reducing the burden on themselves and their staff.”

news.titleEn: Thompson Hine Launches SmartPaTH Plus, Integrating AI in Over 100 Workflows
news.titleZh: Thompson Hine推出SmartPaTH Plus，将AI集成到100多个工作流程中
news.summaryZh: Thompson Hine律师事务所将其2013年推出的SmartPaTH平台升级为SmartPaTH Plus，在原有数据和策略基础上集成了生成式人工智能工具，包括AI驱动的研究、起草和分析等功能。该平台将原有内容与AI增强相结合。AI的加入扩展了平台能力，已有超过100个工作流程嵌入了AI组件，而2013年时并无生成式AI可用。SmartPaTH Plus虽被称为平台，但更接近替代性法律服务提供商（ALSP）的技术驱动型法律服务模式。Garcia认为其与ALSP存在相似之处，但强调它并非单一技术或产品，而是一种从规划阶段就注重高效交付的服务方法。平台嵌入的AI工具包括律所专有的预算与工作计划工具、管理事项解决方案，以及许可的供应商工具如文档分析工具Kira和法律AI平台Harvey。在员工持股计划（ESOP）业务中，SmartPaTH Plus整合了五种AI法律技术工具以简化流程：律师首先使用文档自动化工具快速生成相关文件初稿；在尽职调查阶段，使用文档分析工具减少审查交易文件所需时间；律师还可利用底层大语言模型作为谈判规划的演练伙伴，并用于总结和起草；此外，交易管理工具作为电子成交清单，帮助跟踪成交所需事项的进展；最后，律师可使用电子签名促进成交流程。
news.bodyHtml:
Originally launched in 2013 as SmartPaTH, the upgraded platform now integrates a host of generative artificial intelligence tools into its processes.

“What SmartPaTH Plus does is takes all of the things that we built into SmarPaTH, all of the data, all of the experience, all of the strategies that we built into that, and enhances it with AI, with AI-driven research, drafting analytics, etc,” Thompson Hine managing partner Tony White told Legaltech News.

The firm’s chief practice innovation officer Bill Garcia noted that the addition of AI has expanded what SmartPaTH can achieve. “We've got the tools, we've got the structured data, then we've got the benefit of the AI technology, which lets us enhance specific workflows. We have over 100 workflows where we have specifically embedded an AI component into the workflow, and we obviously didn't have that available 2013, at least not the generative AI.”

While SmartPaTH Plus is described as a platform, it is more akin to the tech-enabled legal services approach that is a staple of alternative legal service providers (ALSPs).

“I think there are certainly parallels between what we do and what ALSP do. … SmartPaTH Plus is not a single technology, it's not a single product. It is a way of approaching engagement, to say from the outset, ‘Okay, let's, let's plan this, and let's plan on how we can be most efficient to deliver this service,'” Garcia noted.

The AI tools that SmartPaTH Plus embeds in its workflows include a mix of proprietary ones created by the firm—including a budget and work planning tool and management matter solution—as well as licensed vendor ones such as document analysis tool Kira and legal AI platform Harvey.

For example, Garcia explained, SmartPaTH Plusintegrates together five AI-enabled legal tech tools to streamline workflows in its employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) practice, where lawyers start with a “a document automation tool, which enables them to generate initial drafts of the relevant documents very quickly.

“Then in the next phase—the equivalent of due diligence where there's a lot of review of transactional documents—they use our document analytics tool, which reduces the time necessary to review the relevant documents sufficiently,” he added.

Garcia noted that attorneys also leverage a large language model that underlies the entire process. “You can use the large language model as a sparring partner in planning negotiations. It's obviously useful for summarizing. It's obviously useful for drafting."

In addition, “attorneys can use a transaction management tool, which is effectively an outline on which you can hang all of the documents, and you're able to then track where you are against all of the items that you would expect to need at closing. ... Think of it as a big electronic closing checklist,” he said.

Lastly, at the end of the engagement, attorneys “are able to use electronic signatures to facilitate the closing process,” Garcia noted.

news.titleEn: Legal Industry Reaches AI Tipping Point: Majority of Lawyers Now Using Gen AI Despite Persistent Reliability Concerns
news.titleZh: 法律行业迎来AI临界点：多数律师已使用生成式AI，但可靠性担忧持续存在
news.summaryZh: SurePoint Technologies发布的《2025年法律行业状况报告》显示，2025年法律行业首次出现使用生成式AI的律师人数超过未使用者的现象。63%的中型律所已正式采用生成式AI，最常用的是Microsoft Copilot，但81%的律所领导者对AI的可靠性和风险表示内部担忧。94%的律所领导者预测AI将增加收入并改善客户服务，但许多预期的结构性变化尚未实现。近三分之一预计AI将重塑计费模式，但尚无律所实际做出此类改变。2025年美国法院在法庭文件中记录了487起AI错误或幻觉事件，是2024年总数的10倍以上，其中持证律师占37.8%。报告称“AI治理正变得与AI能力同等重要”。律师使用生成式AI最常见的应用包括法律研究（40%）、起草通信（25%）、总结法律叙述（23%）、审查法律文件（19%）、起草或模板化合同（13%）、审查证据开示（11%）和尽职调查（8%）。拥有五至九年经验的资深律师采用率最高，超过75%。中型律所正从试验转向运营整合，常见实施包括文档创建自动化（70%）、邮件归档（60%）和数据提取（53%），近半数已调整培训计划以应对AI。Am Law 200中具有AI相关经验的律师横向招聘增长68%，该领域助理招聘同比增长106%。
news.bodyHtml:
The legal profession crossed a significant threshold in 2025: For the first time, more lawyers are using generative AI than not, even as firm leaders express widespread concern about the technology’s reliability, according to the 2025 State of the Legal Industry report released today by SurePoint Technologies.

The tension between adoption and apprehension defines the moment we are in. While 63% of mid-sized law firms have formally adopted gen AI – most commonly Microsoft Copilot – 81% of firm leaders report internal concern about its reliability and risk.

And though 94% predict the technology will increase revenue and improve client service, the structural changes many anticipate have yet to materialize. Nearly one-third expect AI to reshape their billing models, but none have actually made such changes.

To underscore the stakes of getting AI implementation wrong, the report cites data from  Damien Charlotin’s database of AI hallucination cases showing U.S. courts recorded 487 instances of AI errors or hallucinations in court documents during 2025, more than 10 times the 2024 total. Licensed attorneys accounted for 37.8% of these problematic filings.

“AI governance is becoming as important as AI capability,” the report states.

How Lawyers Are Using AI

The most common applications for gen AI among lawyers include legal research (40% of users), drafting communications (25%), summarizing legal narratives (23%), reviewing legal documents (19%), drafting or templating contracts (13%), reviewing discovery (11%), and due diligence (8%).

Senior associates with five to nine years of experience showed the highest adoption rates at more than 75%, the report says, citing data from a Bloomberg Law survey.

Mid-sized firms are moving beyond experimentation into operational integration, the report says. Common implementations include automation of document creation (70%), email filing (60%), and data extraction (53%). Nearly half have changed their training programs to address artificial intelligence.

The demand for AI expertise is reflected in hiring patterns. Lateral hiring for attorneys with AI-related experience grew 68% in 2025 within the Am Law 200, with associate hiring in this specialty up 106% year over year.

Record Lateral Movement

The report documents a legal market experiencing significant structural change beyond technology. Law firms made 28,659 lateral hires in 2025, with hiring rising 8.8% in the Am Law 200 and 8.9% outside it – both reaching the highest levels since the post-pandemic surge.

The largest firms continue to consolidate their advantage in recruiting. The Am Law 50 captured nearly 40% of all Am Law 200 lateral hires, up from 35% in 2023. Counsel hiring showed the strongest momentum at 18% year-over-year growth, outpacing associates (11.7%) and partners (10.6%).

Retention remains a challenge that firms pursuing aggressive growth strategies must weigh. After three years, average retention rates in the Am Law 200 stand at 76% for partners, 61% for counsel, and 52% for associates.

“The number of resumes that I review that have very short stops – a year here and two there, and they’re already looking to move,” Lindsey Higgins, firmwide director of legal recruiting at WilmerHale, is quoted as saying in the report.

Government hiring increased notably in 2025, comprising 7% of Am Law 200 lateral hires compared to 4% in 2024 – exceeding even the 5% share seen in 2021 during the previous presidential administration change.

Merger Activity Sets Record

Law firm combinations reached 59 transactions in 2025, a 25% increase from the prior year and the highest level SurePoint has recorded. These deals involved 2,349 lawyers from acquired firms.

The data challenges the perception that consolidation is primarily a big-firm phenomenon. Two-thirds of the transactions originated outside the Am Law 200, and 22 were initiated by firms with fewer than 150 attorneys. Mid-sized firm involvement doubled from 17 transactions in 2021 to 36 in 2025.

Geographic expansion motivated many deals, with 30 of 59 transactions resulting in new office locations. Denver led with seven new offices, followed by Chicago with six and New York and Washington D.C. with five each.

Post-merger retention presents its own challenges. While firms that completed mergers in 2025 showed 92% retention at year-end, historical data from earlier cohorts suggests roughly one-third of acquired lawyers may leave within three years.

Partnership Models Under Pressure

Partner promotions increased 50.4% in 2025, the report finds, producing 3,732 new partners in the Am Law 200 – the largest class on record. The composition of these classes has shifted dramatically: 70.7% of new partners had entered their firms as lateral hires, nearly double the 37.2% share from a decade ago.

The expansion of non-equity partnership tiers is driving some of this growth. According to the report, 87 of the Am Law 100 now have such tiers, with 70 having increased in size since the pandemic.

The SurePoint survey found notable dissatisfaction among non-equity partners. At Am Law 200 firms, 38% said they earned only slightly more than senior associates, and nearly three-quarters reported having no decision-making power or only limited involvement in firm governance. Only 20% reported seeing colleagues successfully move from non-equity to equity status. 

Private Equity Circling

A notable trend is the increasing interest of private equity in law firms. Two U.S. firms – 70-lawyer Cohen & Gresser and 1,750-lawyer McDermott Will & Emery – have publicly acknowledged exploring management services organization (MSO) structures that could accept outside investment while maintaining compliance with rules prohibiting non-lawyer ownership of law practices.

The U.K. market offers a preview of what expanded outside investment might look like. Private equity investors have put the equivalent of $1.6 billion into British law firms over five years, according to Pinsent Masons data cited in the report.

Seven of 10 mid-sized U.K. firms report being contacted by private equity investors or PE-backed firms about acquisition in the past year.

Regulatory changes in Arizona, Utah, and Puerto Rico – the latter preparing to allow up to 49% non-lawyer ownership – may accelerate similar activity in the U.S.

Practice Area Trends

Immigration led secondary practice areas in hiring growth at 88%, reflecting increased regulatory activity, the report says. Government and environmental practices also saw substantial increases at 38% and 34% respectively.

Among primary practices, real estate and banking showed the highest year-over-year growth at 31% and 29%, while litigation continued to account for the largest share of lateral hires at 37%.

Law school recruiting patterns are also shifting. The share of entry-level hires from T-14 law schools dropped from 47% in 2015 to 33.3% in 2025.

Notably, the report found that associates recruited from outside the T-14 show higher long-term retention rates: 53.8% compared to 49% for T-14 graduates.

The 2025 State of the Legal Industry Report is based on data compiled by SurePoint Legal Insights through January 2026.

news.titleEn: The operating system real assets has been missing, now powered by AI
news.titleZh: 真实资产一直缺失的操作系统，如今由AI驱动
news.summaryZh: Intapp在Amplify 2026大会上回顾了其AI进展。Intapp区分了横向AI与Firm AI：横向AI了解互联网，能起草邮件、总结文档、回答问题，但无法将过往投资决策中的上下文（如2023年因租户集中风险而放弃某房地产投资）应用于当前新机会。Intapp Celeste结合现代AI的速度与对your firm运营方式的深度理解，是新型代理平台，不同于个人使用的聊天机器人。代理无需等待提问，能推理、行动，端到端执行复杂多步骤工作流，同时遵守your firm所遵循的访问控制、信息屏障和合规义务。前沿模型提供商并非要成为企业软件公司，而是构建基础能力，并寻找合作伙伴将这些能力交付到受监管行业所需的工作流和治理结构中。对your firm而言，AI优势不在于选择哪个LLM，而在于专有数据、机构知识和工作流的组织程度。对many of you而言，DealCloud已处于交易流程的中心，存储管道、关系跟踪和每笔交易的历史。今年Amplify大会发布了AI嵌入整个系统的DealCloud with Celeste，它不是附加在CRM上的聊天机器人，而是生活在实际工作系统中的AI，可直接访问数据、交易历史和your firm的关系网络。团队可用自然语言与数据交互，例如关系路径发现、临时管道查询、更新交易状态、现场访问后更新等，Celeste能即时返回结果并触发后续工作流。每条交易记录顶部还会显示AI生成的摘要，包括交易状态、最新互动和推荐下一步。此外，Intapp去年收购TermSheet，并在Amplify上将其重新推出为Intapp Properties，作为房地产操作系统。多数真实资产公司仍依赖电子表格，导致数据分散。Intapp Properties专为支持从初次查看到最终出售的完整真实资产工作流而构建。
news.bodyText:
A recap from Intapp Amplify 2026

From answers to action: the rise of Firm AI

The distinction Intapp drew at Amplify between horizontal AI and Firm AI is worth sitting with. Horizontal AI knows the internet. It can draft an email, summarize a document, answer a question. What it can’t do is connect the fact that you passed on a real estate investment in 2023 due to tenant concentration risk and apply that context to new opportunities coming in now.

Intapp Celeste combines the speed of modern AI with a deep understanding of how your firm operates. It’s a new agentic platform different than the chatbots individuals are using. The difference is that agents don’t wait for you to ask. They reason. They act. They execute complex, multi-step workflows end to end while respecting every access control, information barrier, and compliance obligation your firm operates under.

 

Anthropic and Microsoft were both there to reinforce the point that frontier model providers are not trying to become enterprise software companies. They are building primitives and looking for partners who can deliver those capabilities inside the workflows and governance structures that regulated industries need.

The implication for your firm: your AI advantage won’t come from which LLM you choose. It will come from how well your proprietary data, institutional knowledge, and workflows are structured to power those models. If your data is fragmented, your intelligence will be too. And if your systems don’t work together, your teams can’t move as one especially as agentic AI scales.

DealCloud reimagined, powered by AI

For many of you, DealCloud is already at the center of your deal process. Pipeline, relationship tracking, and the history of every deal your firm has ever touched is stored.

This year at Amplify, we unveiled an even more powerful version of DealCloud, with AI embedded throughout. DealCloud with Celeste isn’t a chatbot bolted onto your CRM. It’s AI that lives inside the system where your actual work gets done, with direct access to your data, your deal history, and your firm’s relationship network. The intelligence is already in there, because the data already lives there.

A significant portion of what your teams do every day isn’t judgment work, it’s administrative overhead created by disconnected systems. DealCloud with Celeste eliminates that friction.

With natural language, your team can interact with your data in plain English asking questions, surfacing insights, and acting instantly. For example:

Relationship path discovery

Ad-hoc pipeline queries

Updating deal status

Post-site-visit updates

Relationship path discovery

Ask Celeste: “Who at our firm has the strongest relationship with this ownership group, and when did we last engage?”

Outcome: Celeste instantly surfaces the best connection using relationship scores, interaction history, and network data no manual digging.

Ad-hoc pipeline queries

Ask Celeste: “Show me all Southeast multifamily deals we passed on in the last 18 months and why.”

Outcome: Celeste returns answers instantly, even for questions that don’t exist in pre-built reports.

Updating deal status

Ask Celeste: “Move Riverside Industrial to LOI Submitted.”

Outcome: Celeste updates the stage and automatically triggers next-step workflows like diligence and IC notifications.

Post-site-visit updates

Ask Celeste: “We toured Westlake higher vacancy than expected, concerns on tenant credit. Pass, but keep the broker warm.”

Outcome: Celeste logs the interaction, updates the deal, flags it as passed, and routes materials no manual entry across systems.

In addition to the natural language chat, every deal record now surfaces an AI-generated summary at the top: deal status, latest interactions, recommended next steps.

This is what it looks like when AI is embedded inside your system of work not layered on top of it. The friction disappears. The context is already there. And your team can focus on making decisions, not assembling information.

Where real assets get its purpose-built operating system

Real estate markets and the firms that invest, operate, and service them are transforming. To manage rising complexity, volatility, and risk while driving returns, leading firms are adopting vertically integrated models that unify capital and operations for greater control, efficiency, and scale.

Last year, Intapp acquired TermSheet. At that time, the strategic rationale was clear: as multi-strategy firms expand into real estate and infrastructure, they need tools built for how real assets work, not adapted from platforms designed to track companies and contacts. At Amplify, we re-introduced TermSheet as Intapp Properties as the operating system for real estate.

With Intapp Properties, we are extending our real assets suite to provide the digital backbone for modern real asset firms.

Most real assets firms aren’t running on purpose-built software, they’re running on spreadsheets.

The result is data scattered across systems, inboxes, and documents.

Intapp Properties is purpose-built to support the full real asset workflow, from first look to final sale. It centralizes acquisitions pipeline management and AI-powered underwriting, coordinates development and construction project management across vendors and timelines, connects directly to property accounting systems to automate financial consolidation and reporting, and surfaces portfolio-wide performance intelligence in real time. Because every data point ties back to the physical asset, teams get a single source of truth that moves with them across the entire asset lifecycle.

From first look to final sale, Intapp Properties is built to support the full real asset workflow without the switching between disconnected point solutions.

What this means for your firm, right now

For real asset firms still running on spreadsheets and disconnected point solutions, an AI-powered unified operating system doesn’t just improve how you work, it changes what’s possible.

What Amplify 2026 surfaced is that firms are seeing a real impact from AI are not the ones experimenting carefully at the edges. They’re the ones that made a foundational commitment. Join us for an upcoming webinar on April 15 to see how leading real asset firms are putting this into practice embedding AI into their workflows, connecting their data, and moving from insight to action in real time.

news.titleEn: Why Legal AI Fails Without Context
news.titleZh: 为什么法律AI缺乏上下文就会失败
news.summaryZh:
法律案件的关键信息分散于案件与律所各处，包括文件、邮件、时间线、司法管辖区、客户历史及律所工作成果。法律AI若无法获取全部信息，便如同盲人摸象，其表现仅取决于用户事先告知的内容。缺乏上下文，AI难以发挥全部潜力；仅理解问题而不了解背后案件的系统，生成的答案仍需人工复核、验证与修正，这并未节省时间，只是转移了工作。具备完整案件上下文的AI无需等待简报，它已了解客户历史、案件轨迹及律所过往立场，从而改变其能力边界与产出可信度。

以合同红线审查为例，无上下文AI可能认为赔偿条款语法正确且法律常见，将其标记为可接受；而Clio Work直接集成Clio Manage，能识别出客户是受董事会强制责任上限约束的高风险初创公司，且对方在特拉华州有诉讼历史，该条款实为战略风险，会标记并建议符合律所交易处理方式的修订。法律研究同理，多数工具只返回结果，Clio Work则提供来自经审核法律数据库的带引用权威分析，因理解问题背后的案件，研究结果即刻可用。律师最常感到上下文缺失的两处：一是将正确文件纳入分析，律所文件是其记忆，多数AI无法访问，Clio Work的文档管理集成将现有文档系统拉入研究与分析流程；二是将推理贯穿至最终工作成果，Clio Work的新Legal Pad功能让律师将推理转化为工作成果而不丢失思考过程。
news.bodyHtml:
Context is the foundation of useful legal AI

The most important information in a legal case lives across the matter and the firm: the documents, the emails, the timeline, the jurisdiction, the client’s history, and the firm’s own work product. Legal AI without access to all of it is working blind, only as good as what you remember to tell it before you start.

Without that context, AI can struggle to realize its full potential. A system that only understands the question, not the matter behind it, produces answers you still have to second-guess, verify, and correct. That’s not saving time. That’s moving the work around.

AI that has full matter context doesn’t wait to be briefed. It already knows the client’s history, the matter’s trajectory, and the firm’s prior positions. That changes not just what it can do, but how much you can trust what it produces.

How context-aware AI changes legal work 

Run an AI tool without context through a standard contract redlining task and the problem becomes clear. It might review an indemnification clause, find it grammatically sound and legally common, and flag it as acceptable.

When we built Clio Work with direct integration into Clio Manage, this is one of the scenarios we were designing against. Clio Work sees what a context-free tool misses: Your client is a high-risk startup operating under board-mandated liability caps, and the counterparty has a documented litigation history in Delaware. The clause isn’t routine, it’s a strategic exposure. Clio Work flags it as such and recommends a revision aligned with how your firm handles this deal type. That’s the difference between a research tool and a genuine partner.

The same principle applies to legal research. Most legal research tools return results. The harder problem is returning results that actually mean something given the specific matter, client, and jurisdiction in front of you. Clio Work provides cited, authoritative analysis drawn from a vetted legal database, and because it understands the matter behind the question, that research is actionable from the moment it lands. Without context, you just have results. 

Two places lawyers feel context loss most acutely–and our solutions

We’ve talked to a lot of lawyers. The complaints vary, but two keep showing up almost every time: getting the right documents into the analysis, and carrying the reasoning through to the final work product.

The first is a knowledge problem. A firm’s documents are its memory. Prior agreements, research memos, work product built over years of practice. Most AI tools have no access to any of it. An AI that can’t see those documents has no idea how your firm actually approaches a problem. Document management integrations in Clio Work address this directly, pulling a firm’s existing document systems into the research and analysis workflow. Centralizing knowledge and analysis helps lawyers reach meaningful insights without the back-and-forth.

The second is a translation problem. AI-assisted analysis is only as valuable as what it produces, and in legal work the deliverable is always a document. Clio Work’s new Legal Pad feature gives lawyers a single place to take that reasoning and turn it into work product, without losing the thinking that got them there.

The best legal AI is the one that already knows your matter

For solo practitioners and small firm lawyers, time is the constraint that governs everything. Every minute spent rebuilding context for an AI tool, summarizing matters, re-uploading documents, re-explaining timelines, is a minute not spent with a client or developing strategy.

Context-aware AI built directly into a practice management system eliminates that tax. The context is already there, embedded in the system that runs your practice. That’s the architectural difference between AI that assists legal work and AI that integrates with it, and it’s the difference we built Clio’s Intelligent Work Platform to make.

For lawyers serious about making AI work in practice, that’s the problem worth solving first.

We’ve talked to a lot of lawyers. The complaints vary, but two keep showing up almost every time: getting the right documents into the analysis, and carrying the reasoning through to the final work product.

The first is a knowledge problem. A firm’s documents are its memory. Prior agreements, research memos, work product built over years of practice. Most AI tools have no access to any of it. An AI that can’t see those documents has no idea how your firm actually approaches a problem. Document management integrations in Clio Work address this directly, pulling a firm’s existing document systems into the research and analysis workflow. Centralizing knowledge and analysis helps lawyers reach meaningful insights without the back-and-forth.

The second is a translation problem. AI-assisted analysis is only as valuable as what it produces, and in legal work the deliverable is always a document. Clio Work’s new Legal Pad feature gives lawyers a single place to take that reasoning and turn it into work product, without losing the thinking that got them there.

The best legal AI is the one that already knows your matter

For solo practitioners and small firm lawyers, time is the constraint that governs everything. Every minute spent rebuilding context for an AI tool, summarizing matters, re-uploading documents, re-explaining timelines, is a minute not spent with a client or developing strategy. Context-aware AI built directly into a practice management system eliminates that tax. The context is already there, embedded in the system that runs your practice. That’s the architectural difference between AI that assists legal work and AI that integrates with it, and it’s the difference we built Clio’s Intelligent Work Platform to make.

For lawyers serious about making AI work in practice, that’s the problem worth solving first.

research.titleEn: When AI output tips to bad but nobody notices: Legal implications of AI's mistakes
research.titleZh: 当AI输出错误但无人察觉时：AI失误的法律影响
research.abstractEn: The adoption of generative AI across commercial and legal professions offers dramatic efficiency gains -- yet for law in particular, it introduces a perilous failure mode in which the AI fabricates fictitious case law, statutes, and judicial holdings that appear entirely authentic. Attorneys who unknowingly file such fabrications face professional sanctions, malpractice exposure, and reputational harm, while courts confront a novel threat to the integrity of the adversarial process. This failure mode is commonly dismissed as random `hallucination', but recent physics-based analysis of the Transformer's core mechanism reveals a deterministic component: the AI's internal state can cross a calculable threshold, causing its output to flip from reliable legal reasoning to authoritative-sounding fabrication. Here we present this science in a legal-industry setting, walking through a simulated brief-drafting scenario. Our analysis suggests that fabrication risk is not an anomalous glitch but a foreseeable consequence of the technology's design, with direct implications for the evolving duty of technological competence. We propose that legal professionals, courts, and regulators replace the outdated `black box' mental model with verification protocols based on how these systems actually fail.
research.abstractZh: 生成式AI在商业和法律行业的应用带来了显著的效率提升——然而对法律领域而言，它引入了一种危险的失效模式：AI会编造完全看似真实的虚构判例法、法规和司法判决。律师若在不知情的情况下提交此类虚构内容，将面临职业处分、渎职风险及声誉损害，而法院则面临着对抗程序完整性的新型威胁。这种失效模式常被轻视为随机‘幻觉’，但近期基于物理学的Transformer核心机制分析揭示了其确定性成分：AI的内部状态可能跨越可计算的阈值，导致其输出从可靠的法律推理转变为听似权威的虚构内容。本文在法律行业背景下呈现这一科学原理，通过模拟案情摘要起草场景进行阐述。我们的分析表明，虚构风险并非异常故障，而是该技术设计可预见的后果，对技术能力义务的演变具有直接影响。我们建议法律从业者、法院和监管机构用基于这些系统实际失效方式的验证协议，取代过时的‘黑箱’思维模型。

research.titleEn: Bridging the Interpretation Gap in Accessibility Testing: Empathetic and Legal-Aware Bug Report Generation via Large Language Models
research.titleZh: 弥合无障碍测试中的解读鸿沟：基于大语言模型的共情与法律意识缺陷报告生成
research.abstractEn: Modern automated accessibility testing tools for mobile applications have significantly improved the detection of interface violations, yet their impact on remediation remains limited. A key reason is that existing tools typically produce low-level, technical outputs that are difficult for non-specialist stakeholders, such as product managers and designers, to interpret in terms of real user harm and compliance risk. In this paper, we present \textsc{HEAR} (\underline{H}uman-c\underline{E}ntered \underline{A}ccessibility \underline{R}eporting), a framework that bridges this interpretation gap by transforming raw accessibility bug reports into empathetic, stakeholder-oriented narratives. Given the outputs of the existing accessibility testing tool, \textsc{HEAR} first reconstructs the UI context through semantic slicing and visual grounding, then dynamically injects disability-oriented personas matched to each violation type, and finally performs multi-layer reasoning to explain the physical barrier, functional blockage, and relevant legal or compliance concerns. We evaluate the framework on real-world accessibility issues collected from four popular Android applications and conduct a user study (N=12). The results show that \textsc{HEAR} generates factually grounded reports and substantially improves perceived empathy, urgency, persuasiveness, and awareness of legal risk compared with raw technical logs, while imposing little additional cognitive burden.
research.abstractZh: 现代移动应用自动化无障碍测试工具在界面违规检测方面已取得显著进步，但其对问题修复的实际影响仍有限。关键原因在于现有工具通常生成低层次的技术性输出，非专业利益相关者（如产品经理和设计师）难以从真实用户伤害和合规风险角度进行解读。本文提出\textsc{HEAR}（\underline{H}uman-c\underline{E}ntered \underline{A}ccessibility \underline{R}eporting）框架，通过将原始无障碍缺陷报告转化为共情化、面向利益相关者的叙述，弥合这一解读鸿沟。基于现有无障碍测试工具的输出，\textsc{HEAR}首先通过语义切片和视觉定位重建用户界面上下文，随后动态注入与各类违规类型匹配的残障导向人物角色，最终执行多层推理以解释物理障碍、功能阻断及相关法律或合规问题。我们在从四款流行安卓应用收集的真实无障碍问题上评估该框架，并开展用户研究（N=12）。结果表明，与原始技术日志相比，\textsc{HEAR}生成的事实依据充分的报告显著提升了感知共情度、紧迫性、说服力及法律风险意识，同时几乎未增加额外认知负担。

news.titleEn: DeepJudge launches SuperSearch
news.titleZh: DeepJudge推出SuperSearch
news.summaryZh: DeepJudge正式宣布推出SuperSearch，称其为下一代搜索体验。该平台基于意图搜索技术，能够从律所数据中提供更细粒度、可操作的洞察，实现跨事项智能。SuperSearch帮助律师发现、呈现并分析模式和见解，以增强风险评估、战略制定和客户成果。平台理解内容、相关性与机构知识之间的复杂关系，通过建立统一智能层，使法律团队能够基于自身历史工作构建、部署和扩展专有AI生态系统。SuperSearch能结构化、验证并即时交付可操作结果，无需手动审查、标记或设置，可回答直接影响交易结果和客户建议的复杂跨事项问题。AI优势来自先进AI与完整上下文、智能编排及精准信息访问的结合，高质量检索至关重要。经过独家早期访问计划，多家领先律所已在并购、诉讼和监管实践中使用SuperSearch，用于发现制胜交易结构、案例策略并验证监管建议一致性。有合伙人要求构建挖掘本地法律顾问意见的生成式AI工具，他展示了SuperSearch，对方称其完全满足需求。
news.bodyHtml:
DeepJudge, the core AI platform that leading law firms use to access and apply their institutional knowledge at scale, today formally announced the launch of SuperSearch, which they describe as a next-generation search experience. Already known for search, DeepJudge says that SuperSearch, which it has teased since Legalweek in New York, will provide even more granular and actionable insights from a firm’s data, enabling unprecedented cross-matter intelligence.

Built on DeepJudge’s intent-based search technology, SuperSearch enables lawyers to find, surface, and analyze patterns and insights that enhance risk assessment, strategy, and client outcomes. The platform understands the complex relationships between content, relevance, and institutional knowledge across a firm’s internal systems. By establishing a unified intelligence layer, DeepJudge enables legal teams to ground their judgment in their own unique historical work. This allows legal teams to build, deploy, and scale their own proprietary AI ecosystems that are accurate, secure, and uniquely their own.

Advertisement

“We’ve fundamentally rethought what search should do,” said Yannic Kilcher, CTO and co-founder of DeepJudge. “SuperSearch structures, validates, and delivers results that you can act on right away. You can refine your path to an answer instantly, focusing on what matters most in the moment, with no manual review, tagging, or setup required. SuperSearch makes it possible to ask and answer complex, cross-matter questions that directly impact deal outcomes, client advice, and the firm’s ability to win and execute high-stakes work.”

Fellow co-founder and CEO Paulina Grnarova added: “AI models are evolving at unprecedented speed. The real advantage comes not from any single model, but from combining advanced AI with complete context, smart orchestration, and precise access to the right information. In law firms, AI delivers value only when it sees the full picture, which is spread across systems, matters, and years of work. Without high-quality retrieval, even the most sophisticated AI is limited.”

Following an exclusive early access program, several leading law firms are already using SuperSearch across practices including M&A, litigation, and regulatory—finding winning deal structures from past transactions, uncovering case-winning strategies, and validating regulatory advice consistency across years of client work.

“Last week a partner asked me to build a generative AI tool that would mine years of local counsel opinions. I showed them DeepJudge SuperSearch. They told me it did exactly what they wanted,” said Douglas Schulz, innovation manager at ArentFox Schiff.
